<file path="src/components/ui/StarRatingInput.tsx">
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// ⭐ StarRatingInput — Star rating selector
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

type StarRatingInputProps = {
  value: number;
  onChange: (rating: number) => void;
  size?: number;
};

// ─── Single star (SVG) ───
function Star({ size, filled }: { size: number; filled: boolean }) {
  return (
    <svg
      width={size}
      height={size}
      viewBox="0 0 24 24"
      fill={filled ? "currentColor" : "none"}
      stroke="currentColor"
      strokeWidth={filled ? 0 : 1.5}
      className={filled ? "text-accent" : "text-border"}
      aria-hidden="true"
    >
      <path d="M12 2l3.09 6.26L22 9.27l-5 4.87 1.18 6.88L12 17.77l-6.18 3.25L7 14.14 2 9.27l6.91-1.01L12 2z" />
    </svg>
  );
}

export function StarRatingInput({
  value,
  onChange,
  size = 32,
}: StarRatingInputProps) {
  const t = useTranslations("Review.form");
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState<number>(0);

  // Display hovered value if hovering, otherwise the current value
  const displayValue = hovered || value;

  return (
    <div
      className="inline-flex items-center gap-2"
      onMouseLeave={() => setHovered(0)}
      role="radiogroup"
      aria-label={t("ratingLabel")}
    >
      {[1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((star) => (
        <button
          key={star}
          type="button"
          onMouseEnter={() => setHovered(star)}
          onClick={() => onChange(star)}
          aria-label={`${star} / 5`}
          aria-checked={value === star}
          role="radio"
          className="transition-transform hover:scale-110 focus:outline-none focus:scale-110"
        >
          <Star size={size} filled={star <= displayValue} />
        </button>
      ))}

      {value > 0 && (
        <span className="text-sm text-muted mr-2">
          {t("ratingOutOf", { value })}
        </span>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

<file path="src/lib/services/analytics.ts">
import { prisma } from "@/lib/prisma";

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 📊 Analytics Service — تجميع البيانات للرسوم البيانية
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

// ─── 1. Category distribution ───
export async function getCategoryDistribution() {
  const categories = await prisma.category.findMany({
    orderBy: { displayOrder: "asc" },
    select: {
      name: true,
      nameEn: true,
      _count: { select: { items: true } },
    },
  });

  return categories.map((cat) => ({
    name: cat.name,
    nameEn: cat.nameEn,
    value: cat._count.items,
  }));
}

// ─── 2. توزيع الأسعار (نطاقات) ───
export async function getPriceDistribution() {
  const items = await prisma.menuItem.findMany({
    where: { isAvailable: true },
    select: { price: true },
  });

  const buckets = [
    { name: "٠ - ٥٠", min: 0, max: 50, value: 0 },
    { name: "٥١ - ١٠٠", min: 51, max: 100, value: 0 },
    { name: "١٠١ - ١٥٠", min: 101, max: 150, value: 0 },
    { name: "١٥١ - ٢٠٠", min: 151, max: 200, value: 0 },
    { name: "٢٠٠+", min: 201, max: Infinity, value: 0 },
  ];

  for (const item of items) {
    const bucket = buckets.find(
      (b) => item.price >= b.min && item.price <= b.max
    );
    if (bucket) bucket.value += 1;
  }

  return buckets.map(({ name, value }) => ({ name, value }));
}

// ─── 3. Featured vs regular ───
export async function getFeaturedDistribution() {
  const [featured, regular] = await Promise.all([
    prisma.menuItem.count({ where: { isFeatured: true, isAvailable: true } }),
    prisma.menuItem.count({ where: { isFeatured: false, isAvailable: true } }),
  ]);

  // Return raw keys; translation happens in the component
  return [
    { name: "featured", value: featured },
    { name: "regular", value: regular },
  ];
}

import { z } from "zod";

type TranslateFn = (key: string) => string;

export function createCategorySchema(t: TranslateFn) {
  return z.object({
    name: z
      .string()
      .trim()
      .min(2, t("categoryNameTooShort"))
      .max(50, t("categoryNameTooLong")),

    nameEn: z
      .string()
      .trim()
      .max(50, t("categoryNameTooLong"))
      .optional()
      .or(z.literal("")),

    slug: z
      .string()
      .trim()
      .toLowerCase()
      .min(2, t("slugTooShort"))
      .max(50, t("slugTooLong"))
      .regex(/^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/, t("slugInvalidFormat")),

    description: z
      .string()
      .trim()
      .max(200, t("descriptionTooLong"))
      .optional()
      .or(z.literal("")),

    displayOrder: z.coerce
      .number()
      .int(t("displayOrderNotInt"))
      .min(0, t("displayOrderNegative"))
      .max(999, t("displayOrderTooLarge")),
  });
}

export type CategoryInput = z.infer<ReturnType<typeof createCategorySchema>>;

<file path="src/lib/validations/reservation.ts">
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 📅 Reservation validation schema (i18n-ready)
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// The schema is created via a factory that accepts a
// translation function `t`. This allows Server Actions
// to pass locale-specific translations at runtime.

import { z } from "zod";
import { DEFAULT_DURATION_MINUTES } from "@/lib/services/table-assignment";

// Translate function signature (subset of next-intl's t)
type TranslateFn = (key: string) => string;

// ─── Factory: create schema with translated messages ───
export function createReservationSchema(t: TranslateFn) {
  return z
    .object({
      guestName: z
        .string()
        .trim()
        .min(2, t("guestNameTooShort"))
        .max(80, t("guestNameTooLong")),

      guestEmail: z
        .string()
        .trim()
        .toLowerCase()
        .email(t("guestEmailInvalid")),

      guestPhone: z
        .string()
        .trim()
        .min(8, t("guestPhoneTooShort"))
        .max(20, t("guestPhoneTooLong"))
        .regex(/^[+\d\s\-()]+$/, t("guestPhoneInvalidChars")),

      guestsCount: z.coerce
        .number()
        .int(t("guestsCountNotInt"))
        .min(1, t("guestsCountMin"))
        .max(10, t("guestsCountMax")),

      date: z.string().regex(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/, t("dateFormatInvalid")),

      time: z.string().regex(/^\d{2}:\d{2}$/, t("timeFormatInvalid")),

      notes: z
        .string()
        .trim()
        .max(500, t("notesTooLong"))
        .optional()
        .or(z.literal("")),
    })
    .refine(
      (data) => {
        const dt = new Date(`${data.date}T${data.time}:00`);
        return dt.getTime() > Date.now();
      },
      { message: t("dateInPast"), path: ["date"] }
    )
    .refine(
      (data) => {
        const dt = new Date(`${data.date}T${data.time}:00`);
        const hours = dt.getHours();
        return hours >= 12 && hours <= 22;
      },
      { message: t("outsideBusinessHours"), path: ["time"] }
    );
}

// ─── Inferred types (same across all locales) ───
export type ReservationInput = z.infer<
  ReturnType<typeof createReservationSchema>
>;

export type ReservationRequest = ReservationInput & {
  durationMinutes: number;
};

// ─── Helpers ───
export function toReservationRequest(
  input: ReservationInput
): ReservationRequest {
  return { ...input, durationMinutes: DEFAULT_DURATION_MINUTES };
}

export function parseReservationDate(date: string, time: string): Date {
  return new Date(`${date}T${time}:00`);
}

      .string()
      .min(MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH, t("passwordTooShort"))
      .max(100, t("passwordTooLong"))
      .optional()
      .or(z.literal("")),

📌 SAVED TECHNICAL LESSONS (DO NOT REPEAT)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. After adding new locale file:
   Ctrl+C → Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .next → npm run dev

2. npx tsc --noEmit = FINAL verdict
   VS Code Problems = fast helper (may be wrong)

3. Restart TS Server after any prisma migrate:
   Ctrl+Shift+P → TypeScript: Restart TS Server

4. MISSING_MESSAGE from next-intl:
   Add key in all 5 files → clear .next → restart

5. HTML5 native validation is English-only:
   Add noValidate on <form> to show Zod messages

6. Prisma + Vercel:
   - prisma-client-js (not prisma-client)
   - binaryTargets: ["native", "rhel-openssl-3.0.x"]
   - --webpack in dev + build
   - DATABASE_URL without -pooler

7. Server Actions + i18n:
   - getTranslations("Errors") inside action
   - Schema Factory pattern: createXxxSchema(t)

8. set-state-in-effect ESLint Rule:
   - No useEffect with sync setState
   - Use useState(() => initialValue) for init-only

9. Metadata in layout:
   - Use generateMetadata() for translations
   - export const metadata = static, cannot be translated

10. Image Picker Auto-Generated Pattern:
    - scripts/generate-local-images.ts reads public/images/
    - Runs via predev + prebuild hooks
    - Reason: Vercel can't read public/ at request time

      <div class="kicker">Phase 08 · Admin Dashboard</div>
      <h1>Complete CRUD, Role-Based Access &amp; Security Boundaries</h1>
      <p class="lede">Build a full-featured admin dashboard with CRUD operations for five entities (Reservations, Menu, Categories, Tables, Users), server-side business-rule enforcement, role-based access control, and reusable UI primitives. Every operation is guarded by defense-in-depth layers — from Edge middleware to per-action authorization.</p>
      <div class="stack">
        <span>Route Groups</span><span>Server Actions</span><span>revalidatePath</span>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal:</strong> Turn the authentication foundation from Phase 7 into a productive admin workspace where staff can manage the entire restaurant without touching code or the database directly.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li><strong>Route Groups</strong> — separate <code>(public)</code>, <code>(auth)</code>, and <code>admin/</code> layouts.</li>
        <li><strong>Dashboard Overview</strong> — 4 stat cards with real-time counts, powered by <code>Promise.all</code>.</li>
        <li><strong>Reservations management</strong> — status transitions (confirm / cancel / complete / delete).</li>
        <li><strong>Menu management</strong> — toggle availability, toggle featured, delete, plus add/edit forms.</li>
        <li><strong>Categories management</strong> — CRUD with cascade protection.</li>
        <li><strong>Tables management</strong> — CRUD with reservation-history protection.</li>
        <li><strong>Users management</strong> — staff CRUD with three safety rules.</li>
        <li><strong>AdminSidebar</strong> — active link highlighting + logout button + role-based link visibility.</li>
        <li><strong>Reusable UI primitives</strong> — <code>EmptyState</code>, <code>LoadingSpinner</code>, <code>ErrorFallback</code>.</li>
        <li><strong>Loading &amp; Error boundaries</strong> — per route group.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="route-groups">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Route Groups — Architectural Decision</h2>
      <p><strong>The problem:</strong> The global <code>layout.tsx</code> from Phase 4 wrapped <em>every</em> page — including <code>/admin</code> — with the customer-facing <code>Navbar</code> and floating <code>WhatsAppButton</code>. The admin workspace deserves its own shell.</p>

      <h3>The three groups</h3>
      <div class="layers">
        <div class="layer client"><strong>(public)/</strong> · Navbar + WhatsAppButton · pages: <code>/</code>, <code>/menu</code>, <code>/reserve</code></div>
        <div class="layer edge"><strong>(auth)/</strong> · Centered minimal layout · page: <code>/login</code></div>
        <div class="layer db"><strong>admin/</strong> · AdminSidebar + protected · pages: <code>/admin/*</code></div>
      </div>

      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Key insight</strong>
        Parentheses <code>()</code> are ignored by the router — <code>src/app/(public)/menu/page.tsx</code> still serves <code>/menu</code>. They exist purely to group <em>layout inheritance</em>, not URLs.
      </div>

      <h3>Files moved</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Before</th><th>After</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>src/app/page.tsx</code></td><td><code>src/app/(public)/page.tsx</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>src/app/menu/**</code></td><td><code>src/app/(public)/menu/**</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>src/app/reserve/page.tsx</code></td><td><code>src/app/(public)/reserve/page.tsx</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>src/app/login/page.tsx</code></td><td><code>src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

      <h3>Query optimization — Promise.all</h3>
      <pre><code>const [
  todayCount,       // prisma.reservation.count
  pendingCount,     // prisma.reservation.count
  itemsCount,       // prisma.menuItem.count
  activeTables,     // prisma.table.count
  totalTables,      // prisma.table.count
  recentReservations, // prisma.reservation.findMany (take: 5)
] = await Promise.all([...])</code></pre>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Performance rationale</strong>
        Six independent queries run in parallel → total latency ≈ slowest query instead of sum of all six. Typical improvement: 500ms instead of 3s.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="statcard">
      <h2><span class="num">5</span> StatCard — Reusable Component</h2>
      <pre><code>type StatCardProps = {
  icon: string;
  label: string;
  value: string | number;
  hint?: string;
  href?: string;
  accent?: boolean;
};</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Polymorphic choice:</strong> when <code>href</code> is provided, the card renders as a <code>&lt;Link&gt;</code> — turning numbers into clickable filters.</p>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Engineering lesson</strong>
        A first attempt used <code>const Wrapper = href ? Link : "div"</code> with <code>{...props as any}</code>. ESLint's <code>no-explicit-any</code> rule rejected it. The cleaner solution: two explicit <code>if</code> branches — a <code>Link</code> when interactive, a <code>div</code> otherwise.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="server-actions">
      <h2><span class="num">6</span> Server Actions Pattern — Across All 5 Entities</h2>
      <p>Every CRUD operation follows an identical structure:</p>
      <pre><code>"use server";

// 1. Authorization guard
async function requireAdmin() {
  const session = await auth();
  if (!session?.user) return null;
  if (session.user.role !== "ADMIN" &amp;&amp; session.user.role !== "STAFF") return null;
  return session.user;
}

// 2. The action
export async function someAction(input: unknown) {
  const user = await requireAdmin();
  if (!user) return { success: false, error: "غير مصرح" };

  // 3. Zod validation
  const parsed = schema.safeParse(input);
  if (!parsed.success) return { success: false, error: "تحقق من البيانات", fieldErrors };

  try {
    // 4. Prisma mutation
    await prisma.model.create / update / delete(...);

    // 5. Cache invalidation
    revalidatePath("/admin/...");
    revalidatePath("/menu");
    revalidatePath("/");
    return { success: true, id };
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[someAction]", error);
    return { success: false, error: "فشل الإجراء" };
  }
}</code></pre>

      <h3>Why revalidatePath?</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Path</th><th>Invalidated when</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>/admin/&lt;section&gt;</code></td><td>Always — refresh the admin list</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/admin</code></td><td>When counters change</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/menu</code></td><td>When items / categories change</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/</code></td><td>When featured items change</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Zero manual refetch</strong>
        After a Server Action completes, Next.js purges the cached HTML for the listed paths. The next browser request re-runs the Server Components with fresh data — no <code>router.refresh()</code> required for the affected paths.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="reservations">
      <h2><span class="num">7</span> Reservations Management</h2>
      <p><strong>Status lifecycle:</strong> <code>PENDING</code> → <code>CONFIRMED</code> → <code>COMPLETED</code> (or <code>CANCELLED</code> at any step).</p>

      <h3>Available actions per status</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Current status</th><th>Actions shown</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>PENDING</code></td><td>✓ تأكيد · ✗ إلغاء</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>CONFIRMED</code></td><td>✓ إكمال · ✗ إلغاء</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>CANCELLED</code></td><td>🗑 حذف (Admin only)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>COMPLETED</code></td><td>🗑 حذف (Admin only)</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>useTransition for loading state</h3>
      <pre><code>const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();

function handleStatus(status) {
  startTransition(async () => {
    const result = await updateReservationStatus(reservation.id, status);
    if (!result.success) setError(result.error);
  });
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why not useState for loading:</strong> <code>useTransition</code> tracks the entire async Server Action — including its network round-trip. Simpler and more accurate.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="menu-crud">
      <h2><span class="num">8</span> Menu Management — Toggles &amp; Delete</h2>
      <p><strong>Three actions per item</strong>, plus visual badges for state:</p>

      <div class="file-grid">
        <div class="file-card">
          <div class="file-title">⊘ إخفاء / ✓ إظهار</div>
          <p class="file-desc">Toggle <code>isAvailable</code> → item disappears from public menu immediately.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="file-card">
          <div class="file-title">⭐ تمييز / ☆ إلغاء</div>
          <p class="file-desc">Toggle <code>isFeatured</code> → item appears on the homepage featured section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="file-card">
          <div class="file-title">🗑 حذف (Admin)</div>
          <p class="file-desc">Permanent deletion — restricted to <code>ADMIN</code> role only.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <h3>Dual filtering</h3>
      <p>Two independent filter bars — by category and by availability. Both preserved in URL:</p>
      <pre><code>/admin/menu?category=desserts&amp;availability=available

function buildURL(params) {
  const qs = new URLSearchParams();
  if (params.category) qs.set("category", params.category);
  if (params.availability) qs.set("availability", params.availability);
  return `/admin/menu${qs.toString() ? `?${qs}` : ""}`;
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why buildURL:</strong> Each filter link preserves the other filter's value — clicking "متاح" while filtered by "حلويات" keeps the category filter intact.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="menu-form">
      <h2><span class="num">9</span> Menu Item Form — Shared Between Add &amp; Edit</h2>
      <p>One component serves both routes: <code>/admin/menu/new</code> and <code>/admin/menu/[id]/edit</code>.</p>

      <pre><code>const isEdit = !!initialData?.id;

const result = isEdit
  ? await updateMenuItem(initialData.id, payload)
  : await createMenuItem(payload);</code></pre>

      <h3>Auto-slugify from English name</h3>
      <pre><code>function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .trim()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9\s-]/g, "")
    .replace(/\s+/g, "-")
    .replace(/-+/g, "-");
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Behavior:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li><strong>In "new" mode:</strong> slug regenerates with every keystroke in the name field.</li>
        <li><strong>In "edit" mode:</strong> slug stays frozen — protects existing URLs from silent changes.</li>
        <li><strong>Arabic names:</strong> slugify strips all Arabic characters → admin enters slug manually (common pattern).</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>Duplicate slug detection</h3>
      <pre><code>const duplicate = await prisma.menuItem.findFirst({
  where: { slug: data.slug, NOT: { id: itemId } },
});
// NOT clause prevents matching the item against itself in edit mode</code></pre>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Tested and verified</strong>
        Attempted to create a new item with slug <code>hummus</code> → rejected with "هذا المعرّف مستخدم بالفعل" shown under the slug field.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="categories-crud">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> Categories Management</h2>
      <p>Standard CRUD with two additional features over the menu:</p>
      <ul>
        <li><strong><code>displayOrder</code></strong> — numeric field controls sort order in filters and menu.</li>
        <li><strong><code>_count</code> on read</strong> — each category displays its item count without a second query.</li>
      </ul>

      <pre><code>const categories = await prisma.category.findMany({
  orderBy: { displayOrder: "asc" },
  include: {
    _count: { select: { items: true } },
  },
});</code></pre>

      <p><strong>Duplicate detection runs on both <code>slug</code> and <code>name</code>:</strong></p>
      <pre><code>const duplicate = await prisma.category.findFirst({
  where: { OR: [{ slug }, { name }] },
});
const key = duplicate.slug === data.slug ? "slug" : "name";
// Report the specific conflicting field</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="cascade">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> Cascade Protection — Category Deletion</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>The hidden trap</strong>
        In Phase 2 we set <code>onDelete: Cascade</code> on <code>MenuItem.category</code>. Deleting a category therefore deletes all its items <em>silently</em>. This is correct for referential integrity but devastating in production if a user clicks "Delete" casually.
      </div>

      <h3>The guard</h3>
      <pre><code>const itemsCount = await prisma.menuItem.count({ where: { categoryId: id } });
if (itemsCount &gt; 0) {
  return {
    success: false,
    error: `لا يمكن حذف التصنيف — يحتوي على ${itemsCount} طبق. انقل الأطباق لتصنيف آخر أولاً.`,
  };
}</code></pre>

      <p><strong>Verification from dev.log:</strong></p>
      <pre><code>deleteCategory("...")  in 25ms    ← protection rejected instantly (fail-fast)
deleteCategory("...")  in 629ms   ← empty category actually deleted</code></pre>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Fail-fast principle</strong>
        The 25ms response proves the guard runs <em>before</em> any database write — no wasted work, no risk of a partial delete.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="tables-crud">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> Tables Management</h2>
      <p>Same CRUD pattern with one critical safety rule: <strong>tables with reservation history cannot be deleted</strong>.</p>

      <h3>Fields</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>number</code> — unique integer (1, 2, 3...)</li>
        <li><code>capacity</code> — number of seats</li>
        <li><code>location</code> — enum-like string (<code>Indoor</code>, <code>Window</code>, <code>Outdoor</code>, <code>VIP</code>)</li>
        <li><code>isActive</code> — enable/disable without deletion</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>Toggle instead of delete</h3>
      <p>Disabled tables stop being considered by the Phase 5 booking engine but remain in the database for historical queries. The <code>isActive</code> flag is the primary lifecycle tool.</p>

      <h3>Reservation count badge</h3>
      <pre><code>include: { _count: { select: { reservations: true } } }
// Row shows "1 حجز" badge if the table has any history</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="table-protect">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> Reservation-History Protection</h2>
      <pre><code>const reservationsCount = await prisma.reservation.count({ where: { tableId: id } });
if (reservationsCount &gt; 0) {
  return {
    success: false,
    error: `لا يمكن حذف الطاولة — لها ${reservationsCount} حجز تاريخي. عطّلها بدلاً من ذلك.`,
  };
}</code></pre>

      <h3>Why stricter than categories?</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Entity</th><th>Deletion allowed when</th><th>Reason</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><strong>Category</strong></td><td>Zero <em>current</em> items</td><td>Items can be reassigned</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Table</strong></td><td>Zero <em>historical</em> reservations</td><td>Reservations are financial records</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Business reality</strong>
        A deleted category leaves items easy to reassign. A deleted table orphans financial records — potentially a tax/legal problem. Stricter for a reason.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="users-crud">
      <h2><span class="num">14</span> Users Management — Admin Only</h2>
      <p>Only users with <code>role === "ADMIN"</code> can access <code>/admin/users</code>. All other roles are redirected to <code>/admin</code>.</p>

      <h3>Fields</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>email</code> — unique, set at creation, <strong>immutable</strong> afterward</li>
        <li><code>name</code> — display name</li>
        <li><code>role</code> — <code>ADMIN</code> or <code>STAFF</code></li>
        <li><code>isActive</code> — soft-disable without deleting</li>
        <li><code>password</code> / <code>newPassword</code> — creation requires it, edit makes it optional</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>Why email is immutable</h3>
      <p>The email is the login identifier. Changing it would invalidate the target user's active session without warning. A safe policy: keep it fixed, create a new user if the email must change.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="user-protect">
      <h2><span class="num">15</span> Three Safety Layers in User Management</h2>
      <div class="sec-layers">
        <div class="sec-row">
          <div class="sec-check">1</div>
          <div class="sec-body">
            <code>if (id === admin.id &amp;&amp; data.role !== "ADMIN") return error;</code>
            <div class="why">You cannot remove your own admin role.</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="sec-row">
          <div class="sec-check">2</div>
          <div class="sec-body">
            <code>if (id === admin.id &amp;&amp; !data.isActive) return error;</code>
            <div class="why">You cannot disable your own account.</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="sec-row">
          <div class="sec-check">3</div>
          <div class="sec-body">
            <code>const otherActiveAdmins = await prisma.user.count({ where: { role: "ADMIN", isActive: true, NOT: { id } } });</code>
            <div class="why">You cannot remove the last active admin — locks the entire system out.</div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Combined effect</strong>
        These three rules make it impossible to accidentally lock the system out of admin access, no matter what combination of role changes or deletions is attempted.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="active-link">
      <h2><span class="num">17</span> Active Link &amp; Logout — UX Essentials</h2>

      <h3>Active link highlighting</h3>
      <pre><code>const pathname = usePathname();

function isActive(href: string, exact?: boolean) {
  if (exact) return pathname === href;
  return pathname === href || pathname.startsWith(href + "/");
}</code></pre>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Path visited</th><th>Link highlighted</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>/admin</code></td><td>نظرة عامة (exact)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/admin/menu</code></td><td>الأطباق</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/admin/menu/new</code></td><td>الأطباق (prefix match)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/admin/menu/xyz/edit</code></td><td>الأطباق</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Why <code>exact</code> for /admin</strong>
        Without <code>exact</code>, <code>/admin</code> would match every admin URL because everything starts with <code>/admin/</code>. The exact flag ensures "نظرة عامة" only lights up on the dashboard itself.
      </div>

      <h3>Logout button — the missing feature</h3>
      <pre><code>function handleLogout() {
  if (!confirm("تسجيل الخروج من لوحة التحكم؟")) return;
  startTransition(async () => {
    await signOut({ callbackUrl: "/login" });
  });
}</code></pre>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Real bug caught in testing</strong>
        During Phase 8 verification, a user could not log out from the admin UI — the button didn't exist. This was corrected by adding the logout button, which now lives prominently in the sidebar footer.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="loading-error">

      <p>Next.js recognizes two special file names per route segment:</p>

          <tr><td><code>error.tsx</code></td><td>When the segment throws an error. Must be a Client Component (uses <code>reset</code>).</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>Files placed</h3>

        </div>
        <div class="file-card">

    <section id="flow">
      <h2><span class="num">20</span> Full CRUD Flow — Reservations Example</h2>
      <div class="flow">
        <div class="flow-step">1. Admin clicks "✓ تأكيد" on a reservation row</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>

        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">3. Server Action invoked: updateReservationStatus(id, "CONFIRMED")</div>
        <div class="flow-label">─── SERVER ───</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">4. requireAdmin() — session verified<br>5. prisma.reservation.update({ data: { status: "CONFIRMED" } })</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>

    <section id="security">
      <h2><span class="num">21</span> Defense-in-Depth — Five Layers</h2>
      <div class="layers">
        <div class="layer client"><strong>Layer 1 · Client Guard</strong> — Buttons hidden by role (<code>isAdmin</code> prop). No security, only UX.</div>
        <div class="layer edge"><strong>Layer 2 · Edge Middleware</strong> — Redirects unauthenticated users away from <code>/admin/*</code> before any page loads.</div>
        <div class="layer guard"><strong>Layer 3 · Layout Guard</strong> — <code>admin/layout.tsx</code> verifies the session — safety net if middleware is bypassed.</div>
        <div class="layer action"><strong>Layer 4 · Server Action Guard</strong> — <code>requireAdmin()</code> runs on every mutation. Cannot be bypassed — the code lives server-side.</div>
        <div class="layer db"><strong>Layer 5 · Business Rule Guard</strong> — Cascade protection, reservation-history checks, and last-admin rule prevent destructive mistakes.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Why so many layers</strong>
        Each layer can fail independently (misconfiguration, middleware exception, session race). Defense-in-depth ensures no single point of failure compromises authorization.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="verify">
      <h2><span class="num">22</span> Verification Checklist</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Check</th><th>Action</th><th>Expected</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Route Groups</td><td>Visit <code>/</code>, <code>/menu</code>, <code>/login</code>, <code>/admin</code></td><td>Public pages show Navbar · login is centered · admin shows sidebar</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Dashboard counters</td><td>Visit <code>/admin</code></td><td>4 cards with real numbers</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Reservation status transition</td><td>Click "تأكيد" on PENDING</td><td>Badge turns green · buttons change</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Reservation filter</td><td>Click "مكتمل"</td><td>URL becomes <code>?status=COMPLETED</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Menu availability toggle</td><td>Click "⊘ إخفاء"</td><td>Item disappears from <code>/menu</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Menu featured toggle</td><td>Click "⭐ تمييز"</td><td>Item appears on <code>/</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Category cascade protection</td><td>Delete a category with items</td><td>Rejected with clear Arabic message</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Table reservation protection</td><td>Delete a table with reservations</td><td>Rejected with reservation count</td></tr>
          <tr><td>User self-delete protection</td><td>Try to delete your own account</td><td>Button not rendered</td></tr>
          <tr><td>User last-admin protection</td><td>Try to downgrade the last ADMIN</td><td>Rejected</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Active link</td><td>Visit <code>/admin/menu</code></td><td>"الأطباق" gold-highlighted</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Logout button</td><td>Click "🚪 تسجيل الخروج"</td><td>Confirm → redirect to <code>/login</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>STAFF access restriction</td><td>Login as STAFF, visit <code>/admin/users</code></td><td>Redirected to <code>/admin</code> (307)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>EmptyState</td><td>Apply a filter with zero results</td><td>Icon + title + optional action button</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">23</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Missing <code>"use client"</code></td><td><code>useTransition</code> errors</td><td>Add at top of any interactive component</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Forgetting <code>revalidatePath</code></td><td>Stale data after mutation</td><td>Call for every affected path</td></tr>
          <tr><td>No <code>requireAdmin()</code></td><td>Any user can call the action</td><td>Guard at the start of every action</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Cascade deletes silently</td><td>Orphaned data loss</td><td>Pre-check <code>_count</code> before delete</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Slug duplicated across items</td><td>Unique constraint error</td><td>Check <code>findFirst</code> with <code>NOT: { id }</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Deleting last admin</td><td>System locked out</td><td>Count other active admins first</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Editing email in user form</td><td>Session invalidated</td><td>Disable email field in edit mode</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Active link matches too broadly</td><td>All admin links highlighted</td><td>Use <code>exact: true</code> for the dashboard link</td></tr>
          <tr><td>No logout button</td><td>User stuck in a session</td><td>Add <code>signOut()</code> button in sidebar</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="glossary">
      <h2><span class="num">24</span> Technical Abbreviations Glossary</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Abbr.</th><th>Full Form</th><th>Plain-English Meaning</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>API</td><td>Application Programming Interface</td><td>Contract for program-to-program calls</td></tr>
          <tr><td>CRUD</td><td>Create, Read, Update, Delete</td><td>The four basic data operations</td></tr>
          <tr><td>CUID</td><td>Collision-resistant Unique Identifier</td><td>25-char ID; sortable, URL-safe</td></tr>
          <tr><td>FK</td><td>Foreign Key</td><td>Column pointing to another table's PK</td></tr>
          <tr><td>HTTP</td><td>HyperText Transfer Protocol</td><td>Protocol for browser-server communication</td></tr>
          <tr><td>JSX</td><td>JavaScript XML</td><td>React's HTML-like syntax</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ORM</td><td>Object-Relational Mapper</td><td>Translates objects ↔ SQL</td></tr>
          <tr><td>PK</td><td>Primary Key</td><td>Column uniquely identifying a row</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RBAC</td><td>Role-Based Access Control</td><td>Permissions assigned by user role</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RPC</td><td>Remote Procedure Call</td><td>Calls a function over a network</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RSC</td><td>React Server Components</td><td>React components rendered on the server</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RTL</td><td>Right-to-Left</td><td>Text direction for Arabic/Hebrew</td></tr>
          <tr><td>SQL</td><td>Structured Query Language</td><td>Standard relational database language</td></tr>
          <tr><td>UI</td><td>User Interface</td><td>What the user sees</td></tr>
          <tr><td>URL</td><td>Uniform Resource Locator</td><td>Web address</td></tr>
          <tr><td>UX</td><td>User Experience</td><td>Overall feel of using an app</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Zod</td><td>(library name)</td><td>TypeScript-first schema validation library</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

        <li>AdminSidebar with active link highlighting and logout button</li>

        <li>Loading and Error boundaries per route group</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>Engineering Outcomes</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><strong>Five-layer defense-in-depth</strong> — client, edge, layout, action, business rule</li>
        <li><strong>Consistent action pattern</strong> — authorize → validate → mutate → revalidate</li>
        <li><strong>Zero stale data</strong> — revalidatePath purges caches automatically</li>
        <li><strong>Impossible to lock out</strong> — last-admin rule guarantees access</li>
        <li><strong>Consistent UX</strong> — every list has empty/loading/error states</li>
        <li>Ready for Phase 9: Deployment on Vercel + Neon PostgreSQL</li>
      </ul>

    <header class="hero">
      <div class="kicker">Phase 12 · Menu EN + About + UX Polish</div>
      <h1>Content, UX, and Storytelling</h1>
      <p class="lede">Extend the internationalized foundation with three coordinated deliverables: bilingual menu items (Arabic + English fallback), an accessible auto-scroll UX pattern that turns validation errors into guided corrections, and a fully translated About page that tells the story of Lumière and its chef. Plus two small polish items: a fade-in scroll-to-top button and bilingual 404 pages for both Next.js and Vercel's CDN.</p>
      <div class="stack">
        <span>Bilingual Content</span><span>Auto-Scroll UX</span>
        <span>5-Locale About</span><span>Reusable Hook</span>
        <span>404 Handling</span><span>Production-Safe Migration</span>
      </div>
    </header>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal:</strong> Close three user-experience gaps that surfaced after Phase 11 shipped: menu items still showing Arabic on English pages, form errors hidden below the fold, and a missing About page. Each is a distinct problem requiring a distinct fix — all delivered in one cohesive phase.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li><strong>Bilingual menu items</strong> — add <code>nameEn</code> + <code>descriptionEn</code> columns to <code>MenuItem</code>, populate 12 dishes, and localize rendering via <code>getLocalizedName()</code>.</li>
        <li><strong>Admin form upgrade</strong> — two new optional English fields per dish, with a clear explanation of the edge case when the admin interface is in English.</li>
        <li><strong>Category dropdown localization</strong> — admin category selects show English names on non-Arabic locales.</li>
        <li><strong>Auto-scroll to first error</strong> — reusable hook applied to all 6 forms, using smooth scroll + delayed focus.</li>
        <li><strong>About page</strong> — 5-section story page with hero, story, chef bio, values, and CTA, fully translated in 5 locales.</li>
        <li><strong>Navbar 5th link</strong> — About between Menu and Reserve, with per-locale labels.</li>
        <li><strong>Scroll-to-top button</strong> — fade-in after 400px, positioned bottom-right (opposite WhatsApp).</li>
        <li><strong>Bilingual 404 handling</strong> — two layers: Next.js root fallback + Vercel static page for missing files.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="scope">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Three Features, One Phase</h2>
      <p>Three seemingly separate requests converged into one cohesive phase, because they share infrastructure and design patterns.</p>
      <div class="decisions">
        <div class="decision-card">
          <h4>🍽️ Bilingual Menu</h4>
          <p>Extends the <code>getLocalizedName()</code> pattern already proven with <code>Category.nameEn</code>. Same migration strategy, same helper, same admin UX.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="decision-card">
          <h4>🎯 Auto-Scroll UX</h4>
          <p>Built once as a hook. Applied to 6 forms. Solves a real-world problem: silent errors that hide below the fold after submit.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="decision-card">
          <h4>📖 About Page</h4>
          <p>Fully integrated with the 5-locale architecture from Phase 11. Same translation pattern, same metadata approach, same sitemap inclusion.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="callout info">
        <strong>Why bundle them?</strong>
        Each feature is small enough to fit in one session, and all three share the same release commit — keeping the git history clean and the Vercel deploy atomic.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="schema">
      <h2><span class="num">5</span> Part 1 · Schema — Add Two Nullable Columns</h2>
      <p><strong>The pattern:</strong> Extend the existing <code>Category.nameEn</code> approach to the <code>MenuItem</code> model. Two new <code>String?</code> fields — optional, never blocking, backward compatible.</p>
      <pre><code>model MenuItem {
  id             String   @id @default(cuid())
  name           String
  nameEn         String?           // ← NEW
  slug           String   @unique
  description    String?
  descriptionEn  String?           // ← NEW
  price          Float
  imageUrl       String?
  isAvailable    Boolean  @default(true)
  isFeatured     Boolean  @default(false)
  ...
}</code></pre>

      <h3>Why these are nullable</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Scenario</th><th>Result</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Existing dish has no English translation</td><td>DB stores <code>null</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Admin skips the English field</td><td>DB stores <code>null</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Non-Arabic user views the dish</td><td>Falls back to Arabic via <code>??</code> in the helper</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Zero-downtime migration</strong>
        Because the columns are nullable, the migration is non-breaking. Production data continues to work; only new writes populate the English fields.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="migration">
      <h2><span class="num">6</span> Part 1 · Migration + Seed</h2>
      <pre><code>npx prisma migrate dev --name add_menu_item_name_en</code></pre>

      <div class="terminal">
        <div class="terminal-bar"><span class="terminal-dot red"></span><span class="terminal-dot yellow"></span><span class="terminal-dot green"></span></div>
        <div class="terminal-body">
          <div class="out">Applying migration <span class="dim">`20261002075553_add_menu_item_name_en`</span></div>
          <div class="out">Your database is now in sync with your schema.</div>
          <div class="out"><span class="ok">✔ Generated Prisma Client (v6.19.3) to .\node_modules\@prisma\client in 580ms</span></div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <h3>Seed data strategy</h3>
      <p>Each dish in <code>prisma/data/menu-items.ts</code> gains <code>nameEn</code> and <code>descriptionEn</code>. Example for one dish:</p>
      <pre><code>{
  name: "شوربة العدس",
  nameEn: "Lentil Soup",
  slug: "lentil-soup",
  description: "شوربة عدس تقليدية مع الكمون والليمون",
  descriptionEn: "Traditional lentil soup with cumin and lemon",
  price: 45,
  isFeatured: false,
  categorySlug: "appetizers",
  imageUrl: "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1547592180-...",
}</code></pre>

      <h3>The seed.ts simplification</h3>
      <p>Instead of listing every field explicitly, the create loop now spreads the object directly:</p>
      <div class="two-col">
        <div class="col-card before">
          <h5>Before</h5>
          <pre style="margin:0.5rem 0;border:none;padding:0.75rem;font-size:0.7rem"><code>await prisma.menuItem.create({
  data: {
    name: itemData.name,
    slug: itemData.slug,
    description: itemData.description,
    price: itemData.price,
    isFeatured: itemData.isFeatured,
    imageUrl: itemData.imageUrl,
    categoryId: category.id,
  },
})</code></pre>
        </div>
        <div class="col-card after">
          <h5>After</h5>
          <pre style="margin:0.5rem 0;border:none;padding:0.75rem;font-size:0.7rem"><code>await prisma.menuItem.create({
  data: {
    ...itemData,
    categoryId: category.id,
  },
})</code></pre>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Why the spread is better here</strong>
        Adding future fields (e.g., <code>nameFr</code>, <code>nameDe</code>) requires zero changes to <code>seed.ts</code>. The data file is the only place that grows.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="backfill">
      <h2><span class="num">7</span> Part 1 · Idempotent Backfill Script</h2>
      <p><strong>The problem:</strong> Vercel production has live data. Running <code>npm run db:seed</code> would wipe reservations and demo history.</p>
      <p><strong>The solution:</strong> A dedicated script that <em>updates in place</em> — one row at a time, matched by <code>slug</code>.</p>
      <pre><code>// scripts/update-menu-items-en.ts
const UPDATES = [
  { slug: "lentil-soup", nameEn: "Lentil Soup",
    descriptionEn: "Traditional lentil soup with cumin and lemon" },
  // ... 11 more entries
];

for (const update of UPDATES) {
  await prisma.menuItem.update({
    where: { slug: update.slug },
    data: {
      nameEn: update.nameEn,
      descriptionEn: update.descriptionEn,
    },
  });
}</code></pre>

      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Property</th><th>Value</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Destructive?</td><td>❌ No — only touches 2 columns</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Idempotent?</td><td>✅ Yes — running twice is safe</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Prod-safe?</td><td>✅ Yes — no DELETE, no TRUNCATE</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Fails loudly?</td><td>✅ <code>process.exit(1)</code> on any error</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="helper">
      <h2><span class="num">8</span> Part 1 · <code>getLocalizedName()</code> Extension</h2>
      <p><strong>The core insight:</strong> A single helper function decides which value to render, based on the current locale.</p>
      <pre><code>export function getLocalizedName(
  name: string,
  nameEn: string | null | undefined,
  locale: string
): string {
  if (locale === "ar") return name;
  return nameEn ?? name;
}</code></pre>

      <h3>Behavior table</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Locale</th><th>nameEn present?</th><th>Renders</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>ar</td><td>—</td><td>Arabic <code>name</code> (always)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>en/fr/de/es</td><td>✅ Yes</td><td>English <code>nameEn</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>en/fr/de/es</td><td>❌ No</td><td>Falls back to Arabic <code>name</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <div class="callout info">
        <strong>One helper, all content types</strong>
        The same function handles <code>Category.name</code>, <code>MenuItem.name</code>, and <code>MenuItem.description</code> — the shape of the arguments is identical: (arValue, enValue, locale).
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="public-pages">
      <h2><span class="num">9</span> Part 1 · Public Pages Update</h2>
      <p>Three pages needed localization. All follow the same pattern: fetch both columns, map results through <code>getLocalizedName()</code>, pass localized values to the presentation component.</p>

      <h3>Which pages changed</h3>
      <div class="layers">
        <div class="layer client"><strong>/[locale]/(public)/menu</strong> · menu grid — name + description localized per card</div>
        <div class="layer client"><strong>/[locale]/(public)/menu/[slug]</strong> · item detail — name in <code>&lt;h1&gt;</code>, description, metadata title, and <code>alt</code> attribute</div>
        <div class="layer client"><strong>/[locale]/(public)</strong> · homepage — featured dishes shown in current locale</div>
      </div>

      <h3>Why the presentation components stayed untouched</h3>
      <p><code>MenuItemCard.tsx</code> receives <code>item.name</code>, <code>item.description</code>, <code>item.category.name</code> — all already localized by the parent. The card is locale-agnostic and doesn't need to know about i18n.</p>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Layer separation preserved</strong>
        Data fetching + localization lives in the page (Server Component). Presentation lives in the card. Neither knows about the other's concerns.
      </div>

      <h3>Detail page — three places, not two</h3>
      <p>The <code>[slug]</code> page needed four total localizations, easy to miss the last one:</p>
      <ol>
        <li><code>&lt;h1&gt;</code> — item name</li>
        <li><code>&lt;p&gt;</code> — item description</li>
        <li><code>generateMetadata</code> — title + OpenGraph</li>
        <li><code>alt</code> attribute on the hero <code>&lt;Image&gt;</code> — <strong>the one that got missed initially</strong></li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="admin-form">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> Part 1 · Admin Form — Bilingual Fields</h2>
      <p>Two optional fields added to <code>MenuItemForm.tsx</code>, aligned to the <code>dir="ltr"</code> attribute (English is always left-to-right, even on RTL admin pages).</p>

      <h3>The four files touched</h3>

        <thead><tr><th>File</th><th>Change</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>messages/*.json</code> × 5</td><td>+4 keys: <code>nameEnLabel</code>, <code>nameEnPlaceholder</code>, <code>descriptionEnLabel</code>, <code>descriptionEnPlaceholder</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>validations/menu-item.ts</code></td><td>+2 Zod fields (optional, max 80 / 500)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>actions/admin-menu.ts</code></td><td>create + update + audit log before/after</td></tr>

          <tr><td><code>admin/menu/[id]/edit/page.tsx</code></td><td>Pass <code>nameEn</code>, <code>descriptionEn</code> to <code>initialData</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>Audit log integration</h3>
      <p>The <code>before</code> and <code>after</code> snapshots now include <code>nameEn</code>, so the Audit Log shows a diff when English names change:</p>
      <pre><code>before: { name: "حمص", nameEn: "Hummus", price: 55, ... }
after:  { name: "حمص", nameEn: "Hummus with Tahini", price: 55, ... }
//        └─ nameEn changed → visible in admin /audit-log</code></pre>

    <section id="dropdown">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> Part 1 · Category Dropdown Fix</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Bug caught during manual testing</strong>
        The menu item form's category dropdown showed Arabic names (<code>مقبلات</code>, <code>أطباق رئيسية</code>) even on English admin pages.
      </div>
      <p><strong>Root cause:</strong> The admin pages fetched categories with <code>select: { id, name, slug }</code> — no <code>nameEn</code> — so the data was Arabic by default.</p>
      <p><strong>Fix:</strong> Add <code>nameEn</code> to the select, then map through <code>getLocalizedName()</code> before passing to <code>MenuItemForm</code>.</p>
      <pre><code>const categoriesRaw = await prisma.category.findMany({
  orderBy: { displayOrder: "asc" },
  select: { id: true, name: true, nameEn: true, slug: true },
});

const categories = categoriesRaw.map((cat) => ({
  id: cat.id,
  name: getLocalizedName(cat.name, cat.nameEn, locale),
  slug: cat.slug,
}));</code></pre>

      <h3>Where the fix was applied</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>File</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>src/app/[locale]/admin/menu/new/page.tsx</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>src/app/[locale]/admin/menu/[id]/edit/page.tsx</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Lesson</strong>
        Whenever admin pages surface DB content as labels for other admins, they must run through <code>getLocalizedName()</code> just like public pages. The rule isn't "public pages localize" — it's "any content the user sees localizes."
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="tradeoff">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> Part 1 · The "English Admin" Trade-off</h2>
      <p><strong>The situation:</strong> An English admin logs into <code>/en/admin/menu/[id]/edit</code>. The form shows both a main "Dish Name" field (containing the Arabic name) and an "English Name" field (containing the English name).</p>

      <div class="two-col">
        <div class="col-card before">
          <h5>Option A — Hide the EN fields</h5>
          <p style="font-size:0.85rem;margin:0.5rem 0">On <code>/en/admin/*</code>, hide the EN fields entirely. Mirror the main fields into the EN columns on submit.</p>
          <p style="font-size:0.82rem;color:var(--danger);margin-top:0.5rem"><strong>Problem:</strong> If the admin edits a bilingual dish, the Arabic name overwrites the English one when they save. Silent data loss.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="col-card after">
          <h5>Option B — Keep them visible ✅</h5>
          <p style="font-size:0.85rem;margin:0.5rem 0">Always show both fields. Accept the "duplicate-looking" UI on English admin. Document the trade-off.</p>
          <p style="font-size:0.82rem;color:var(--success);margin-top:0.5rem"><strong>Chosen because:</strong> Zero silent data loss. Theoretical edge case documented for a future Phase 13 refinement.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <p><strong>Why this is the right call for now:</strong> The real admin is Arabic-speaking. The "English admin" is a portfolio-demo scenario. Hiding fields to solve a cosmetic "duplication" issue silently corrupts bilingual data — the wrong trade-off.</p>

      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Future refinement (Phase 13 candidate)</strong>
        On <code>/en/admin/*</code>, rename the main field label from "Dish Name" to "Arabic Dish Name" and the EN field to "English Dish Name". This makes the purpose explicit without hiding data.
      </div>
    </section>

    <!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
         PART 2 — AUTO-SCROLL UX
         ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

    <section id="ux-problem">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> Part 2 · The Real Problem</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Observed in manual testing</strong>
        Admin fills a form. Clicks "Add Dish". Nothing visible happens — the error message is 700px above, off-screen. Admin assumes the internet broke, or the app is stuck, or the button didn't register.
      </div>
      <p><strong>Root cause:</strong> When validation fails, errors appear inline <em>next to their fields</em>. If the field is scrolled out of view, the user has no signal about what happened.</p>

      <h3>Who this affects</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Form</th><th>Length</th><th>Risk of hidden error</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Menu item (new/edit)</td><td>~8 fields, 2 screens tall</td><td>High — errors can be 800px above</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Category</td><td>~5 fields</td><td>Medium</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Table</td><td>~4 fields</td><td>Low</td></tr>
          <tr><td>User</td><td>~6 fields</td><td>Medium</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Reservation</td><td>~7 fields</td><td>Medium</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Review</td><td>~4 fields</td><td>Low</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="industry">
      <h2><span class="num">14</span> Part 2 · Why "Error Near Button" is Wrong</h2>
      <p>The instinctive fix — a badge near the submit button saying "3 errors" — is a common anti-pattern. It was proposed but rejected. Here's why.</p>

      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Approach</th><th>User steps needed</th><th>Verdict</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><strong>Badge near button</strong></td><td>1. Notice badge · 2. Scroll up · 3. Find field · 4. Read error · 5. Fix</td><td>❌ 5 steps</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Auto-scroll to error</strong></td><td>1. See scroll · 2. Read error · 3. Fix</td><td>✅ 3 steps</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Toast notification</strong></td><td>1. Read toast · 2. Scroll up · 3. Find field · 4. Fix</td><td>❌ Toast disappears before scroll</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>What real products do</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><strong>Stripe Checkout</strong> — scrolls to first error field</li>
        <li><strong>GitHub settings</strong> — scrolls + focuses the first invalid input</li>
        <li><strong>Shopify admin</strong> — scrolls + focuses</li>
        <li><strong>Google Forms</strong> — scrolls + red highlight</li>
        <li><strong>Vercel deployments</strong> — same pattern</li>
      </ul>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>The industry standard</strong>
        Auto-scroll is universal. Users' eyes follow the scroll motion; they land on the error naturally. No second action required.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="hook">
      <h2><span class="num">15</span> Part 2 · The <code>useScrollToFirstError</code> Hook</h2>
      <p>A single hook, applied to all 6 forms. Built once, used everywhere — modular design.</p>
      <pre><code>export function useScrollToFirstError(
  fieldErrors: Record&lt;string, string[]&gt; | undefined
) {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!fieldErrors) return;
    const firstKey = Object.keys(fieldErrors)[0];
    if (!firstKey) return;

    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      const input = document.querySelector(`[name="${firstKey}"]`);
      if (!(input instanceof HTMLElement)) return;

      input.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth", block: "center" });

      setTimeout(() => {
        if (input instanceof HTMLInputElement ||
            input instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement ||
            input instanceof HTMLSelectElement) {
          input.focus({ preventScroll: true });
        }
      }, 400);
    }, 50);

    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  }, [fieldErrors]);
}</code></pre>

      <h3>The three clever details</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Detail</th><th>Why</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>setTimeout(…, 50)</code></td><td>Lets React paint the error message first — otherwise layout height shifts mid-scroll and the target moves</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>setTimeout(…, 400)</code> before focus</td><td>Lets the smooth-scroll animation finish before focus moves — otherwise focus triggers a second native scroll that fights the smooth one</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>focus({ preventScroll: true })</code></td><td>Focus the input without letting the browser scroll again. The user just watched the scroll — they don't need a second one</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>Why <code>document.querySelector</code> instead of refs</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Simpler — no ref threading through every form</li>
        <li>Scoped to <code>[name="..."]</code> — collision risk is negligible since forms render one at a time</li>
        <li>Server Actions return <code>fieldErrors</code> keyed by input <code>name</code> — perfect match</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="six-forms">
      <h2><span class="num">16</span> Part 2 · Applied to 6 Forms</h2>
      <p>Two lines per form. Same pattern across all of them.</p>

      <h3>The pattern (4 forms with local state)</h3>
      <pre><code>const [fieldErrors, setFieldErrors] = useState({});

useScrollToFirstError(
  Object.keys(fieldErrors).length > 0 ? fieldErrors : undefined
);</code></pre>

      <h3>The pattern (2 forms with result state)</h3>
      <p>Reservation and Review use a discriminated union <code>result</code> — the errors live under <code>result.fieldErrors</code>:</p>
      <pre><code>const [result, setResult] = useState&lt;Result&gt;({ kind: "idle" });

useScrollToFirstError(
  result.kind === "error" ? result.fieldErrors : undefined
);</code></pre>

      <h3>Forms updated</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Form</th><th>State pattern</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>MenuItemForm</td><td>local <code>fieldErrors</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>CategoryForm</td><td>local <code>fieldErrors</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>TableForm</td><td>local <code>fieldErrors</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>UserForm</td><td>local <code>fieldErrors</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>ReservationForm</td><td>discriminated <code>result</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>ReviewForm</td><td>discriminated <code>result</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>The ReviewForm exception</h3>
      <p>Review's "Please select a star rating" error lives at the bottom of the form, right above the submit button. Since users are already at the bottom when they click submit, the error is <strong>already visible</strong>. No scroll needed.</p>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Why the hook silently does nothing here</strong>
        The star rating error is a cross-field <code>result.message</code>, not a <code>result.fieldErrors[fieldName]</code>. The hook looks for <code>fieldErrors</code> — finds none — returns early. Perfect.
      </div>
    </section>

  return (
    &lt;div className="bg-card border border-border rounded-2xl p-8 text-center"&gt;

        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>Hero</code></td><td>kicker · title · subtitle</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Story</code></td><td>kicker · title · paragraph1 · paragraph2 · paragraph3</td></tr>

          <tr><td><code>Values</code></td><td>kicker · title · quality{Title,Body} · authenticity{Title,Body} · hospitality{Title,Body}</td></tr>

        The About page contains full prose paragraphs, not short labels. This is a real translation exercise — 3 long paragraphs per locale × 5 locales = 15 paragraph translations. Google Translate assisted, then human-refined.

         BONUS
         ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

    <section id="scroll-top">
      <h2><span class="num">20</span> Bonus · Scroll-to-Top Button</h2>
      <p>A small circular button that appears after 400px of scroll, positioned bottom-right (opposite the WhatsApp button on the bottom-left).</p>

      <h3>Design decisions</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Decision</th><th>Rationale</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>SHOW_AFTER_PX = 400</code></td><td>Industry standard (Stripe, Tailwind docs use 300-500px)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Fade + slide-in</td><td>Opacity + 12px translate — subtle motion, not jarring</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Physical <code>right-6</code> (not logical <code>end-6</code>)</td><td>WhatsApp is also physically at <code>left-6</code>. Keeping both physical preserves ergonomics across RTL/LTR</td></tr>
          <tr><td>48×48px circular</td><td>Big enough to tap on mobile, small enough not to compete with content</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Icon only (SVG chevron)</td><td>No text label — <code>aria-label</code> handles accessibility</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>pointer-events-none</code> when hidden</td><td>Invisible button doesn't intercept clicks</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <pre><code>useEffect(() => {
  function handleScroll() {
    setVisible(window.scrollY > SHOW_AFTER_PX);
  }
  handleScroll();
  window.addEventListener("scroll", handleScroll, { passive: true });
  return () => window.removeEventListener("scroll", handleScroll);
}, []);</code></pre>

      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Passive scroll listener</strong>
        <code>{ passive: true }</code> tells the browser the handler won't <code>preventDefault()</code> — enables the browser's hardware-accelerated scroll optimizations.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="root-404">
      <h2><span class="num">21</span> Bonus · Root 404 Pages</h2>
      <p>Two independent 404 layers — one for Next.js routes, one for Vercel's CDN.</p>

      <h3>Layer 1 — Next.js route 404</h3>
      <p><code>src/app/not-found.tsx</code> catches any unmatched route not inside a valid <code>[locale]</code> prefix.</p>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Requirement discovered the hard way</strong>
        Root-level <code>not-found.tsx</code> must include its own <code>&lt;html&gt;</code> and <code>&lt;body&gt;</code> tags — because the root layout is a passthrough (returns <code>children</code>), not a full document. Without these tags, Next.js throws "Missing &lt;html&gt; and &lt;body&gt; tags in the root layout."
      </div>

      <h3>The Client Component conversion</h3>
      <p>Two ESLint/TypeScript errors surfaced:</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Error</th><th>Cause</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>react/no-unescaped-entities</code></td><td>Raw apostrophes in "you're" / "Don't"</td><td>Use <code>&amp;apos;</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Type 'string' is not assignable to 'MouseEventHandler'</td><td><code>onClick="history.back()"</code> — string form works in HTML, not JSX</td><td>Convert to <code>"use client"</code> + arrow function</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>Layer 2 — Vercel static 404</h3>
      <p><code>public/404.html</code> is served by Vercel's CDN <em>before</em> Next.js runs, for missing static files. It has no access to <code>NEXT_LOCALE</code> or URL context — so it's bilingual English + Arabic with inline CSS.</p>

      <div class="callout info">
        <strong>Two layers, two purposes</strong>
        <ul style="margin-top:0.5rem;margin-bottom:0">
          <li><strong>Next.js layer</strong> — for missing app routes (<code>/en/wrong-page</code>)</li>
          <li><strong>Vercel layer</strong> — for missing static files (<code>/old-image.png</code>, <code>/legacy.html</code>)</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </section>

    <!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
         ERRORS
         ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

    <section id="errors">
      <h2><span class="num">22</span> The Errors Journey</h2>
      <p>Nine distinct issues surfaced during Phase 12 — each one teaches a specific lesson.</p>

      <div class="error-journey">
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 1 — Prisma Studio shows English names in DB</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Migration + seed work, but Prisma Studio shows nameEn filled — expected this time ✅</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Lesson:</strong> When a migration adds nullable columns, <code>db:seed</code> populates them; <code>update-menu-items-en.ts</code> fills existing prod rows. Two paths for two environments.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 2 — VS Code stale TS after migration</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Property 'nameEn' does not exist on type 'MenuItem'</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> <code>Ctrl + Shift + P → TypeScript: Restart TS Server</code>. Terminal <code>tsc --noEmit</code> was silent — the IDE was holding a stale Prisma Client in memory.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 3 — alt attribute still Arabic in English pages</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Right-click image on /en/menu/hummus → alt="حمص بالطحينة"</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> The <code>&lt;Image alt={item.name}&gt;</code> on the item detail page was the "hidden 4th" localization spot. Changed to <code>alt={localizedName}</code>.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 4 — "Try again" button didn't recover</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Clicking Try Again re-renders the same error — user must refresh browser</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> <code>router.refresh()</code> before <code>reset()</code>. The RSC payload was cached with the error state; refreshing busts the cache, then reset clears the boundary.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 5 — Root 404 missing document tags</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Missing &lt;html&gt; and &lt;body&gt; tags in the root layout.</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Root <code>not-found.tsx</code> must provide its own <code>&lt;html&gt;</code> + <code>&lt;body&gt;</code>, because the root layout is a passthrough, not a full document.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 6 — ESLint no-unescaped-entities</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">`'` can be escaped with `&amp;apos;`, `&amp;lsquo;`, `&amp;#39;`, `&amp;rsquo;`</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Replace <code>you're</code> → <code>you&amp;apos;re</code>, <code>Don't</code> → <code>Don&amp;apos;t</code>. ESLint's React rules require escaped entities for cleanliness.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 7 — onClick string in Server Component</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'MouseEventHandler&lt;HTMLButtonElement&gt;'</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> <code>onClick="history.back()"</code> works in plain HTML but not JSX. Convert file to <code>"use client"</code> + <code>onClick={() =&gt; window.history.back()}</code>. Also replaces the <code>metadata</code> export with explicit <code>&lt;meta&gt;</code> tags.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 8 — AboutPageProps removed but still used</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Cannot find name 'AboutPageProps'</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Restore the type declaration. Only the page body should drop <code>params</code>; <code>generateMetadata</code> still needs the type to extract <code>locale</code>.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 9 — Tailwind canonical class hint</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">The class `aspect-16/9` can be written as `aspect-video`</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Rename to <code>aspect-video</code>. Warning only, but matches Tailwind's canonical vocabulary.</div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">24</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Running <code>db:seed</code> on prod</td><td>Wipes reservations</td><td>Use <code>update-menu-items-en.ts</code> instead</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Forgetting <code>getLocalizedName</code> on one page</td><td>Arabic shows up in one specific place</td><td>Grep for <code>item.name</code> / <code>item.description</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Hiding EN fields on English admin</td><td>Silent overwrite of English names</td><td>Keep them visible, accept cosmetic duplication</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Auto-scroll without focus delay</td><td>Page scrolls then jumps back</td><td>400ms delay before <code>focus({ preventScroll: true })</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Missing <code>&lt;html&gt;/&lt;body&gt;</code> in root 404</td><td>"Missing tags" runtime error</td><td>Include them in the self-contained file</td></tr>
          <tr><td>String <code>onClick</code> in JSX</td><td>TypeScript rejects it</td><td>Convert to <code>"use client"</code> + arrow function</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Raw apostrophes in JSX text</td><td>ESLint <code>no-unescaped-entities</code></td><td>Use <code>&amp;apos;</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Scroll button on short forms</td><td>Button appears where it's useless</td><td>400px threshold auto-hides it on short pages</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Prisma schema changed, VS Code stale</td><td>Red squiggles but <code>tsc</code> clean</td><td><code>Restart TS Server</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Running migration before committing code</td><td>Server code references columns that don't exist in prod</td><td>Commit both migration + code before pushing</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="glossary">
      <h2><span class="num">25</span> Technical Abbreviations Glossary</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Abbr.</th><th>Full Form</th><th>Plain-English Meaning</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>UX</td><td>User Experience</td><td>How pleasant it feels to use an app</td></tr>
          <tr><td>a11y</td><td>Accessibility</td><td>Making apps usable for everyone, including disabilities</td></tr>
          <tr><td>CDN</td><td>Content Delivery Network</td><td>Geographically distributed cache servers</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RSC</td><td>React Server Components</td><td>Components rendered on the server</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RTL</td><td>Right-to-Left</td><td>Text direction for Arabic, Hebrew, Farsi</td></tr>
          <tr><td>LTR</td><td>Left-to-Right</td><td>Text direction for Latin scripts</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Hook</td><td>(React concept)</td><td>Reusable function that taps into React state</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Idempotent</td><td>—</td><td>Safe to run multiple times — same result each run</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Nullable</td><td>—</td><td>A DB column that can hold NULL (no value)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Spread</td><td><code>...obj</code></td><td>JS syntax to expand object properties inline</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Smooth scroll</td><td>—</td><td>Browser animation between scroll positions</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Threshold</td><td>—</td><td>A minimum amount before something activates</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Passive listener</td><td>—</td><td>Event listener that won't call preventDefault()</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Focus</td><td>—</td><td>Which element receives keyboard input</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Edge case</td><td>—</td><td>Unusual scenario that most users won't hit</td></tr>
          <tr><td>WCAG</td><td>Web Content Accessibility Guidelines</td><td>International a11y standard</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

// استخدام upsert: آمن للتشغيل المتكرر
// الاستخدام: npm run db:admin

import "dotenv/config";
import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";
import { hashPassword } from "../src/lib/auth/password";

const prisma = new PrismaClient();

// ─── حساب الإنتاج (لا يُنشر أبداً) ───
const ADMIN_DATA = {
  email: "admin@lumiere.com",
  password: "Admin@Lumiere2026",
  name: "مدير Lumière",
  role: "ADMIN",
  isDemo: false,
} as const;

// ─── حساب العرض (يُنشر في README للـ Portfolio) ───
const DEMO_DATA = {
  email: "demo@lumiere.com",
  password: "Demo2026!",
  name: "Demo User",
  role: "ADMIN",
  isDemo: true,
} as const;

// ─── دالة مساعدة: إنشاء/تحديث مستخدم ───
async function upsertUser(data: {
  email: string;
  password: string;
  name: string;
  role: string;
  isDemo: boolean;
}) {
  if (data.password.length < 8) {
    throw new Error(`كلمة السر قصيرة جداً للحساب: ${data.email}`);
  }

  const passwordHash = await hashPassword(data.password);

  const user = await prisma.user.upsert({
    where: { email: data.email },
    update: {
      passwordHash,
      name: data.name,
      role: data.role,
      isActive: true,
    },
    create: {
      email: data.email,
      passwordHash,
      name: data.name,
      role: data.role,
      isActive: true,
    },
  });

  return user;
}

// ─── نقطة الدخول ───
async function main() {
  console.log("\n👤 إنشاء / تحديث الحسابات...\n");

  // 1. حساب الإنتاج
  const admin = await upsertUser(ADMIN_DATA);
  console.log("✅ حساب الإنتاج (admin):");
  console.log(`   ID:        ${admin.id}`);
  console.log(`   البريد:    ${admin.email}`);
  console.log(`   الاسم:     ${admin.name}`);
  console.log(`   الدور:     ${admin.role}`);
  console.log(`   كلمة السر: ${ADMIN_DATA.password}  ← احفظها في مكان آمن`);
  console.log(`   ⚠️  لا تُنشر هذه البيانات أبداً`);

  // 2. حساب العرض
  const demo = await upsertUser(DEMO_DATA);
  console.log("\n✅ حساب العرض (demo):");
  console.log(`   ID:        ${demo.id}`);
  console.log(`   البريد:    ${demo.email}`);
  console.log(`   الاسم:     ${demo.name}`);
  console.log(`   الدور:     ${demo.role}`);
  console.log(`   كلمة السر: ${DEMO_DATA.password}  ← عام للـ Portfolio`);
  console.log(`   ℹ️  يمكن نشره في README — تغييراته ستُعاد تعيينها`);

  console.log("\n✨ اكتمل الإعداد\n");
}

  .catch((error) => {
