    <header class="hero">
      <div class="kicker">Phase 03 · API Layer</div>
      <h1>Route Handlers, Prisma Singleton &amp; Dynamic Routes</h1>
      <p class="lede">Build the HTTP API layer that exposes the database to any external consumer — mobile app, Postman, third-party integration — using Next.js Route Handlers with a consistent JSON envelope and discipline around HTTP status codes.</p>
      <div class="stack">
        <span>Route Handlers</span><span>Prisma Singleton</span>
        <span>Dynamic Routes</span><span>REST API</span><span>HTTP Status Codes</span>
      </div>
    </header>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal:</strong> Expose the seeded database through HTTP endpoints that any external consumer can use — without coupling them to the frontend.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li><code>src/lib/prisma.ts</code> — Prisma Client singleton (hot-reload safe, absolute SQLite path).</li>
        <li><code>GET /api/menu/categories</code> — returns all categories with item counts.</li>
        <li><code>GET /api/menu/items</code> — returns all items with <code>?category=</code>, <code>?featured=</code>, <code>?limit=</code> filters.</li>
        <li><code>GET /api/menu/items/[slug]</code> — returns a single item by slug, or 404.</li>
        <li>Consistent JSON envelope: <code>{ success, data }</code> or <code>{ success, error }</code>.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="decision">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Route Handler vs Server Action vs Server Component</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Style</th><th>Use Case</th><th>Chosen For</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><strong>Route Handlers</strong> (<code>app/api/**/route.ts</code>)</td><td>External HTTP consumers, webhooks, mobile apps</td><td>✅ Menu endpoints</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Server Actions</strong> (<code>"use server"</code>)</td><td>Internal form submissions from React components</td><td>Phase 5 (reservations)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Server Components</strong></td><td>Direct DB access from page components</td><td>Phase 4 (menu UI)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Legacy API Routes (<code>pages/api/</code>)</td><td>Next.js &lt; 13 pattern</td><td>❌ Deprecated</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Engineering rationale</strong>
        Route Handlers are the only API style producing a stable public URL. Server Actions are opaque RPC endpoints — not shareable, not testable via Postman, not consumable by a mobile app. The menu must be consumable by external systems, so Route Handlers win.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="routing">
      <h2><span class="num">3</span> File-Based Routing Mental Model</h2>
      <p><strong>No central router file.</strong> Directories ARE the URL.</p>
      <div class="route-map">
        <div class="file">src/app/api/menu/categories/route.ts</div>
        <div class="arrow">→</div>
        <div class="url">/api/menu/categories</div>

        <div class="file">src/app/api/menu/items/route.ts</div>
        <div class="arrow">→</div>
        <div class="url">/api/menu/items</div>

        <div class="file">src/app/api/menu/items/[slug]/route.ts</div>
        <div class="arrow">→</div>
        <div class="url">/api/menu/items/&lt;any-slug&gt;</div>

        <div class="file">src/app/api/reservations/route.ts</div>
        <div class="arrow">→</div>
        <div class="url">/api/reservations</div>
      </div>

      <h3>Comparison to Django</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Concept</th><th>Django</th><th>Next.js App Router</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Route registry</td><td><code>urls.py</code> (central)</td><td>Folder names (distributed)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>View function</td><td><code>views.py</code></td><td><code>route.ts</code> (named exports)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>URL parameters</td><td><code>&lt;slug:slug&gt;</code> in path</td><td><code>[slug]</code> folder name</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Query strings</td><td><code>request.GET</code></td><td><code>new URL(request.url).searchParams</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="commands">
      <h2><span class="num">4</span> Complete Commands Table</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Command</th><th>Purpose</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>1</td><td><code>npx tsc --noEmit</code></td><td>TypeScript check — verifies singleton compiles</td></tr>
          <tr><td>2</td><td><code>npm run dev</code></td><td>Start dev server (default port 3000)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>3</td><td><code>curl http://localhost:3000/api/menu/categories</code></td><td>Test endpoint from CLI (alternative to browser)</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>No new packages required in Phase 3.</strong> Everything ships with Next.js and Prisma.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="structure">
      <h2><span class="num">5</span> Target Folder Structure</h2>
      <div class="filetree">
        <div><span class="dir">src/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="dir">app/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-2"><span class="dir new">api/</span> <span class="note">← NEW: API routes live here</span></div>
        <div class="indent-3"><span class="dir">menu/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-3" style="padding-left:5rem"><span class="dir">categories/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-3" style="padding-left:6.25rem"><span class="file new">route.ts</span> <span class="note">← GET /api/menu/categories</span></div>
        <div class="indent-3" style="padding-left:5rem"><span class="dir">items/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-3" style="padding-left:6.25rem"><span class="file new">route.ts</span> <span class="note">← GET /api/menu/items</span></div>
        <div class="indent-3" style="padding-left:6.25rem"><span class="dir">[slug]/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-3" style="padding-left:7.5rem"><span class="file new">route.ts</span> <span class="note">← GET /api/menu/items/:slug</span></div>
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="dir">lib/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-2"><span class="file new">prisma.ts</span> <span class="note">← NEW: Prisma singleton</span></div>
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="dir">generated/prisma/</span> <span class="note">← from Phase 2</span></div>
      </div>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Rule enforced</strong>
        No <code>components/</code> or <code>lib/</code> may live inside <code>app/</code>. App Router treats every subfolder as a URL segment — a stray <code>components/</code> inside <code>app/</code> would create a phantom <code>/components/...</code> route.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="singleton">
      <h2><span class="num">6</span> Why a Prisma Singleton?</h2>
      <h3>The hot-reload problem</h3>
      <ol>
        <li>Developer saves a file.</li>
        <li>Next.js dev server reloads the module graph (HMR).</li>
        <li>Every reload executes <code>new PrismaClient()</code> again.</li>
        <li>Each client opens a new database connection pool.</li>
        <li>After ~20 saves, the pool exceeds SQLite/Postgres limits.</li>
        <li>Errors: <code>Too many clients</code>, <code>SQLITE_BUSY</code>, or silent hangs.</li>
      </ol>
      <p><strong>The Singleton fix:</strong> Store one <code>PrismaClient</code> instance on <code>globalThis</code>. On reload, reuse it.</p>

      <h3>src/lib/prisma.ts — Full File</h3>
      <pre><code>import path from 'node:path'
import { PrismaClient } from '../generated/prisma/client'

const globalForPrisma = globalThis as unknown as {
  prisma: PrismaClient | undefined
}

const sqlitePath = path
  .join(process.cwd(), 'prisma', 'dev.db')
  .replace(/\\/g, '/')

export const prisma =
  globalForPrisma.prisma ??
  new PrismaClient({
    datasourceUrl: `file:${sqlitePath}`,
    log: ['error', 'warn'],
  })

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') {
  globalForPrisma.prisma = prisma
}</code></pre>

      <h3>Line-by-line rationale</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>import path from 'node:path'</code> — Node's path utility; the <code>node:</code> prefix is ESM best practice.</li>
        <li><code>globalThis as unknown as {...}</code> — TypeScript cast so <code>globalThis.prisma</code> is type-safe.</li>
        <li><code>path.join(process.cwd(), 'prisma', 'dev.db')</code> — builds an absolute path from the project root.</li>
        <li><code>.replace(/\\/g, '/')</code> — normalizes Windows backslashes to forward slashes for URI format.</li>
        <li><code>??</code> (nullish coalescing) — reuse existing instance if present, else create new.</li>
        <li><code>datasourceUrl</code> — overrides the <code>.env</code> value at runtime (fixes the path resolution bug — see next section).</li>
        <li><code>NODE_ENV !== 'production'</code> — only cache globally in dev (production has no HMR).</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="pathbug">
      <h2><span class="num">7</span> The SQLite Path Resolution Bug &amp; Fix</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Symptom encountered</strong>
        <code>Error querying the database: Error code 14: Unable to open the database file</code>
        <code>GET /api/menu/categories 500 in 10.2s</code>
      </div>
      <p><strong>Root cause:</strong> <code>DATABASE_URL="file:./dev.db"</code> in <code>.env</code> is <strong>relative</strong>. Its meaning depends on who reads it:</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Consumer</th><th>Working Directory</th><th>Resolves To</th><th>Works?</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>prisma migrate</code></td><td><code>prisma/</code></td><td><code>prisma/dev.db</code></td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>prisma studio</code></td><td><code>prisma/</code></td><td><code>prisma/dev.db</code></td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>prisma db seed</code></td><td><code>prisma/</code></td><td><code>prisma/dev.db</code></td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong><code>next dev</code> runtime</strong></td><td>project root</td><td><code>./dev.db</code> (wrong!)</td><td>❌</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>The fix:</strong> In <code>src/lib/prisma.ts</code>, compute an absolute path at runtime:</p>
      <pre><code>const sqlitePath = path.join(process.cwd(), 'prisma', 'dev.db')</code></pre>
      <p><strong>WHY this is portable:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li><code>process.cwd()</code> always returns the project root when Next.js runs.</li>
        <li>No hardcoded <code>D:\...</code> paths — works on any machine.</li>
        <li>CLI tools keep using <code>.env</code> (relative) — no change needed there.</li>
      </ul>
      <p><strong>Production note:</strong> When migrating to PostgreSQL (Phase 9), <code>datasourceUrl</code> will be removed and <code>.env</code> will hold the hosted URL directly (no relative path issue exists for network URLs).</p>
    </section>

    <section id="categories">
      <h2><span class="num">8</span> GET /api/menu/categories</h2>
      <pre><code>import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma'

export async function GET() {
  try {
    const categories = await prisma.category.findMany({
      orderBy: { displayOrder: 'asc' },
      select: {
        id: true,
        name: true,
        slug: true,
        description: true,
        _count: {
          select: { items: true },
        },
      },
    })

    return NextResponse.json({
      success: true,
      data: categories,
    })
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[GET /api/menu/categories]', error)
    return NextResponse.json(
      { success: false, error: 'فشل تحميل التصنيفات' },
      { status: 500 }
    )
  }
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Named export <code>GET</code> matches the HTTP method. Next.js invokes it for <code>GET /api/menu/categories</code>.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY this shape:</strong> Consistent <code>{ success, data }</code> envelope lets clients branch on <code>success</code> without parsing HTTP status text.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="query-select">
      <h2><span class="num">9</span> Query Deep-Dive — select, _count, orderBy</h2>
      <h3>orderBy: { displayOrder: 'asc' }</h3>
      <p>Sorts categories by the numeric <code>displayOrder</code> column. <strong>WHY:</strong> Admin controls menu order without editing code.</p>

      <h3>select: { id, name, slug, description }</h3>
      <p>Returns only the listed fields. <strong>WHY:</strong> Reduces payload size; prevents leaking future sensitive fields (e.g., <code>internalNotes</code>).</p>

      <h3>_count: { select: { items: true } }</h3>
      <p>Prisma's relation-count aggregation. Generates <code>SELECT COUNT(*) FROM menu_items WHERE categoryId = ...</code> per row. <strong>WHY:</strong> The UI shows "3 items" per category without a second query. One request, zero N+1.</p>

      <h3>Example response</h3>
      <pre><code>{
  "success": true,
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "cmu...",
      "name": "مقبلات",
      "slug": "appetizers",
      "description": "أطباق خفيفة...",
      "_count": { "items": 3 }
    }
  ]
}</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="items">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> GET /api/menu/items with Filters</h2>
      <pre><code>import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma'

export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  try {
    const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url)
    const categorySlug = searchParams.get('category')
    const featured = searchParams.get('featured')
    const limit = searchParams.get('limit')

    const items = await prisma.menuItem.findMany({
      where: {
        isAvailable: true,
        ...(categorySlug && { category: { slug: categorySlug } }),
        ...(featured === 'true' && { isFeatured: true }),
      },
      orderBy: [{ isFeatured: 'desc' }, { name: 'asc' }],
      take: limit ? parseInt(limit, 10) : undefined,
      include: {
        category: {
          select: { id: true, name: true, slug: true },
        },
      },
    })

    return NextResponse.json({ success: true, data: items })
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[GET /api/menu/items]', error)
    return NextResponse.json(
      { success: false, error: 'فشل تحميل الأطباق' },
      { status: 500 }
    )
  }
}</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="spread">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> Query Deep-Dive — Spread Conditions &amp; include</h2>
      <h3>The spread-condition pattern</h3>
      <pre><code>...(categorySlug && { category: { slug: categorySlug } })</code></pre>
      <p><strong>How it works:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>If <code>categorySlug</code> is truthy → spreads <code>{ category: { slug: '...' } }</code> into <code>where</code>.</li>
        <li>If <code>categorySlug</code> is <code>null</code> → spreads <code>false</code> (Prisma ignores non-objects).</li>
      </ul>
      <p><strong>WHY instead of if/else:</strong> Keeps the query as a single expression. Composable: add more filters without nested branches.</p>

      <h3>include vs select</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Keyword</th><th>Behavior</th><th>Use When</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>select</code></td><td>Returns only the listed fields</td><td>You know exactly what you need</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>include</code></td><td>Returns all scalar fields + relations</td><td>You want everything plus relation data</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Here:</strong> <code>include</code> returns all item fields + a trimmed category object.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="matrix">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> Filter Test Matrix</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>#</th><th>URL</th><th>Expected Result</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>1</td><td><code>/api/menu/items</code></td><td>12 items (all available)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>2</td><td><code>/api/menu/items?category=appetizers</code></td><td>3 items (only appetizers)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>3</td><td><code>/api/menu/items?featured=true</code></td><td>4 items (hummus, kebab, knafeh, coffee)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>4</td><td><code>/api/menu/items?category=desserts&amp;featured=true</code></td><td>1 item (knafeh only)</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Observed in dev logs:</strong></p>
      <pre><code>GET /api/menu/items 200
GET /api/menu/items?category=appetizers 200
GET /api/menu/items?featured=true 200
GET /api/menu/items?category=desserts&amp;featured=true 200</code></pre>
      <p><strong>WHY this matters:</strong> Proves <code>searchParams</code> parsing, conditional spread, and combined filters all compose correctly.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="slug">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> GET /api/menu/items/[slug] (Dynamic Route)</h2>
      <pre><code>import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma'

type RouteParams = {
  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
}

export async function GET(request: NextRequest, { params }: RouteParams) {
  try {
    const { slug } = await params

    const item = await prisma.menuItem.findUnique({
      where: { slug },
      include: {
        category: {
          select: { id: true, name: true, slug: true },
        },
      },
    })

    if (!item) {
      return NextResponse.json(
        { success: false, error: 'الطبق غير موجود' },
        { status: 404 }
      )
    }

    return NextResponse.json({ success: true, data: item })
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[GET /api/menu/items/[slug]]', error)
    return NextResponse.json(
      { success: false, error: 'فشل تحميل الطبق' },
      { status: 500 }
    )
  }
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Folder <code>[slug]</code> captures any URL segment as a string.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY <code>params: Promise&lt;...&gt;</code>:</strong> Next.js 15+ made route params async to support streaming metadata. <code>await params</code> is mandatory.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="notfound">
      <h2><span class="num">14</span> Query Deep-Dive — findUnique and 404 Handling</h2>
      <h3>findUnique({ where: { slug } })</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Compiles to <code>SELECT * FROM menu_items WHERE slug = ? LIMIT 1</code>.</li>
        <li>Requires <code>slug</code> to have a <code>@unique</code> constraint (it does — Phase 2).</li>
        <li><strong>WHY findUnique not findFirst:</strong> <code>findUnique</code> uses the DB index directly; <code>findFirst</code> scans. Faster + guarantees zero ambiguity.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>404 handling</h3>
      <pre><code>if (!item) {
  return NextResponse.json(
    { success: false, error: 'الطبق غير موجود' },
    { status: 404 }
  )
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>WHY explicit 404 instead of throwing:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>Throwing produces a generic 500.</li>
        <li>Clients must distinguish "resource missing" (404, do not retry) from "server broken" (500, retry).</li>
        <li>Browser DevTools confirms via <code>Failed to load resource: 404</code>.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="status">
      <h2><span class="num">15</span> HTTP Status Code Discipline</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Status</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Used In</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><strong>200</strong></td><td>Success</td><td>All GET routes on success</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>400</strong></td><td>Bad Request — malformed input</td><td>Phase 5: Zod failures</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>404</strong></td><td>Not Found — resource missing</td><td><code>/items/[slug]</code> no match</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>500</strong></td><td>Server Error — unexpected</td><td>Any caught exception</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>WHY explicit codes matter:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>CDNs, load balancers, and monitoring tools route on status.</li>
        <li>404 responses are not cached the same way 200 responses are.</li>
        <li>Mobile apps can apply retry logic only for 5xx.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Anti-pattern avoided</strong>
        Returning 200 for "not found" with <code>{ success: false }</code> — breaks HTTP semantics and confuses clients.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="envelope">
      <h2><span class="num">16</span> Response Envelope Design</h2>
      <h3>Success</h3>
      <pre><code>{ "success": true, "data": &lt;payload&gt; }</code></pre>
      <h3>Failure</h3>
      <pre><code>{ "success": false, "error": "رسالة عربية واضحة" }</code></pre>
      <p><strong>WHY this contract:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>Single branching point: <code>if (response.success) { ... } else { show(response.error) }</code>.</li>
        <li>Arabic error messages are ready to display directly.</li>
        <li>Future extensibility: add <code>meta: { pagination }</code> alongside <code>data</code> without breaking clients.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="flow">
      <h2><span class="num">17</span> Request Data Flow — Trace a Single Call</h2>
      <p><strong>Flow for <code>GET /api/menu/items?category=desserts</code>:</strong></p>
      <div class="flow">
        <div class="flow-step">1. Browser → GET /api/menu/items?category=desserts</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step">2. Next.js router matches → app/api/menu/items/route.ts → GET()</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">3a. new URL(request.url) → extracts searchParams<br>3b. searchParams.get('category') → "desserts"<br>3c. Spreads { category: { slug: 'desserts' } } into where</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">4. Prisma → SQL:<br>SELECT ... FROM menu_items<br>WHERE isAvailable = 1 AND categoryId IN (...)<br>ORDER BY isFeatured DESC, name ASC</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step">5. SQLite engine executes → returns rows</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step">6. Prisma deserializes → TypeScript objects</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step">7. NextResponse.json → serializes to JSON string</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step success">8. Response: 200, Content-Type: application/json</div>
      </div>
      <p><strong>Boundary rationale:</strong> Each transition (URL → object → SQL → JSON) validates shape. Any mismatch fails loudly and early.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="nofetch">
      <h2><span class="num">18</span> Why Not fetch() Between Server Components and API?</h2>
      <p><strong>Question:</strong> Now that we have <code>/api/menu/items</code>, should the menu page fetch it?</p>
      <p><strong>Answer:</strong> No — the menu page queries <code>prisma</code> directly.</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Approach</th><th>Network hops</th><th>Serialization</th><th>Latency</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Page → <code>fetch('/api/menu/items')</code> → Server → DB</td><td>2 (loopback + DB)</td><td>JSON twice</td><td>High</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Page → <code>prisma.menuItem.findMany()</code> → DB</td><td>1 (DB only)</td><td>None</td><td>Minimal</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>WHY keep both:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li><strong>Route Handlers exist for external consumers:</strong> mobile apps, partners, webhooks, Postman.</li>
        <li><strong>Server Components consume the database directly:</strong> internal, zero network, zero JSON.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>This is the core value of Next.js Full-Stack</strong>
        The internal API layer is optional, not mandatory.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="boundary">
      <h2><span class="num">19</span> Request Lifecycle — Server vs Client Boundaries</h2>
      <div class="flow">
        <div class="flow-step code" style="background:#fdecea;color:#c0392b;border-color:#c0392b;">CLIENT (Browser)<br>• HTML, CSS, minimal JS<br>• No Prisma, no DATABASE_URL, no secrets</div>
        <div class="flow-label">HTTP (JSON over TLS in production)</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code" style="background:#eaf7ef;color:#1e7e45;border-color:#27ae60;">SERVER (Node.js on Vercel / localhost)<br>• Route Handler executes here<br>• Prisma Client instantiated here<br>• dev.db / Postgres accessed here</div>
      </div>
      <p><strong>Boundary rationale:</strong> The client never touches the database. Every byte of data crossing the boundary is explicitly shaped by <code>NextResponse.json()</code>. Secrets never leak.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="verify">
      <h2><span class="num">20</span> Verification Checklist</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Check</th><th>Action</th><th>Expected</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>TypeScript clean</td><td><code>npx tsc --noEmit</code></td><td>No output</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Categories endpoint</td><td><code>http://localhost:3000/api/menu/categories</code></td><td>4 categories with <code>_count.items</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>All items</td><td><code>/api/menu/items</code></td><td>12 items</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Filter by category</td><td><code>/api/menu/items?category=appetizers</code></td><td>3 items</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Filter featured</td><td><code>/api/menu/items?featured=true</code></td><td>4 items</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Combined filters</td><td><code>/api/menu/items?category=desserts&amp;featured=true</code></td><td>1 item</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Single item (valid)</td><td><code>/api/menu/items/hummus</code></td><td>Full object</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Single item (invalid)</td><td><code>/api/menu/items/pizza</code></td><td>404 + error JSON</td></tr>
          <tr><td>DevTools check</td><td>Network tab</td><td>Status codes 200/404 correct</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">21</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Wrong filename</td><td>404 on route</td><td>File must be <code>route.ts</code> (not <code>.tsx</code>, not <code>index.ts</code>)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Missing <code>export</code></td><td>404 on route</td><td><code>export async function GET()</code> — <code>export</code> mandatory</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Wrong path for <code>lib/</code></td><td><code>Cannot find module '@/lib/prisma'</code></td><td><code>src/lib/prisma.ts</code> (not under <code>app/</code>)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Missing <code>.env</code> load</td><td><code>Environment variable not found</code></td><td>Runtime uses absolute path in <code>lib/prisma.ts</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>searchParams</code> sync read</td><td>TypeScript error</td><td><code>new URL(request.url).searchParams</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>params</code> not awaited</td><td>Runtime warning in Next.js 15+</td><td><code>const { slug } = await params</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Cached response</td><td>Stale data after DB update</td><td>Add <code>export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'</code> if needed</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="glossary">
      <h2><span class="num">22</span> Technical Abbreviations Glossary</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Abbr.</th><th>Full Form</th><th>Plain-English Meaning</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>API</td><td>Application Programming Interface</td><td>Contract for program-to-program calls</td></tr>
          <tr><td>CDN</td><td>Content Delivery Network</td><td>Geographically distributed cache servers</td></tr>
          <tr><td>CLI</td><td>Command-Line Interface</td><td>Program operated by typing commands</td></tr>
          <tr><td>CUID</td><td>Collision-resistant Unique Identifier</td><td>25-char ID; sortable, URL-safe</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ESM</td><td>ECMAScript Modules</td><td>Standard <code>import</code>/<code>export</code> syntax</td></tr>
          <tr><td>FK</td><td>Foreign Key</td><td>Column referencing another table's PK</td></tr>
          <tr><td>HMR</td><td>Hot Module Replacement</td><td>Live code updates without full reload</td></tr>
          <tr><td>HTTP</td><td>HyperText Transfer Protocol</td><td>Protocol browsers use to talk to servers</td></tr>
          <tr><td>JSON</td><td>JavaScript Object Notation</td><td>Text format for structured data</td></tr>
          <tr><td>N+1</td><td>N-plus-1 Query Problem</td><td>1 query + N follow-ups; inefficient</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ORM</td><td>Object-Relational Mapper</td><td>Code layer translating objects ↔ SQL</td></tr>
          <tr><td>PK</td><td>Primary Key</td><td>Column uniquely identifying a row</td></tr>
          <tr><td>REST</td><td>Representational State Transfer</td><td>Style of APIs using HTTP verbs + URLs</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RPC</td><td>Remote Procedure Call</td><td>Style of APIs calling functions over network</td></tr>
          <tr><td>SQL</td><td>Structured Query Language</td><td>Standard language for relational databases</td></tr>
          <tr><td>TLS</td><td>Transport Layer Security</td><td>Encryption for network traffic</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

      <h1>Server Components, RTL Layout &amp; Interactive Menu UI</h1>
      <p class="lede">Build the customer-facing UI using Next.js Server Components for zero-JS data rendering, with minimal Client Components only where interactivity is required. The result: 5 Server Components, 1 Client Component, zero fetch calls to the internal API.</p>
      <div class="stack">
        <span>Server Components</span><span>Client Components</span>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal:</strong> Render the database through an elegant, RTL, mobile-responsive interface where only the small interactive parts ship JavaScript to the browser.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li>RTL Arabic layout with sticky Navbar and Lumière branding.</li>
        <li><code>/menu</code> page rendering 12 items via Server Component + Prisma.</li>
        <li><code>MenuItemCard</code> reusable component (grid-aligned, hover-animated).</li>
        <li><code>CategoryFilter</code> — a Client Component that filters via URL <code>searchParams</code>.</li>
        <li><code>/menu/[slug]</code> detail page with dynamic routing.</li>
        <li>Custom <code>not-found.tsx</code> for elegant 404s.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="server-client">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Architectural Decision — Server vs Client Components</h2>
      <p>The core Next.js 16 mental model:</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Aspect</th><th>Server Component</th><th>Client Component</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Executes on</td><td>Server</td><td>Browser</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Direct Prisma access</td><td>✅ Yes</td><td>❌ No (must <code>fetch</code>)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>useState</code> / <code>useEffect</code></td><td>❌ Forbidden</td><td>✅ Allowed</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>onClick</code> / <code>onChange</code></td><td>❌ Forbidden</td><td>✅ Allowed</td></tr>
          <tr><td>JS shipped to browser</td><td><strong>Zero</strong></td><td>Full bundle</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Default in App Router</td><td>✅ <strong>Yes</strong></td><td>Opt-in via <code>"use client"</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Rule of thumb</strong>
        Keep everything Server. Convert only the smallest interactive leaf to Client.
      </div>
      <p><strong>Engineering rationale:</strong> Every Client Component adds JS bytes to the browser bundle. On slow connections, more JS = slower Time-to-Interactive. Server Components deliver HTML with zero hydration cost.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="tree">
      <h2><span class="num">3</span> Component Tree for /menu</h2>
      <div class="tree">
        <div class="row">
          <span class="comp-name">📄 page.tsx</span>
          <span class="badge server">SERVER</span>
          <span class="desc">Queries Prisma directly</span>
        </div>
        <div class="row indent-1">
          <span class="comp-name">├─ Navbar</span>
          <span class="badge server">SERVER</span>
          <span class="desc">Static links</span>
        </div>
        <div class="row indent-1">
          <span class="comp-name">├─ CategoryFilter</span>
          <span class="badge client">CLIENT</span>
          <span class="desc">⚡ URL updates on click</span>
        </div>
        <div class="row indent-1">
          <span class="comp-name">└─ MenuItemCard × 12</span>
          <span class="badge server">SERVER</span>
          <span class="desc">Static render, zero JS</span>
        </div>
      </div>
      <p><strong>WHY this split:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>Only <code>CategoryFilter</code> needs interactivity → only it becomes Client.</li>
        <li><code>MenuItemCard</code> is pure presentation → stays Server, ships 0 bytes.</li>
        <li>The page itself stays Server → direct Prisma query, no <code>fetch</code>.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Anti-pattern avoided</strong>
        Marking <code>/menu/page.tsx</code> as <code>"use client"</code> — that would force all 12 cards to ship JS and require an HTTP call to <code>/api/menu/items</code>.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="components-rule">
      <h2><span class="num">6</span> Why components/ Cannot Live Inside app/</h2>
      <p><strong>The phantom route problem:</strong></p>
      <pre><code>src/app/components/layout/Navbar.tsx
        ^^^^^^^^^^
        treated as a URL segment</code></pre>
      <p>Next.js App Router generates routes from folder names. A folder <code>src/app/components/</code> is interpreted as the URL prefix <code>/components/</code>. Even though <code>Navbar.tsx</code> isn't a <code>page.tsx</code>, developers will:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>Waste time debugging why <code>/components/layout/Navbar</code> returns 404.</li>
        <li>Accidentally create conflicting routes.</li>
      </ul>
      <p><strong>The fix:</strong> Move <code>components/</code> up one level to <code>src/components/</code>.</p>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Verified in Phase 4</strong>
        <code>src/app/</code> → URLs only · <code>src/components/</code> → React components · <code>src/lib/</code> → logic · <code>src/generated/</code> → Prisma Client
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="tokens">
      <h2><span class="num">7</span> Design Tokens — globals.css</h2>
      <pre><code>@import "tailwindcss";

@theme {
  --color-background: #faf7f2;
  --color-foreground: #1a1a1a;
  --color-card:       #ffffff;
  --color-border:     #e5ddd0;

  --color-accent:       #c9a961;
  --color-accent-dark:  #a88847;
  --color-accent-light: #f5ecd9;

  --color-muted: #6b6b6b;

  --font-sans: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Tahoma, Arial, sans-serif;
}

body {
  background-color: var(--color-background);
  color: var(--color-foreground);
  font-family: var(--font-sans);
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> <code>@theme</code> block defines custom Tailwind v4 tokens that generate utility classes automatically (<code>bg-accent</code>, <code>text-muted</code>, <code>border-border</code>).</p>
      <p><strong>WHY this approach:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>Centralizes brand colors in one file — change once, propagates everywhere.</li>
        <li>Tailwind v4 uses CSS variables under the hood — no <code>tailwind.config.js</code> needed.</li>
        <li><code>system-ui</code> font avoids a 150 KB Google Fonts download.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="layout">
      <h2><span class="num">9</span> layout.tsx — Full File</h2>
      <pre><code>import type { Metadata } from "next";
import "./globals.css";
import { Navbar } from "@/components/layout/Navbar";

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: "Lumière | مطعم Lumière",
  description: "مطعم Lumière — تجربة طعام استثنائية",
};

export default function RootLayout({ children }: LayoutProps&lt;"/"&gt;) {
  return (
    &lt;html lang="ar" dir="rtl" className="h-full antialiased"&gt;
      &lt;body className="min-h-full flex flex-col"&gt;
        &lt;Navbar /&gt;
        &lt;main className="flex-1"&gt;{children}&lt;/main&gt;
      &lt;/body&gt;
    &lt;/html&gt;
  );
}</code></pre>
      <h3>Line-by-line rationale</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>lang="ar"</code> — tells browsers, screen readers, and search engines the content language.</li>
        <li><code>dir="rtl"</code> — flips all layout (text, flexbox, margins) to right-to-left.</li>
        <li><code>h-full</code> + <code>min-h-full flex flex-col</code> — sticky footer pattern.</li>
        <li><code>flex-1</code> on <code>&lt;main&gt;</code> — pushes content to fill available space.</li>
        <li><code>&lt;Navbar /&gt;</code> — rendered once, appears on every page.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="rtl">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> RTL — How dir="rtl" Changes Everything</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>CSS Property</th><th>LTR Behavior</th><th>RTL Behavior</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Text alignment</td><td>Left</td><td>Right</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>margin-left</code></td><td>Left side</td><td><strong>Mirrored</strong></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>padding-inline-start</code></td><td>Left padding</td><td><strong>Right padding</strong></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Flexbox row</td><td>Left → Right</td><td><strong>Right → Left</strong></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Scroll bar</td><td>Right side</td><td><strong>Left side</strong></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>The magic:</strong> Tailwind's logical utilities (<code>ms-*</code>, <code>me-*</code>, <code>ps-*</code>, <code>pe-*</code>) auto-mirror. Physical utilities (<code>ml-*</code>, <code>mr-*</code>) do not.</p>
      <pre><code>// ❌ Breaks in RTL
&lt;div className="ml-4 mr-2"&gt;

// ✅ Mirrors automatically
&lt;div className="ms-4 me-2"&gt;</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="navbar">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> Navbar Component</h2>
      <pre><code>import Link from "next/link";

const navLinks = [
  { href: "/", label: "الرئيسية" },
  { href: "/menu", label: "القائمة" },
  { href: "/reserve", label: "احجز طاولة" },
] as const;

export function Navbar() {
  return (
    &lt;header className="sticky top-0 z-50 bg-background/85 backdrop-blur-md border-b border-border"&gt;
      &lt;nav className="max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 h-16 flex items-center justify-between"&gt;
        &lt;Link href="/" className="text-2xl font-bold text-accent hover:text-accent-dark transition-colors"&gt;
          Lumière
        &lt;/Link&gt;
        &lt;ul className="flex items-center gap-6"&gt;
          {navLinks.map((link) =&gt; (
            &lt;li key={link.href}&gt;
              &lt;Link href={link.href} className="text-foreground/80 hover:text-accent transition-colors text-sm font-medium"&gt;
                {link.label}
              &lt;/Link&gt;
            &lt;/li&gt;
          ))}
        &lt;/ul&gt;
      &lt;/nav&gt;
    &lt;/header&gt;
  );
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Server Component:</strong> No state, no events. Ships zero JavaScript.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="navbar-sticky">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> Navbar Deep-Dive — Sticky &amp; Backdrop Blur</h2>
      <h3>sticky top-0 z-50</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>sticky</code> — element scrolls with page, then sticks at <code>top: 0</code>.</li>
        <li><code>z-50</code> — stacks above page content (Tailwind scale 0–50).</li>
        <li><strong>WHY:</strong> Modern UX expects persistent navigation; users reach any page in one click.</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>bg-background/85 backdrop-blur-md</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>bg-background/85</code> — 85% opacity background.</li>
        <li><code>backdrop-blur-md</code> — Gaussian blur of content behind the header.</li>
        <li><strong>WHY:</strong> Content scrolls under the header but stays partially visible — a premium iOS/macOS aesthetic.</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>max-w-6xl mx-auto</h3>
      <p>Constrains content to 1152px and centers it. <strong>WHY:</strong> Prevents stretched text on ultra-wide monitors.</p>
      <h3>as const on navLinks</h3>
      <p>Freezes the array literal — TypeScript narrows string types. <strong>WHY:</strong> Typos in <code>href</code> become compile errors.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="card">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> MenuItemCard — Full File</h2>

    <section id="card-tricks">
      <h2><span class="num">14</span> Card Deep-Dive — Key Techniques</h2>
      <h3>group + group-hover:</h3>
      <p>Parent gets <code>group</code> class; children react to <code>group-hover:*</code>. <strong>WHY:</strong> Hover on any part of the card animates all children (image zoom, text color, border).</p>

      <h3>aspect-4/3</h3>
      <p>New Tailwind v4 syntax for <code>aspect-ratio: 4 / 3</code>. Replaces <code>aspect-[4/3]</code>. <strong>WHY:</strong> Uniform image heights keep grid rows aligned.</p>

      <h3>fill on &lt;Image&gt;</h3>
      <p>Image fills its parent container absolutely. Requires parent with <code>position: relative</code> + fixed dimensions. <strong>WHY:</strong> Enables <code>object-cover</code> (crop to fit) instead of distortion.</p>

      <h3>sizes="(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 33vw"</h3>
      <p>Tells Next.js how wide the image renders. <strong>WHY:</strong> Generates optimal <code>srcset</code> — mobile downloads smaller images.</p>

      <h3>line-clamp-2</h3>
      <p>Truncates text after 2 lines with ellipsis. <strong>WHY:</strong> Prevents variable-length descriptions from breaking grid uniformity.</p>

      <h3>mt-auto</h3>
      <p>Pushes price to card bottom. <strong>WHY:</strong> Cards with short descriptions still align prices at the bottom.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="menu-page">
      <h2><span class="num">15</span> Menu Page — Full File</h2>
      <pre><code>import { prisma } from "@/lib/prisma";
import { MenuItemCard } from "@/components/menu/MenuItemCard";
import { CategoryFilter } from "@/components/menu/CategoryFilter";

type MenuPageProps = {
  searchParams: Promise&lt;{ category?: string }&gt;;
};

export default async function MenuPage({ searchParams }: MenuPageProps) {
  const { category } = await searchParams;

  const [categories, items] = await Promise.all([
    prisma.category.findMany({
      orderBy: { displayOrder: "asc" },
      select: { id: true, name: true, slug: true },
    }),
    prisma.menuItem.findMany({
      where: {
        isAvailable: true,
        ...(category &amp;&amp; { category: { slug: category } }),
      },
      orderBy: [{ isFeatured: "desc" }, { name: "asc" }],
      include: { category: { select: { name: true, slug: true } } },
    }),
  ]);

  return (
    &lt;div className="max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 py-12"&gt;
      &lt;div className="text-center mb-12"&gt;
        &lt;span className="text-accent text-sm font-medium tracking-widest"&gt;OUR MENU&lt;/span&gt;
        &lt;h1 className="text-4xl md:text-5xl font-bold mt-3 mb-4"&gt;قائمة Lumière&lt;/h1&gt;
        &lt;p className="text-muted max-w-xl mx-auto"&gt;
          مجموعة مختارة بعناية من أشهى الأطباق، مُعدّة بأجود المكونات
        &lt;/p&gt;
      &lt;/div&gt;

      &lt;CategoryFilter categories={categories} /&gt;

      {items.length === 0 ? (
        &lt;p className="text-center text-muted py-16"&gt;
          لا توجد أطباق في هذا التصنيف حالياً.
        &lt;/p&gt;
      ) : (
        &lt;div className="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6"&gt;
          {items.map((item) =&gt; (
            &lt;MenuItemCard key={item.id} item={item} /&gt;
          ))}
        &lt;/div&gt;
      )}
    &lt;/div&gt;
  );
}</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="searchparams">
      <h2><span class="num">16</span> Menu Page Deep-Dive — searchParams &amp; Promise.all</h2>
      <h3>searchParams: Promise&lt;{ category?: string }&gt;</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Next.js 15+ passes <code>searchParams</code> as an async value.</li>
        <li>Must <code>await</code> before destructuring.</li>
        <li><strong>WHY this change:</strong> Enables streaming — the page shell renders before params resolve.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>Promise.all([...])</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Fires both Prisma queries concurrently.</li>
        <li>Total latency = <code>max(query1, query2)</code> instead of <code>query1 + query2</code>.</li>
        <li><strong>WHY:</strong> SQLite handles concurrent reads; no reason to serialize.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>Conditional spread</h3>
      <pre><code>...(category &amp;&amp; { category: { slug: category } })</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li>If <code>category</code> exists → adds filter.</li>
        <li>If undefined → spreads <code>false</code>, which Prisma ignores.</li>
        <li><strong>WHY:</strong> One query handles both "all items" and "filtered items" without branching.</li>
      </ul>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Zero-JS verification</strong>
        Open DevTools → Network. The <code>/menu</code> request returns <code>Content-Type: text/html</code>. No <code>fetch('/api/menu/items')</code> call exists. This is the Server Component advantage in action.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="filter">
      <h2><span class="num">17</span> CategoryFilter — Client Component</h2>
      <pre><code>"use client";

import { useRouter, useSearchParams, usePathname } from "next/navigation";

type Category = { id: string; name: string; slug: string };

export function CategoryFilter({ categories }: { categories: Category[] }) {
  const router = useRouter();
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
  const activeSlug = searchParams.get("category");

  function handleFilter(slug: string | null) {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString());
    if (slug) {
      params.set("category", slug);
    } else {
      params.delete("category");
    }
    router.push(`${pathname}?${params.toString()}`);
  }

  return (
    &lt;div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-2 mb-10"&gt;
      &lt;FilterButton label="الكل" isActive={!activeSlug} onClick={() =&gt; handleFilter(null)} /&gt;
      {categories.map((cat) =&gt; (
        &lt;FilterButton key={cat.id} label={cat.name}
          isActive={activeSlug === cat.slug}
          onClick={() =&gt; handleFilter(cat.slug)} /&gt;
      ))}
    &lt;/div&gt;
  );
}

function FilterButton({ label, isActive, onClick }: { label: string; isActive: boolean; onClick: () =&gt; void }) {
  return (
    &lt;button type="button" onClick={onClick}
      className={`px-5 py-2 rounded-full text-sm font-medium border transition-all ${
        isActive
          ? "bg-accent text-white border-accent shadow-sm"
          : "bg-card text-foreground border-border hover:border-accent hover:text-accent"
      }`}&gt;
      {label}
    &lt;/button&gt;
  );
}</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="url-state">
      <h2><span class="num">18</span> Filter Deep-Dive — URL-Driven State</h2>
      <p><strong>Why URL state beats useState:</strong></p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Aspect</th><th>useState</th><th>URL searchParams</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Shareable link</td><td>❌</td><td>✅ <code>/menu?category=desserts</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Browser back/forward</td><td>❌</td><td>✅ Works</td></tr>
          <tr><td>SEO indexable</td><td>❌</td><td>✅ Crawlable</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Server re-renders</td><td>❌</td><td>✅ Data re-fetched server-side</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>The cycle</h3>
      <div class="flow">
        <div class="flow-step">User clicks "حلويات"</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">router.push("/menu?category=desserts")</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step">Next.js re-renders &lt;MenuPage /&gt; (Server Component)</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">MenuPage reads searchParams.category = "desserts"</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step">Prisma returns only desserts</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step success">HTML streams to browser</div>
      </div>

      <h3>URLSearchParams API</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Standard Web API — works in Node and browser.</li>
        <li>Preserves existing params (<code>?utm_source=...</code>) when adding <code>category</code>.</li>
        <li>Auto-encodes Arabic / special characters.</li>
      </ul>

    <section id="detail">
      <h2><span class="num">19</span> Item Detail Page — /menu/[slug]</h2>

}</code></pre>

    <section id="notfound">
      <h2><span class="num">20</span> notFound() &amp; Custom 404</h2>
      <p><strong>params: Promise&lt;{ slug: string }&gt;</strong> — Next.js 15+ async params. <code>await params</code> before use. <strong>WHY:</strong> Enables parallel rendering of layout + page.</p>

      <p><strong>notFound()</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>Throws <code>NEXT_NOT_FOUND</code> — Next.js catches it and renders the nearest <code>not-found.tsx</code>.</li>
        <li>Automatically sets HTTP status to 404.</li>
        <li><strong>WHY explicit call:</strong> <code>findUnique</code> returns <code>null</code> when not found; without <code>notFound()</code>, the page would try to render <code>item.name</code> on <code>null</code> → runtime crash → 500.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>Custom not-found.tsx</h3>
      <pre><code>import Link from "next/link";

export default function MenuItemNotFound() {
  return (
    &lt;div className="max-w-2xl mx-auto px-4 py-24 text-center"&gt;
      &lt;div className="text-8xl mb-6"&gt;🍽️&lt;/div&gt;
      &lt;h1 className="text-3xl font-bold mb-4"&gt;الطبق غير موجود&lt;/h1&gt;
      &lt;p className="text-muted mb-8"&gt;ربما تم حذف هذا الطبق أو أن الرابط غير صحيح.&lt;/p&gt;
      &lt;Link href="/menu"
        className="inline-block bg-accent hover:bg-accent-dark text-white font-medium px-8 py-3 rounded-full transition-colors"&gt;
        العودة إلى القائمة
      &lt;/Link&gt;
    &lt;/div&gt;
  );
}</code></pre>

      <p><strong>Verified behavior:</strong></p>
      <pre><code>GET /menu/pizza 404 in 189ms
GET /menu/hummus 200 in 1974ms (first build)
GET /menu/aleppo-kebab 200 in 162ms (warm)</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="flow">
      <h2><span class="num">21</span> Request Data Flow</h2>
      <p><strong>Trace of <code>GET /menu?category=desserts</code>:</strong></p>
      <div class="flow">
        <div class="flow-step">1. User navigates to /menu</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">2. Server Component &lt;MenuPage /&gt; executes:<br>await searchParams → { category: undefined }</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">3. Promise.all fires:<br>• prisma.category.findMany() (4 rows)<br>• prisma.menuItem.findMany({ where: { isAvailable: true } })</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step">4. React streams HTML with 12 &lt;MenuItemCard /&gt; + &lt;CategoryFilter /&gt;</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step">5. Filter buttons hydrate — click "حلويات"</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">6. router.push("/menu?category=desserts")</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step">7. Next.js re-runs &lt;MenuPage /&gt; with new searchParams</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step success">8. Streamed HTML replaces previous grid (3 desserts)</div>
      </div>
      <p><strong>Boundary rationale:</strong> Data crosses from SQLite → Prisma → React tree → HTML string → browser DOM. Each step is typed; any shape mismatch fails at compile time.</p>
    </section>

      <ul>
        <li>60%+ of restaurant traffic is mobile.</li>

    <section id="cheatsheet">
      <h2><span class="num">23</span> Server vs Client — Decision Cheat Sheet</h2>
      <p><strong>Ask these questions in order:</strong></p>
      <ol>
        <li>Does the component fetch data from Prisma? → <strong>Server</strong></li>
        <li>Does it use <code>useState</code>, <code>useEffect</code>, <code>useRef</code>? → <strong>Client</strong></li>
        <li>Does it attach event handlers (<code>onClick</code>, <code>onSubmit</code>)? → <strong>Client</strong></li>
        <li>Does it access <code>window</code>, <code>localStorage</code>, <code>document</code>? → <strong>Client</strong></li>
        <li>Otherwise → <strong>Server</strong> (default)</li>
      </ol>

      <h3>Phase 4 breakdown</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Type</th><th>Reason</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Navbar</td><td>Server</td><td>Static links, no state</td></tr>
          <tr><td>MenuItemCard</td><td>Server</td><td>Static presentation</td></tr>
          <tr><td>MenuPage</td><td>Server</td><td>Direct Prisma query</td></tr>
          <tr><td>MenuItemPage</td><td>Server</td><td>Direct Prisma query</td></tr>
          <tr><td>not-found</td><td>Server</td><td>Static content</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>CategoryFilter</strong></td><td><strong>Client</strong></td><td><code>onClick</code> + <code>useRouter</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Ratio:</strong> 5 Server : 1 Client. The Client component ships ~3 KB gzipped.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">25</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>components/</code> inside <code>app/</code></td><td><code>Module not found: @/components/...</code></td><td>Move to <code>src/components/</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Missing <code>"use client"</code></td><td><code>useState is not defined</code></td><td>Add at top of file (first line)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Forgetting <code>await params</code></td><td>Warning: <code>params should be awaited</code></td><td><code>const { slug } = await params</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>dir="rtl"</code> on body only</td><td>Text mirrors but Flexbox doesn't</td><td>Set on <code>&lt;html&gt;</code>, not <code>&lt;body&gt;</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Image 404</td><td><code>next/image</code> refuses remote domains</td><td>Add domain to <code>next.config.ts</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Slow first dev compile</td><td>40+ second initial load</td><td>Expected in dev; production build is &lt;500ms</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Empty grid on filter</td><td>Wrong param name</td><td>Match <code>searchParams.get()</code> exactly</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="glossary">
      <h2><span class="num">26</span> Technical Abbreviations Glossary</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Abbr.</th><th>Full Form</th><th>Plain-English Meaning</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>CSS</td><td>Cascading Style Sheets</td><td>Language for styling web pages</td></tr>
          <tr><td>DOM</td><td>Document Object Model</td><td>In-memory tree of the rendered page</td></tr>

  <main>
    <header class="hero">
      <div class="kicker">Phase 05 · Reservation Engine</div>
      <h1>Smart Table Assignment &amp; Booking Pipeline</h1>
      <p class="lede">Build the flagship feature of the project — an intelligent table assignment engine that selects the optimal table for each booking, backed by server-side validation and atomic persistence. Pure business logic, decoupled from HTTP and the database.</p>
      <div class="stack">
        <span>Pure Function</span><span>Interval Overlap</span>
        <span>Zod Validation</span><span>Server Action</span>
        <span>Discriminated Union</span><span>Fail-Safe Design</span>
      </div>
    </header>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal:</strong> Take a guest's desired date, time, and party size and determine — in milliseconds — which table fits, without conflicting with existing bookings.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li><code>src/lib/services/table-assignment.ts</code> — pure function implementing 4 business rules.</li>
        <li><code>scripts/test-assignment.ts</code> — 5-scenario test harness.</li>
        <li><code>src/components/ui/FormField.tsx</code> — reusable form primitive.</li>
        <li><code>src/components/reservation/ReservationForm.tsx</code> — Client Component with success screen.</li>
        <li><code>src/app/reserve/page.tsx</code> — RTL reservation page.</li>
        <li><code>src/lib/validations/reservation.ts</code> — Zod schema with custom refinements.</li>
        <li><code>src/actions/reservation.ts</code> — Server Action saving reservations transactionally.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="decision">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Architectural Decision — Pure Business Logic Separation</h2>
      <p><strong>The problem:</strong> Where does "which table for this booking" logic belong?</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Location</th><th>Pros</th><th>Cons</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Inside the Server Action</td><td>Fewer files</td><td>Untestable without DB; mixes I/O with logic</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Inside the Prisma model</td><td>Reusable</td><td>Requires ORM to exist</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Separate pure function</strong></td><td>Testable, portable, explainable</td><td>One extra file</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Chosen approach:</strong> Pure function in <code>src/lib/services/table-assignment.ts</code>.</p>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Engineering rationale</strong>
        <ul style="margin-top:0.5rem;margin-bottom:0">
          <li><strong>Testable without a database</strong> — a Node script exercises all rules in milliseconds.</li>
          <li><strong>Portable</strong> — the same function can run in a mobile app, a cron job, or a webhook handler.</li>
          <li><strong>Explainable to clients</strong> — logic is isolated in one file, not scattered across HTTP handlers.</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="rules">
      <h2><span class="num">3</span> The Four Business Rules</h2>
      <p><strong>Input:</strong> <code>(guestsCount, reservationDate, durationMinutes, tablesWithReservations)</code></p>
      <p><strong>Output:</strong> <code>bestTable | null</code></p>
      <div class="rules-grid">
        <div class="rule-card">
          <span class="rule-num">1</span>
          <h4>Capacity Fit</h4>
          <p>Table seats the party, no more than 3 extra seats.</p>
          <code>capacity >= guestsCount &amp;&amp; capacity &lt;= guestsCount + 3</code>
        </div>
        <div class="rule-card">
          <span class="rule-num">2</span>
          <h4>No Time Overlap</h4>
          <p>Existing reservations must not intersect the new window.</p>
          <code>existingStart &lt; newEnd &amp;&amp; existingEnd &gt; newStart</code>
        </div>
        <div class="rule-card">
          <span class="rule-num">3</span>
          <h4>Ranking</h4>
          <p>Smallest capacity first, then fewest existing reservations.</p>
          <code>sort by capacity, then reservations.length</code>
        </div>
        <div class="rule-card">
          <span class="rule-num">4</span>
          <h4>Active Only</h4>
          <p>Only tables flagged as active are considered.</p>
          <code>isActive === true</code>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Why "no more than 3 extra seats"</strong>
        A party of 2 should not occupy a 10-seat table. The buffer of 3 balances flexibility (small parties can use medium tables) against revenue loss (blocking a large table for a small party).
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="overlap">
      <h2><span class="num">4</span> Interval Overlap Logic — The Math</h2>
      <p><strong>The formula:</strong></p>
      <pre><code>Overlap = (existingStart &lt; newEnd) AND (existingEnd &gt; newStart)</code></pre>

      <p><strong>Truth table for a new booking 8:00 → 9:30:</strong></p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Existing Booking</th><th>existingStart &lt; 9:30</th><th>existingEnd &gt; 8:00</th><th>Overlap?</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>6:00 → 7:30</td><td>✅</td><td>❌</td><td><strong>No</strong></td></tr>
          <tr><td>6:00 → 8:30</td><td>✅</td><td>✅</td><td><strong>Yes</strong></td></tr>
          <tr><td>7:00 → 10:00</td><td>✅</td><td>✅</td><td><strong>Yes</strong></td></tr>
          <tr><td>8:00 → 9:30</td><td>✅</td><td>✅</td><td><strong>Yes</strong></td></tr>
          <tr><td>8:15 → 10:00</td><td>✅</td><td>✅</td><td><strong>Yes</strong></td></tr>
          <tr><td>9:30 → 11:00</td><td>❌</td><td>✅</td><td><strong>No</strong></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>Visual Timeline</h3>
      <div class="timeline">
        <div class="timeline-row">
          <div class="timeline-label">Existing</div>
          <div class="timeline-track"><div class="timeline-block existing" style="left:5%;width:35%">7:30 – 9:00</div></div>
        </div>
        <div class="timeline-row">
          <div class="timeline-label">New (overlap)</div>
          <div class="timeline-track"><div class="timeline-block overlap" style="left:20%;width:35%">8:00 – 9:30</div></div>
        </div>
        <div class="timeline-row">
          <div class="timeline-label">New (OK)</div>
          <div class="timeline-track"><div class="timeline-block ok" style="left:60%;width:30%">9:00 – 10:30</div></div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <p style="font-size:0.82rem;color:var(--fg-muted);">The bottom row starts exactly when the top row ends — <strong>touching, no overlap</strong>. This is a critical edge case (see next section).</p>
    </section>

    <section id="touch">
      <h2><span class="num">5</span> Touching Bookings Decision</h2>
      <p><strong>The edge case:</strong> existing booking ends at 8:00, new booking starts at 8:00.</p>
      <pre><code>existingEnd (8:00) &gt; newStart (8:00)  →  false  →  no overlap ✅</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why <code>&gt;</code> not <code>&gt;=</code>:</strong> Touching bookings are allowed. This is a <strong>business decision</strong> — the guest leaves, the next guest sits. No gap required.</p>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Future enhancement (Phase 10)</strong>
        A 15-minute cleaning buffer can be added by changing the formula to <code>existingEnd + 15min &gt; newStart</code>. Deferred to Polish phase.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="commands">
      <h2><span class="num">6</span> Complete Commands Table</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Command</th><th>Purpose</th></tr></thead>

    <section id="architecture">
      <h2><span class="num">8</span> Three-Layer Architecture</h2>
      <div class="layers">
        <div class="layer client"><strong>CLIENT</strong> · ReservationForm.tsx — collects input, calls Server Action</div>
        <div class="layer action"><strong>ACTION</strong> · actions/reservation.ts — validates, orchestrates, persists</div>
        <div class="layer pure"><strong>PURE LOGIC</strong> · lib/services/table-assignment.ts — decides which table</div>
        <div class="layer data"><strong>DATA</strong> · Prisma + SQLite — stores the reservation</div>
      </div>
      <p><strong>Boundary rules:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>Client cannot call pure logic or Prisma directly.</li>
        <li>Server Action orchestrates but delegates the decision to the pure function.</li>
        <li>Pure function has no knowledge of HTTP, DB, or React.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="pseudocode">
      <h2><span class="num">9</span> Design in Pseudo-code</h2>
      <p><strong>Before writing TypeScript, the algorithm in plain prose:</strong></p>
      <pre><code>find_best_table(guestsCount, reservationDate, durationMinutes, tables):

  1. Compute newStart = reservationDate.timestamp
     Compute newEnd = newStart + durationMinutes * 60_000

  2. Filter tables where:
       - isActive == true
       - capacity >= guestsCount
       - capacity <= guestsCount + 3
       - No reservation overlaps [newStart, newEnd]

  3. If empty list → return null

  4. Sort candidates by:
       - capacity ascending (smallest first)
       - reservations.length ascending (least booked first)

  5. Return candidates[0]</code></pre>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Why pseudo-code first</strong>
        Catches logical gaps (e.g., "what if two tables tie?") before touching TypeScript. Saves rewrite cycles.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="types">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> Types &amp; Constants</h2>
      <pre><code>export const DEFAULT_DURATION_MINUTES = 90;
export const CAPACITY_BUFFER = 3;

export type TableWithReservations = {
  id: string;
  number: number;
  capacity: number;
  location: string | null;
  isActive: boolean;
  reservations: {
    reservationDate: Date;
    durationMinutes: number;
  }[];
};

export type AssignmentRequest = {
  guestsCount: number;
  reservationDate: Date;
  durationMinutes?: number;
};</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><code>DEFAULT_DURATION_MINUTES = 90</code> — industry-standard dining duration; used when callers omit it.</li>
        <li><code>CAPACITY_BUFFER = 3</code> — business rule extracted as a named constant (no magic numbers).</li>
        <li><code>TableWithReservations</code> — <strong>narrow shape</strong> the function needs, not the full Prisma model.</li>
        <li><code>durationMinutes</code> optional — callers may override the default.</li>
      </ul>
      <p><strong>Why define our own types instead of importing Prisma types:</strong> The function must run in contexts without Prisma (tests, future mobile app). Narrow input types keep it portable.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="fn">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> findBestTable Function</h2>
      <pre><code>export function findBestTable(
  tables: TableWithReservations[],
  request: AssignmentRequest
): TableWithReservations | null {
  const duration = request.durationMinutes ?? DEFAULT_DURATION_MINUTES;

  const newStart = request.reservationDate.getTime();
  const newEnd = newStart + duration * 60_000;

  const candidates = tables
    .filter((table) =&gt; table.isActive)
    .filter(
      (table) =&gt;
        table.capacity &gt;= request.guestsCount &amp;&amp;
        table.capacity &lt;= request.guestsCount + CAPACITY_BUFFER
    )
    .filter((table) =&gt; !hasOverlappingReservation(table, newStart, newEnd));

  if (candidates.length === 0) return null;

  candidates.sort((a, b) =&gt; {
    if (a.capacity !== b.capacity) return a.capacity - b.capacity;
    return a.reservations.length - b.reservations.length;
  });

  return candidates[0];
}</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="fn-deep">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> Function Deep-Dive</h2>
      <h3>request.durationMinutes ?? DEFAULT_DURATION_MINUTES</h3>
      <p><code>??</code> (nullish coalescing) — falls back only if <code>undefined</code> or <code>null</code>. <strong>Why not <code>||</code>:</strong> <code>||</code> would also replace <code>0</code>, but a 0-minute reservation is invalid and should error upstream, not silently default.</p>

      <h3>getTime() for timestamp math</h3>
      <p>Returns milliseconds since Unix epoch (a <code>number</code>). <strong>Why numbers not Date objects:</strong> Numeric comparisons are faster; no timezone re-parsing; no accidental mutation.</p>

      <h3>60_000 instead of 60000</h3>
      <p>Underscore separator — pure readability, zero runtime effect.</p>

      <h3>Chained .filter() calls</h3>
      <p>Each filter is a single concern: active → capacity → overlap. <strong>Why not one giant filter:</strong> Chaining reads top-to-bottom like English; single <code>&amp;&amp;</code> chains lose clarity.</p>

      <h3>Sort comparator</h3>
      <pre><code>if (a.capacity !== b.capacity) return a.capacity - b.capacity;
return a.reservations.length - b.reservations.length;</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li>Primary sort: capacity ascending.</li>
        <li>Tiebreaker: fewest existing reservations (load balancing).</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="overlap-fn">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> hasOverlappingReservation</h2>
      <pre><code>function hasOverlappingReservation(
  table: TableWithReservations,
  newStart: number,
  newEnd: number
): boolean {
  return table.reservations.some((reservation) =&gt; {
    const existingStart = reservation.reservationDate.getTime();
    const existingEnd = existingStart + reservation.durationMinutes * 60_000;
    return existingStart &lt; newEnd &amp;&amp; existingEnd &gt; newStart;
  });
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why <code>.some()</code> instead of <code>.filter().length &gt; 0</code>:</strong> <code>.some()</code> short-circuits on the first match — returns immediately. <code>.filter()</code> scans all elements even after finding one.</p>
      <p><strong>Why this is a separate function:</strong> Single responsibility — overlap logic isolated from filtering. Reusable if other code paths (e.g., cancel-reservation check) need it.</p>
    </section>

  "w-full px-4 py-2.5 rounded-lg border border-border bg-background text-foreground focus:outline-none focus:border-accent focus:ring-2 focus:ring-accent/20 transition-all";

export function FormField({
  label,

    <section id="form">
      <h2><span class="num">17</span> ReservationForm — Client Component</h2>
      <pre><code>"use client";

import { useState, type ChangeEvent, type FormEvent } from "react";
import { FormField, inputClasses } from "@/components/ui/FormField";
import { createReservation, type CreateReservationResult } from "@/actions/reservation";

const TIME_SLOTS = Array.from({ length: 21 }, (_, i) =&gt; {
  const totalMinutes = 12 * 60 + i * 30;
  const hours = Math.floor(totalMinutes / 60);
  const minutes = totalMinutes % 60;
  const value = `${String(hours).padStart(2, "0")}:${String(minutes).padStart(2, "0")}`;
  return { value, label: value };
});

const TODAY = new Date().toISOString().split("T")[0];

type Result =
  | { kind: "idle" }
  | { kind: "submitting" }
  | { kind: "success"; tableNumber: number; reservationId: string }
  | { kind: "error"; message: string; fieldErrors?: Record&lt;string, string[]&gt; };

export function ReservationForm() {
  const [formData, setFormData] = useState({
    guestName: "", guestEmail: "", guestPhone: "",
    guestsCount: 2, date: TODAY, time: "20:00", notes: "",
  });

  const [result, setResult] = useState&lt;Result&gt;({ kind: "idle" });

  function handleChange(e: ChangeEvent&lt;HTMLInputElement | HTMLSelectElement | HTMLTextAreaElement&gt;) {
    const { name, value } = e.target;
    setFormData((prev) =&gt; ({ ...prev, [name]: value }));
  }

  async function handleSubmit(e: FormEvent) {
    e.preventDefault();
    setResult({ kind: "submitting" });
    const response: CreateReservationResult = await createReservation(formData);

    if (response.success) {
      setResult({ kind: "success", tableNumber: response.tableNumber, reservationId: response.reservationId });
      return;
    }
    setResult({ kind: "error", message: response.error, fieldErrors: response.fieldErrors });
  }

  if (result.kind === "success") {
    return (
      &lt;div className="bg-card border border-border rounded-2xl p-8 md:p-12 text-center shadow-sm"&gt;
        &lt;div className="text-6xl mb-4"&gt;✅&lt;/div&gt;
        &lt;h2 className="text-2xl font-bold mb-3"&gt;تم استلام حجزك!&lt;/h2&gt;
        &lt;p className="text-muted mb-6"&gt;
          تم تخصيص &lt;span className="text-accent font-bold"&gt;طاولة رقم {result.tableNumber}&lt;/span&gt; لك.
        &lt;/p&gt;
        &lt;a href="/menu" className="inline-block bg-accent hover:bg-accent-dark text-white font-medium px-8 py-3 rounded-full transition-colors"&gt;
          تصفح القائمة
        &lt;/a&gt;
      &lt;/div&gt;
    );
  }

  return ( /* form JSX */ );
}</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="form-state">
      <h2><span class="num">18</span> Result State Pattern — Discriminated Union</h2>
      <pre><code>type Result =
  | { kind: "idle" }
  | { kind: "submitting" }
  | { kind: "success"; tableNumber: number; reservationId: string }
  | { kind: "error"; message: string; fieldErrors?: Record&lt;string, string[]&gt; };</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why a discriminated union:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li><strong>Impossible states are unrepresentable</strong> — you cannot have <code>success</code> without a <code>tableNumber</code>.</li>
        <li>TypeScript narrows the type inside <code>if (result.kind === "success")</code>.</li>
        <li>Prevents <code>result.message</code> access when the state is <code>success</code>.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>TIME_SLOTS generation</h3>
      <p>21 slots from 12:00 to 22:00 every 30 minutes. <code>String(h).padStart(2, "0")</code> → <code>"09"</code> not <code>"9"</code> — matches HTML <code>&lt;input type="time"&gt;</code> format. <strong>Why not a native time picker:</strong> Native time pickers differ per browser; a curated <code>&lt;select&gt;</code> enforces business hours visually.</p>

      <h3>handleChange name-based pattern</h3>
      <pre><code>const { name, value } = e.target;
setFormData((prev) =&gt; ({ ...prev, [name]: value }));</code></pre>
      <p>One handler for 7 fields. Adding a new field requires zero handler changes — just <code>name="..."</code> on the input.</p>
    </section>
