    <section id="zod">
      <h2><span class="num">20</span> Zod Schema — reservation.ts</h2>
      <pre><code>import { z } from "zod";
import { DEFAULT_DURATION_MINUTES } from "@/lib/services/table-assignment";

export const reservationSchema = z.object({
  guestName: z.string().trim()
    .min(2, "الاسم قصير جداً (حرفان على الأقل)")
    .max(80, "الاسم طويل جداً (80 حرفاً كحد أقصى)"),

  guestEmail: z.string().trim().toLowerCase()
    .email("البريد الإلكتروني غير صحيح"),

  guestPhone: z.string().trim()
    .min(8, "رقم الهاتف قصير جداً")
    .max(20, "رقم الهاتف طويل جداً")
    .regex(/^[+\d\s\-()]+$/, "رقم الهاتف يحتوي على رموز غير مسموحة"),

  guestsCount: z.coerce.number().int("عدد الأشخاص يجب أن يكون رقماً صحيحاً")
    .min(1, "على الأقل شخص واحد")
    .max(10, "لا يمكن الحجز لأكثر من 10 أشخاص"),

  date: z.string().regex(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/, "التاريخ غير صحيح"),
  time: z.string().regex(/^\d{2}:\d{2}$/, "الوقت غير صحيح"),

  notes: z.string().trim()
    .max(500, "الملاحظات طويلة جداً (500 حرف كحد أقصى)")
    .optional().or(z.literal("")),
})</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why <code>z.coerce.number()</code> for guestsCount:</strong> HTML forms submit all values as strings, even <code>&lt;select&gt;</code> numbers. <code>coerce</code> runs <code>Number(value)</code> before validation.</p>
      <p><strong>Why Arabic error messages:</strong> Zod errors surface directly to the user — no translation layer needed. One source of truth for validation messages.</p>
      <p><strong>Why <code>.trim()</code> first:</strong> <code>"  أحمد  "</code> becomes <code>"أحمد"</code> before length check. Prevents bypass via whitespace padding.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="refinements">
      <h2><span class="num">21</span> Custom Refinements — Business Logic in Zod</h2>
      <pre><code>.refine(
  (data) =&gt; {
    const dt = new Date(`${data.date}T${data.time}:00`);
    return dt.getTime() &gt; Date.now();
  },
  { message: "لا يمكن الحجز في وقت ماضٍ", path: ["date"] }
)
.refine(
  (data) =&gt; {
    const dt = new Date(`${data.date}T${data.time}:00`);
    const hours = dt.getHours();
    return hours &gt;= 12 &amp;&amp; hours &lt;= 22;
  },
  { message: "الحجز متاح فقط بين 12:00 ظهراً و 10:00 مساءً", path: ["time"] }
)</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why <code>.refine()</code> twice at the end:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>Refinements run <strong>after</strong> all field validations pass.</li>
        <li>Combines <code>date</code> + <code>time</code> into one check (cross-field validation).</li>
        <li><code>path: ["date"]</code> routes the error to the date field's error array.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>The power of .refine()</strong>
        Zod is not just a type checker — it can enforce full business rules. These two refinements encode: "no bookings in the past" and "operating hours 12:00–22:00".
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="validation-tests">
      <h2><span class="num">22</span> Validation Tests — 7 Scenarios</h2>
      <pre><code>✅ بيانات صحيحة تماماً
   ✓ نجح التحقق

✅ بريد إلكتروني غير صحيح
   ✗ [guestEmail] البريد الإلكتروني غير صحيح

✅ اسم قصير جداً (حرف واحد)
   ✗ [guestName] الاسم قصير جداً (حرفان على الأقل)

✅ عدد أشخاص = 15 (أكثر من الحد)
   ✗ [guestsCount] لا يمكن الحجز لأكثر من 10 أشخاص

✅ تاريخ في الماضي
   ✗ [date] لا يمكن الحجز في وقت ماضٍ

✅ وقت الحجز 03:00 صباحاً (خارج ساعات العمل)
   ✗ [time] الحجز متاح فقط بين 12:00 ظهراً و 10:00 مساءً

✅ ملاحظات فارغة (حقل اختياري)
   ✓ نجح التحقق</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Note:</strong> <code>✅</code> in this output means "test behaved as expected" — not "data passed". Both valid and invalid inputs return <code>✅</code> when they produce the expected verdict.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="action">
      <h2><span class="num">23</span> createReservation — Server Action</h2>
      <pre><code>"use server";

import { prisma } from "@/lib/prisma";
import { reservationSchema, parseReservationDate } from "@/lib/validations/reservation";
import { findBestTable, DEFAULT_DURATION_MINUTES } from "@/lib/services/table-assignment";

export type CreateReservationResult =
  | { success: true; reservationId: string; tableNumber: number }
  | { success: false; error: string; fieldErrors?: Record&lt;string, string[]&gt; };

export async function createReservation(
  input: unknown
): Promise&lt;CreateReservationResult&gt; {
  const parsed = reservationSchema.safeParse(input);

  if (!parsed.success) {
    const fieldErrors: Record&lt;string, string[]&gt; = {};
    for (const issue of parsed.error.issues) {
      const key = issue.path.join(".") || "_";
      (fieldErrors[key] ??= []).push(issue.message);
    }
    return { success: false, error: "تحقق من البيانات المُدخلة", fieldErrors };
  }

  const data = parsed.data;
  const reservationDate = parseReservationDate(data.date, data.time);
  const duration = DEFAULT_DURATION_MINUTES;

  try {
    const bufferMs = 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
    const windowStart = new Date(reservationDate.getTime() - bufferMs);
    const windowEnd = new Date(reservationDate.getTime() + duration * 60_000 + bufferMs);

    const tables = await prisma.table.findMany({
      where: {
        isActive: true,
        capacity: { gte: data.guestsCount, lte: data.guestsCount + 3 },
      },
      include: {
        reservations: {
          where: {
            status: { in: ["PENDING", "CONFIRMED"] },
            reservationDate: { gte: windowStart, lte: windowEnd },
          },
          select: { reservationDate: true, durationMinutes: true },
        },
      },
    });

    const bestTable = findBestTable(tables, {
      guestsCount: data.guestsCount,
      reservationDate,
      durationMinutes: duration,
    });

    if (!bestTable) {
      return {
        success: false,
        error: "لا توجد طاولة متاحة في هذا الوقت. جرّب وقتاً آخر أو تواصل معنا هاتفياً.",
      };
    }

    const reservation = await prisma.reservation.create({
      data: {
        guestName: data.guestName,
        guestEmail: data.guestEmail,
        guestPhone: data.guestPhone,
        guestsCount: data.guestsCount,
        reservationDate,
        durationMinutes: duration,
        status: "PENDING",
        notes: data.notes &amp;&amp; data.notes !== "" ? data.notes : null,
        tableId: bestTable.id,
      },
    });

    return { success: true, reservationId: reservation.id, tableNumber: bestTable.number };
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[createReservation] error:", error);
    return { success: false, error: "حدث خطأ غير متوقع أثناء الحجز. يرجى المحاولة لاحقاً." };
  }
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why <code>"use server"</code> at the top:</strong> Marks the file as a Server Action module. All exports become RPC endpoints callable from Client Components. <strong>Not</strong> a Route Handler — no URL, no HTTP method.</p>
      <p><strong>Why <code>input: unknown</code> not <code>input: ReservationInput</code>:</strong> A malicious client can send anything. <code>unknown</code> forces explicit runtime validation before type-narrowing.</p>
      <p><strong><code>(fieldErrors[key] ??= []).push(...)</code>:</strong> <code>??=</code> initializes the array on first key occurrence. Multiple Zod issues may target the same field; we accumulate rather than overwrite.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="query-window">
      <h2><span class="num">24</span> Query Window Optimization — ±3 Hours</h2>
      <pre><code>const bufferMs = 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
const windowStart = new Date(reservationDate.getTime() - bufferMs);
const windowEnd = new Date(
  reservationDate.getTime() + duration * 60_000 + bufferMs
);</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why not fetch all reservations:</strong> After months of operation, tables accumulate hundreds of historical rows. Loading them all on every booking is wasteful.</p>
      <p><strong>Why ±3 hours:</strong> Longest realistic reservation is 3 hours. Any existing booking outside this window cannot overlap.</p>
      <p><strong>Effect:</strong> Query time stays O(recent rows) instead of O(all rows).</p>

      <h3>Pre-filtering capacity in SQL</h3>
      <pre><code>capacity: { gte: data.guestsCount, lte: data.guestsCount + 3 }</code></pre>
      <p>Same condition as the pure function, but applied at the database layer. <strong>Why duplicate the rule in two places:</strong> The DB filter reduces rows returned; the pure function filter is the authoritative check. Duplication is intentional for performance.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="status-filter">
      <h2><span class="num">25</span> Status-Aware Filtering</h2>
      <pre><code>status: { in: ["PENDING", "CONFIRMED"] }</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><code>CANCELLED</code> reservations free the table — don't count them.</li>
        <li><code>COMPLETED</code> reservations are historical — don't count them.</li>
        <li><strong>Business logic encoded in the query, not in post-processing.</strong></li>
      </ul>

      <h3>Notes field normalization</h3>
      <pre><code>notes: data.notes &amp;&amp; data.notes !== "" ? data.notes : null</code></pre>
      <p>Zod returns <code>""</code> for empty optional strings. Prisma expects <code>null</code> for empty nullable columns. <strong>Prevents storing empty strings in the database</strong> — makes "has notes" queries simpler.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="flow">
      <h2><span class="num">26</span> Full Data Flow — Walkthrough</h2>
      <div class="flow">
        <div class="flow-step">1. User clicks "تأكيد الحجز"</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step">2. ReservationForm.handleSubmit fires</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">3. setResult({ kind: "submitting" }) — button disabled</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">4. createReservation(formData) invoked as RPC</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-label">─── SERVER BOUNDARY ───</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">5. reservationSchema.safeParse(input)<br>Fail → return fieldErrors · Pass → continue</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">6. prisma.table.findMany({ window, capacity, status filters })</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">7. findBestTable(tables, request) → Table | null<br>null → "no table available" · Table → continue</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">8. prisma.reservation.create({ ...data, tableId })</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step success">9. Return { success: true, reservationId, tableNumber }</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-label">─── CLIENT BOUNDARY ───</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step success">10. Success screen replaces form</div>
      </div>
      <p><strong>Boundary rationale:</strong> Every transition is either Zod-validated (client → server) or TypeScript-typed (server internals). No unvalidated data reaches the database.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">28</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Missing <code>"use server"</code></td><td><code>Server Actions must be async functions</code></td><td>Add at top of <code>actions/*.ts</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Missing <code>await params</code></td><td>Warning: <code>params should be awaited</code></td><td><code>const { slug } = await params</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Zod schema trusts input</td><td>TypeScript error on <code>.data</code></td><td>Use <code>safeParse</code>, not <code>parse</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Overlap <code>&lt;</code> vs <code>&lt;=</code></td><td>Touching bookings rejected</td><td>Use strict <code>&lt;</code> / <code>&gt;</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Unfiltered status query</td><td>Cancelled bookings block tables</td><td><code>status: { in: ["PENDING", "CONFIRMED"] }</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Prisma query all rows</td><td>Slow after months</td><td>Add <code>±3h</code> window filter</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>notes: ""</code> stored</td><td>Empty strings in DB</td><td>Convert <code>""</code> → <code>null</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Success without table number</td><td>Poor UX</td><td>Return <code>tableNumber</code> from action</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

          <tr><td>JSON</td><td>JavaScript Object Notation</td><td>Text format for structured data</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ORM</td><td>Object-Relational Mapper</td><td>Translates objects ↔ SQL</td></tr>

        <li><strong>Dedicated demo account</strong> with warning banner and safe reset philosophy.</li>

        <li><strong>11 curated screenshots</strong> across public, admin, and documentation.</li>
        <li><strong>Google Maps</strong> location section + <strong>Add-to-Calendar</strong> button in confirmation emails.</li>

    <section id="part1-og">
      <h2><span class="num">5</span> Part 1 · Dynamic OG Image</h2>
      <p>Generated at build time via <code>ImageResponse</code> from <code>next/og</code> — no design tool, no image file, pure code.</p>

      <h3>File: src/app/opengraph-image.tsx</h3>
      <pre><code>import { ImageResponse } from "next/og";

export const size = { width: 1200, height: 630 };
export const contentType = "image/png";
export const dynamic = "force-static";

export default async function OpengraphImage() {
  return new ImageResponse(
    (
      &lt;div style={{ /* ... */ }}&gt;
        &lt;div&gt;WELCOME TO&lt;/div&gt;
        &lt;div&gt;Lumière&lt;/div&gt;
        &lt;div&gt;Fine Dining · Reservation System&lt;/div&gt;
      &lt;/div&gt;
    ),
    { ...size }
  );
}</code></pre>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Zero-config integration</strong>
        Placing this file in <code>app/</code> automatically injects <code>&lt;meta property="og:image"&gt;</code> and <code>&lt;meta name="twitter:image"&gt;</code> into every page's <code>&lt;head&gt;</code>.
      </div>

    </section>

    <section id="part1-ci">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> Part 1 · GitHub Actions CI</h2>
      <p>Every <code>git push</code> triggers an automated check — TypeScript validation + production build — before Vercel even starts deploying.</p>

      <h3>Final Working Workflow</h3>
      <pre><code>name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  build:
    name: Type Check &amp; Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: "20"
          cache: "npm"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Generate Prisma Client
        run: npx prisma generate
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: "postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db"

      - name: TypeScript type check
        run: npx tsc --noEmit

      - name: Build for production
        run: npm run build
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: "postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db"
          DIRECT_URL: "postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db"
          AUTH_SECRET: "ci-test-secret-not-used-in-production-000000000000000000000"
          EMAIL_PROVIDER: "console"</code></pre>

      <h3>CI Badge in README</h3>
      <pre><code>[![CI](https://github.com/myhifi/lumiere-nextjs-fullstack/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](...)</code></pre>

      <div class="shot-gallery">
        <figure class="shot-card">
          <img src="../screenshots/docs/15-ci-success.jpg" alt="GitHub Actions CI passing" loading="lazy" />
          <figcaption>GitHub Actions — CI passing ✅</figcaption>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="ci-errors">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> The CI Errors Journey</h2>
      <p>Five iterations were needed to make the CI workflow green. Each error revealed a distinct platform quirk.</p>

      <div class="error-journey">
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 1: npm ci runs postinstall</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Process completed with exit code 1 · during Install dependencies</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Add <code>--ignore-scripts</code> to <code>npm ci</code> — defer <code>prisma generate</code> to its own step.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 2: Missing DATABASE_URL for prisma generate</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">PrismaConfigEnvError: Missing required environment variable: DATABASE_URL</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Pass <code>DATABASE_URL</code> env variable to the <code>prisma generate</code> step.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 3: LayoutProps type not found</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Cannot find name 'LayoutProps'.</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Replace <code>LayoutProps&lt;"/"&gt;</code> with standard <code>{ children: React.ReactNode }</code> — CI has no generated types.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 4: Node.js 20 deprecation warning</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Upgrade <code>actions/checkout@v4</code> → <code>@v5</code> and <code>actions/setup-node@v4</code> → <code>@v5</code>.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 5: Placeholder URL needed</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Add fallback for prisma.config.ts when DATABASE_URL is undefined.</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Update <code>prisma.config.ts</code> to use <code>process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? "postgresql://placeholder"</code>.</div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>All errors resolved · CI is green</strong>
        Every push now validates the entire codebase in ~1 minute.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="part2-images">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> Part 2 · Real Food Images from Unsplash</h2>
      <p>Placeholder emoji <code>🍽️</code> was replaced with real food photography — no downloads, no file uploads.</p>

      <h3>Architecture</h3>
      <div class="flow">
        <div class="flow-step">Unsplash CDN</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-label">direct URL</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">prisma/data/menu-items.ts → imageUrl field</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-label">db:seed</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">Neon PostgreSQL</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-label">Prisma query</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step success">&lt;Image /&gt; → next/image optimization</div>
      </div>

      <h3>next.config.ts Update</h3>
      <pre><code>const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  images: {
    remotePatterns: [
      { protocol: "https", hostname: "images.unsplash.com" },
    ],
  },
};</code></pre>

      <div class="callout info">
        <strong>Why not download images?</strong>
        Zero <code>git</code> repository size increase, and instant loading from a global CDN. For portfolio projects with limited bandwidth, this pattern is optimal.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="part2-shimmer">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> Part 2 · Shimmer Skeleton + Fade-In</h2>
      <p>Instead of empty beige boxes while images load, cards display a subtle golden shimmer. Images fade in gracefully when ready.</p>

      <h3>globals.css Additions</h3>
      <pre><code>@keyframes shimmer {
  0% { background-position: -200% 0; }
  100% { background-position: 200% 0; }
}

.shimmer {
  background: linear-gradient(
    90deg,
    #f5ecd9 0%, #e8ddc0 20%, #f9f3e3 50%,
    #e8ddc0 80%, #f5ecd9 100%
  );
  background-size: 200% 100%;
  animation: shimmer 2.5s ease-in-out infinite;
}

@keyframes fadeIn {
  from { opacity: 0; }
  to { opacity: 1; }
}</code></pre>

      <h3>The Isolation Pattern</h3>
      <pre><code>&lt;div className="relative aspect-4/3 overflow-hidden"&gt;
  {/* Shimmer layer — behind the image */}
  &lt;div className="absolute inset-0 z-0 shimmer" aria-hidden="true" /&gt;

  {/* Image — fades in on top */}
  &lt;Image className="... z-10 animate-[fadeIn_0.4s_ease-out]" /&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;</code></pre>

      <div class="two-col">
        <div class="col-card before">
          <h5>❌ Anti-pattern</h5>
          <p style="font-size:0.85rem;">Shimmer applied to the <em>parent</em> container — the image inherits the opacity and never fully appears.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="col-card after">
          <h5>✅ Solution</h5>
          <p style="font-size:0.85rem;">Shimmer on an isolated <code>z-0</code> layer behind. Image on <code>z-10</code> covers it when loaded.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>LCP optimization</strong>
        The first 3 cards receive <code>priority</code> → instant loading. <code>LCP warning</code> from Next.js is eliminated.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="part2-maps">
      <h2><span class="num">15</span> Part 2 · Google Maps Section</h2>
      <p>A "Visit Us" section was added to the homepage with location info + an embedded interactive map.</p>

      <h3>Zero-API-Key Approach</h3>
      <pre><code>&lt;iframe
  src="https://maps.google.com/maps?q=Qaryat+El+Asad+Alexandria+Desert+Rd&amp;output=embed"
  width="100%"
  height="100%"
  style={{ border: 0, minHeight: "450px" }}
  allowFullScreen
  loading="lazy"
  referrerPolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"
/&gt;</code></pre>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Why iframe, not Google Maps API?</strong>
        No <code>API key</code>, no billing account, no usage limits. For an embedded map in a portfolio project, this is the optimal choice.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="part2-calendar">
      <h2><span class="num">16</span> Part 2 · Add-to-Calendar Button</h2>
      <p>The confirmation email now includes a golden button that opens Google Calendar with the reservation pre-filled.</p>

      <h3>Pure Function Generator</h3>
      <pre><code>export function generateGoogleCalendarLink(
  params: CalendarEventParams
): string {
  const endDate = new Date(
    startDate.getTime() + durationMinutes * 60_000
  );

  const formatDate = (d: Date): string =&gt; {
    // YYYYMMDDTHHmmss
    ...
  };

  const dates = `${formatDate(startDate)}/${formatDate(endDate)}`;

  const searchParams = new URLSearchParams({
    action: "TEMPLATE",
    text: title,
    dates,
    details: description,
    location,
  });

  return `https://calendar.google.com/calendar/render?${searchParams}`;
}</code></pre>

      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Why this matters</strong>
        Reducing friction at the reservation confirmation stage increases show-up rates — a business metric that a restaurant owner immediately understands.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="part2-analytics">
      <h2><span class="num">17</span> Part 2 · Interactive Analytics Dashboard</h2>
      <p>Three Recharts visualizations embedded in <code>/admin</code> — donut charts for category distribution and featured balance, bar chart for price ranges.</p>

      <h3>Architecture — Pure Data Layer</h3>
      <div class="filetree">
        <div><span class="dir">src/lib/services/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="file new">analytics.ts</span> <span class="note">← pure aggregation functions</span></div>
        <div><span class="dir">src/components/admin/charts/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="file new">AnalyticsCharts.tsx</span> <span class="note">← Client Component (Recharts)</span></div>
      </div>

      <h3>Server Component → Client Component Boundary</h3>
      <pre><code>// admin/page.tsx (Server Component)
const [categoryData, priceData, featuredData] = await Promise.all([
  getCategoryDistribution(),
  getPriceDistribution(),
  getFeaturedDistribution(),
]);

return (
  &lt;AnalyticsCharts
    categoryData={categoryData}
    priceData={priceData}
    featuredData={featuredData}
  /&gt;
);</code></pre>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Clean separation</strong>
        <code>analytics.ts</code> contains pure aggregation logic — runs server-side, queries Prisma. <code>AnalyticsCharts.tsx</code> is the only Client Component, receiving already-processed data as props.
      </div>

      <h3>Custom Legend Pattern</h3>
      <p>Instead of <code>Recharts</code>' built-in labels (which overlapped on the donut chart), a custom <code>CustomLegend</code> component renders below each chart — clean, readable, and RTL-friendly.</p>

      <div class="two-col">
        <div class="col-card before">
          <h5>❌ Default Labels</h5>
          <p style="font-size:0.85rem;">Text rendered inside donut segments — overlapped in Arabic, unreadable.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="col-card after">
          <h5>✅ Custom Legend</h5>
          <p style="font-size:0.85rem;">Horizontal color-coded legend below each chart — clean, scalable.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">20</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>npm ci</code> runs scripts</td><td>CI fails on <code>postinstall</code></td><td>Add <code>--ignore-scripts</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Missing env for <code>prisma generate</code></td><td><code>PrismaConfigEnvError</code></td><td>Pass <code>DATABASE_URL</code> to step</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>LayoutProps&lt;"/"&gt;</code> in CI</td><td><code>Cannot find name</code></td><td>Use <code>React.ReactNode</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Shimmer on parent div</td><td>Image never fully appears</td><td>Isolate shimmer on <code>z-0</code> layer</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Recharts labels overlap</td><td>Arabic text collides</td><td>Custom legend below chart</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Recharts <code>formatter</code> type</td><td>TS <code>ValueType</code> mismatch</td><td>Remove formatter (defaults work)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Unsplash remote image blocked</td><td><code>next/image</code> rejects URL</td><td>Add to <code>remotePatterns</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Demo account exposed admin</td><td>Anyone can delete data</td><td>Separate <code>demo@</code> account + banner</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>middleware.ts</code> deprecation</td><td>Yellow warning every build</td><td>Rename to <code>proxy.ts</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal:</strong> Extend the reach of the existing 5-locale infrastructure to 7, and add a genuinely useful interactive feature that demonstrates a different class of engineering — algorithmic matching under tight cost and latency constraints.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li><strong>Italian locale</strong> — <code>messages/it.json</code> (~400 keys) + routing + switcher + email date locale.</li>
        <li><strong>Chinese locale</strong> — <code>messages/zh.json</code> with ICU plural rules adapted for Chinese (single-form <code>other</code>).</li>
        <li><strong>Smart FAQ Assistant</strong> — a floating chat panel with 10 intents supported in 7 languages.</li>
        <li><strong>Serverless</strong> — pure TypeScript keyword matcher, no LLM, no external API, no data download.</li>
        <li><strong>Priority tie-break</strong> — explicit policy for when two intents match a single query.</li>
        <li><strong>Duplicate-keyword dedupe</strong> — defensive fix for cross-language keyword collisions.</li>
        <li><strong>Responsive UI</strong> — bottom-left trigger above WhatsApp, panel that works on phones and desktops.</li>
        <li><strong>Full test matrix</strong> — verification across all 7 locales for all 10 intents.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="scope">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Two Features, One Phase</h2>
      <p>Both features share the same release cycle, and their paths converge on the same underlying principle: <strong>Direct server-side data access</strong>.</p>
      <div class="callout info">
        <strong>The shared principle</strong>
        <ul style="margin-top:0.5rem;margin-bottom:0">
          <li><strong>Locales</strong> — never call a translation API at runtime; every string lives in a JSON file.</li>
          <li><strong>Assistant</strong> — never call an LLM at runtime; every answer lives in a translation file too, chosen by a pure matcher.</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </section>
    <section id="commands">
      <h2><span class="num">3</span> Commands Table</h2>

          <tr><td>1</td><td><code>Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .next</code></td><td>Clear Next.js cache after adding new locale files</td></tr>

      <h3>Why Italian + Chinese?</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Language</th><th>Why this choice</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>🇮🇹 Italian</td><td>Real tourist market in Egypt — Italian visitors are common. Latin script, familiar plural rules, no surprises.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>🇨🇳 Mandarin</td><td><strong>Proves the system scales to non-Latin scripts.</strong> Chinese tourism to Cairo is growing, and the ICU plural rules differ fundamentally (only one form: <code>other</code>).</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Portfolio impact</strong>
        Adding Italian is easy. Adding Chinese is a demonstration — it proves the architecture handles CJK scripts, non-plural languages, and different date formats without any code path changes.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="routing">
      <h2><span class="num">6</span> Part 1 · routing.ts Update</h2>
      <pre><code>export const routing = defineRouting({
  locales: ['ar', 'en', 'fr', 'de', 'es', 'it', 'zh'],
  defaultLocale: 'ar',
  localePrefix: 'always'
});</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Everything else stays the same.</strong> The <code>RTL_LOCALES</code> constant remains <code>['ar']</code> — both Italian and Chinese are LTR.</p>
      <p><strong>Why defaultLocale stays Arabic:</strong> Google's <code>x-default</code> hreflang points to the default locale's URL. Since the restaurant is physically in Cairo, Arabic-first is correct regardless of how many other locales exist.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="switcher">
      <h2><span class="num">7</span> Part 1 · LanguageSwitcher Update</h2>
      <pre><code>const LOCALES_DATA: Record&lt;string, { label: string; code: string }&gt; = {
  ar: { label: "العربية", code: "eg" },
  en: { label: "English", code: "gb" },
  fr: { label: "Français", code: "fr" },
  de: { label: "Deutsch", code: "de" },
  es: { label: "Español", code: "es" },
  it: { label: "Italiano", code: "it" },
  zh: { label: "中文", code: "cn" },
};</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Two entries.</strong> The dropdown automatically iterates the new list because it reads from <code>routing.locales</code> (source of truth) — the <code>LOCALES_DATA</code> map only provides labels and flag codes.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="date-locale">
      <h2><span class="num">8</span> Part 1 · Email Date Locale</h2>
      <p>Email confirmation templates use <code>Intl.DateTimeFormat</code> to render the reservation date in the recipient's language. Two new BCP-47 codes required:</p>
      <pre><code>function getDateLocale(locale: string): string {
  const map: Record&lt;string, string&gt; = {
    ar: "ar-EG", en: "en-US", fr: "fr-FR",
    de: "de-DE", es: "es-ES",
    it: "it-IT",  // ← NEW
    zh: "zh-CN",  // ← NEW
  };
  return map[locale] ?? locale;
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>The result:</strong> An Italian reservation confirmation shows dates like <code>giovedì 15 ottobre 2026, 20:30</code>, and a Chinese one shows <code>2026年10月15日星期四 20:30</code> — from a single formatting line.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="cache-issue">
      <h2><span class="num">9</span> Part 1 · The .next Cache Issue</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Symptom</strong>
        After adding <code>it.json</code> and <code>zh.json</code>, navigating to <code>/it</code> and <code>/zh</code> throws:
        <pre style="margin:0.5rem 0;background:transparent;border:none;padding:0;color:inherit;font-size:0.78rem"><code style="background:transparent;color:inherit;padding:0">Cannot find module './it.json'</code></pre>
      </div>
      <p><strong>Root cause:</strong> Next.js/webpack caches the module context for dynamic <code>import()</code> calls. When <code>request.ts</code> contains:</p>
      <pre><code>messages: (await import(`../../messages/${locale}.json`)).default,</code></pre>
      <p>Webpack builds a static list of files matching <code>../../messages/*.json</code> at build time. Adding a new file to that directory does not invalidate the cached context.</p>
      <p><strong>Fix — always after adding a new locale file:</strong></p>
      <pre><code>Ctrl+C
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .next
npm run dev</code></pre>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Rule to remember</strong>
        Any time you add a file that's imported via a template-literal dynamic import, clear <code>.next</code> and restart. This is a Next.js quirk, not a bug in the project.
      </div>
    </section>

    <!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
         PART 2 — SMART FAQ ASSISTANT
         ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

    <section id="why-no-llm">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> Part 2 · Why Not an LLM</h2>
      <p><strong>The instinctive design</strong> for a "Smart Assistant" is to plug in an LLM (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) via an API. Every option was evaluated and rejected:</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Option</th><th>Why it doesn't fit</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><strong>WebLLM (Llama/Phi)</strong></td><td>1-2 GB download on first visit. Kills mobile users immediately.</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Transformers.js</strong></td><td>30-150 MB download, unreliable on mobile Safari (WebGL throttling).</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>The actual winner</strong>
        A <strong>pure TypeScript intent matcher</strong> — ~200 lines, zero dependencies, zero download, sub-50 ms response, works offline, works on every device.
      </div>
      <p><strong>Is it "real AI"?</strong> No — and that's the point. It doesn't pretend to. It's a well-engineered <em>information retrieval system</em>.</p>
      <p><strong>For a portfolio:</strong> Interviewers consistently rate "built a system" higher than "wrapped an API". This feature demonstrates algorithmic thinking — normalization, scoring, priority, tie-breaks — not prompt engineering.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="architecture">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> Part 2 · Architecture</h2>
      <div class="flow">
        <div class="flow-step">1. User types a question in any language</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">2. Client calls <code>askAssistant(query)</code> Server Action</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">3. <code>detectIntent(query)</code> normalizes + scores against 10 intents</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">4. Priority tie-break if two intents score equal</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">5. Winning intent's response pulled from current locale</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step success">6. Response returned in &lt; 50 ms, no external API</div>
      </div>
      <h3>Three files, three responsibilities</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>File</th><th>Responsibility</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>knowledge-base.ts</code></td><td>Pure data — 10 intents, each with keyword lists in all 7 languages</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>matcher.ts</code></td><td>Pure algorithm — normalize, score, dedupe, priority tie-break</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>actions/assistant.ts</code></td><td>Orchestration — call matcher, fetch translation, return reply</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Why this separation matters:</strong> The matcher is testable in isolation (<code>npx tsx -e "..."</code> — one command), and the knowledge base can grow to 30+ intents without touching any other file.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="knowledge">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> Part 2 · Knowledge Base</h2>
      <p>Ten intents × 7 languages = ~70 keyword lists, but only ~120 total keywords because many are shared across Romance and Germanic languages.</p>
      <pre><code>export const INTENT_KEYWORDS: Record&lt;IntentKey, string[]&gt; = {
  cancel: [
    "cancel", "cancellation", "modify", "change my", "reschedule",
    "الغاء", "الغيت", "الغي", "تعديل", "اغير", "ااجل",
    "annuler", "annulation", "modifier", "changer",
    "stornieren", "stornierung", "andern", "verschieben",
    "cancelar", "cancelacion", "cambiar", "modificar",
    "annullare", "annullamento", "cambiare", "modificare",
    "取消", "改期", "修改",
  ],
  // ... 9 more intents
};</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Two design decisions:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li><strong>Keywords are pre-normalized in the source.</strong> No accents, no diacritics, no Arabic tashkeel. The matcher normalizes user input the same way, so both sides compare on equal footing. This makes the file more readable and stable.</li>
        <li><strong>Keywords list every plural form explicitly.</strong> Romance languages have inflected plurals (<code>vegetariano</code> / <code>vegetariani</code>), and the matcher uses word boundaries for Latin scripts — so <code>vegetarian</code> won't match <code>vegetarianos</code>. Listing plurals is simpler and more predictable than adding a stemmer.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>
    <section id="matcher">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> Part 2 · Intent Matcher</h2>
      <p>A pure function with no side effects. Give it a query string, get back an intent or <code>null</code>.</p>
      <pre><code>export function detectIntent(rawQuery: string): IntentKey | null {
  const query = normalize(rawQuery);
  if (!query) return null;

  let bestIntent: IntentKey | null = null;
  let bestScore = 0;

  for (const [intentKey, keywords] of Object.entries(INTENT_KEYWORDS)) {
    const intent = intentKey as IntentKey;
    let score = 0;
    const seen = new Set&lt;string&gt;();

    for (const keyword of keywords) {
      const kw = normalize(keyword);
      if (!kw || seen.has(kw)) continue;
      seen.add(kw);

      const isLatin = /^[a-z0-9 ]+$/.test(kw);
      const matched = isLatin
        ? new RegExp(`\\b${escapeRegex(kw)}\\b`).test(query)
        : query.includes(kw);

      if (matched) score += kw.length &gt;= 4 ? 2 : 1;
    }

    // ... priority tie-break (next section)
  }

  return bestScore &gt;= MIN_SCORE ? bestIntent : null;
}</code></pre>

      <h3>The normalize() function</h3>
      <pre><code>function normalize(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .normalize("NFD")
    .replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, "")        // Latin diacritics: é → e
    .replace(/[\u064B-\u065F\u0670]/g, "")  // Arabic tashkeel
    .replace(/[إأآ]/g, "ا")                  // Arabic alef variants
    .replace(/ى/g, "ي")                      // Arabic alef maqsura
    .replace(/ة/g, "ه")                      // Arabic ta marbuta
    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
    .trim();
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why this is critical:</strong> A user typing <code>réservation</code> (French with accent) and a user typing <code>reservation</code> (no accent) should both match the same keyword list. Similarly, Arabic users typing <code>مواعيد</code> vs <code>مَوَاعِيد</code> (with tashkeel) should both match.</p>

      <h3>Scoring rules</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Case</th><th>Score</th><th>Rationale</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Keyword length ≥ 4</td><td>+2</td><td>Longer keywords are more specific</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Keyword length &lt; 4</td><td>+1</td><td>Short keywords like "map" could match unrelated words</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Latin keywords</td><td>word-boundary match</td><td><code>reserve</code> won't match <code>preserved</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Arabic / CJK keywords</td><td>substring match</td><td>No clear word boundaries in these scripts</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="priority">
      <h2><span class="num">14</span> Part 2 · Priority Tie-Break</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>The subtle bug</strong>
        Query: <code>"cancel my reservation"</code>. This matches <strong>both</strong> intents:
        <ul style="margin:0.5rem 0 0">
          <li><code>cancel</code> — via keyword <code>"cancel"</code> (score 2)</li>
          <li><code>reservation</code> — via keyword <code>"reservation"</code> (score 2)</li>
        </ul>
        <p style="margin:0.5rem 0 0"><strong>Tie.</strong> Which one wins?</p>
      </div>
      <p><strong>The wrong approach:</strong> rely on the order of keys in <code>knowledge-base.ts</code>. This is fragile — reordering the file would silently break behavior.</p>
      <p><strong>The right approach:</strong> an explicit <code>PRIORITY</code> array — priority as a policy decision, not an implementation detail.</p>
      <pre><code>// Lower index = higher priority on tie
const PRIORITY: IntentKey[] = [
  "cancel",       // specific action on a booking
  "allergies",    // safety concern
  "halal",        // dietary requirement
  "vegetarian",   // dietary preference
  "events",       // specific occasion
  "parking",      // specific facility
  "location",     // info request
  "hours",        // info request
  "reservation",  // general topic
  "menu",         // most general
];

const PRIORITY_INDEX = new Map&lt;IntentKey, number&gt;(
  PRIORITY.map((k, i) =&gt; [k, i])
);</code></pre>

      <h3>Tie-break logic</h3>
      <pre><code>const isBetter =
  score &gt; bestScore ||
  (score === bestScore &amp;&amp; score &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; candidatePriority &lt; currentPriority);

if (isBetter) {
  bestScore = score;
  bestIntent = intent;
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Three cases:</strong></p>
      <ol>
        <li><strong>Higher score</strong> → always wins (<code>score &gt; bestScore</code>)</li>
        <li><strong>Tie, higher priority</strong> → wins (<code>score === bestScore &amp;&amp; candidatePriority &lt; currentPriority</code>)</li>
        <li><strong>Tie, lower priority</strong> → keeps the existing winner</li>
      </ol>

      <h3>Why "cancel beats reservation"</h3>
      <p><strong>Cancelling is a specific action on a general concept.</strong> Every "cancel" query is also about a reservation, but not every "reservation" query is about cancelling. When a user types <code>cancel my reservation</code>, they're overwhelmingly asking about cancellation — the intent with the word <em>reservation</em> is just context.</p>
      <div class="callout info">
        <strong>The general principle</strong>
        When two intents tie, the more <strong>specific</strong> one wins. This is a well-known heuristic in information retrieval — used in search engines, recommendation systems, and email spam filters. Being explicit about the priority order documents the policy in code.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="dedupe">
      <h2><span class="num">15</span> Part 2 · The Duplicate Keyword Bug</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Discovered by adding debug logging</strong>
        <pre style="margin:0.5rem 0;background:transparent;border:none;padding:0;color:inherit;font-size:0.78rem"><code style="background:transparent;color:inherit;padding:0">{ intent: 'cancel', score: 2, bestScore: 0, bestIntent: null }
{ intent: 'reservation', score: 4, bestScore: 2, bestIntent: 'cancel' }
                                              ↑↑↑ should be 2</code></pre>
        Reservation scored <strong>4</strong> instead of 2 — so the priority tie-break never even ran.
      </div>
      <p><strong>Root cause:</strong> The keyword <code>"reservation"</code> appears <strong>twice</strong> in the array — once under the English comment, once under the French comment. Both got counted, doubling the score.</p>
      <pre><code>reservation: [
  "reserve", "reservation", "book", "booking", "table for",  // English
  ...
  "reserver", "reservation", "reserv",                       // French
                ↑↑↑ duplicate
],</code></pre>

      <h3>The fix: dedupe at the matcher level</h3>
      <pre><code>let score = 0;
const seen = new Set&lt;string&gt;();

for (const keyword of keywords) {
  const kw = normalize(keyword);
  if (!kw || seen.has(kw)) continue;   // ← dedupe here
  seen.add(kw);
  // ...
}</code></pre>

      <p><strong>Why this fix, and not the "obvious" one:</strong> We could have removed the duplicate from the knowledge base. But that only fixes today's bug. Tomorrow, adding a new language that shares a word with English (e.g., adding Portuguese, where "menu" is also "menu") would reintroduce it. Deduping in the matcher is <strong>idempotent, defensive, and forward-proof</strong>.</p>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>After the fix</strong>
        <pre style="margin:0.5rem 0;background:transparent;border:none;padding:0;color:inherit;font-size:0.78rem"><code style="background:transparent;color:inherit;padding:0">cancel my reservation       → cancel    ✅
je veux annuler ma réservation → cancel   ✅
book a table                → reservation ✅</code></pre>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="action">
      <h2><span class="num">16</span> Part 2 · Server Action</h2>
      <pre><code>"use server";

import { getTranslations } from "next-intl/server";
import { detectIntent } from "@/lib/assistant/matcher";
import type { IntentKey } from "@/lib/assistant/knowledge-base";

export type AssistantReply = {
  intent: IntentKey | null;
  text: string;
};

export async function askAssistant(query: string): Promise&lt;AssistantReply&gt; {
  if (!query || typeof query !== "string" || query.trim().length &lt; 2) {
    const t = await getTranslations("Assistant");
    return { intent: null, text: t("fallback") };
  }

  const t = await getTranslations("Assistant");
  const intent = detectIntent(query);

  if (!intent) {
    return { intent: null, text: t("fallback") };
  }

  const textMap: Record&lt;IntentKey, string&gt; = {
    hours: t("intents.hours"),
    location: t("intents.location"),
    parking: t("intents.parking"),
    reservation: t("intents.reservation"),
    cancel: t("intents.cancel"),
    menu: t("intents.menu"),
    allergies: t("intents.allergies"),
    vegetarian: t("intents.vegetarian"),
    halal: t("intents.halal"),
    events: t("intents.events"),
  };

  return { intent, text: textMap[intent] };
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why an explicit map instead of a template literal:</strong> next-intl v4 has strict typing for <code>t()</code>. A dynamic key like <code>t(\`intents.${intent}\`)</code> may or may not satisfy the compiler depending on the project config. The explicit map is type-safe, self-documenting, and turns the intent list into a compile-time checklist — if you add an 11th intent, TypeScript errors until you add its entry.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="errors">
      <h2><span class="num">20</span> The Errors Journey</h2>
      <p>Five real bugs surfaced during Phase 13 — each one taught a specific lesson.</p>

      <div class="error-journey">
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 1 — Cannot find module './it.json'</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">GET /it 500 · MODULE_NOT_FOUND</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Clear <code>.next</code> cache and restart. Webpack caches the module context for dynamic imports; adding a new locale file doesn't invalidate it.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 2 — IntentKey not exported from matcher</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Module '"./matcher"' declares 'IntentKey' locally, but it is not exported.</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Import <code>IntentKey</code> from its source (<code>knowledge-base.ts</code>) where it's defined, not from the file that consumes it. Type definitions belong where they're created.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 3 — French cancel lost to French reservation</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">"je veux annuler ma réservation" → returned reservation reply</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Priority tie-break — explicit array, not object-key order. Cancel beats reservation on tie.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 4 — Spanish plural not matched</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">"¿hay mesas vegetarianas?" → returned fallback</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Added explicit plural forms to the vegetarian keyword list. Word boundaries don't stem — plural "vegetarianas" must be listed separately.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="error-item">
          <h4>🎯 Error 5 — Duplicate keyword inflates score by 2×</h4>
          <div class="error-msg">Debug log: reservation scored 4 (should be 2) because "reservation" appears in both English and French blocks</div>
          <div class="error-fix"><strong>Fix:</strong> Dedupe keyword strings inside the matcher loop with a <code>Set&lt;string&gt;</code>. Defensive — prevents future languages from re-triggering the bug.</div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">22</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>New locale file not found</td><td>MODULE_NOT_FOUND after adding <code>xx.json</code></td><td>Clear <code>.next</code>, restart dev</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Type imported from wrong file</td><td>TS2459 "declares X locally"</td><td>Import from source, not consumer</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Two intents tie</td><td>Wrong reply for mixed queries</td><td>Explicit priority array</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Plural not matching</td><td>Romance-language plurals miss</td><td>List explicit plural forms in keywords</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Duplicate keywords</td><td>Score 2× expected → wrong winner</td><td>Dedupe with a <code>Set</code> inside the matcher</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Assistant behind WhatsApp</td><td>Buttons overlap</td><td><code>bottom-24</code> for assistant, <code>bottom-6</code> for WhatsApp</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Assistant on admin pages</td><td>Chat panel shows on /admin</td><td>Mount in <code>(public)/layout.tsx</code>, not root</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Panel behind modal</td><td>Click doesn't reach input</td><td>Both trigger and panel use <code>z-50</code></td></tr>

<file path="src/actions/admin-menu.ts">
"use server";

import { revalidatePath } from "next/cache";
import { getTranslations } from "next-intl/server";
import { auth } from "@/auth";
import { prisma } from "@/lib/prisma";
import { createMenuItemSchema } from "@/lib/validations/menu-item";
import { logAction } from "@/lib/services/audit";
import { tError } from "@/lib/utils/server-errors";

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 🍽️ Server Actions: Menu items management
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

type ActionResult = { success: true } | { success: false; error: string };

export type MenuItemActionResult =
  | { success: true; id: string }
  | { success: false; error: string; fieldErrors?: Record<string, string[]> };

async function requireAdmin() {
  const session = await auth();
  if (!session?.user) return null;
  if (session.user.role !== "ADMIN" && session.user.role !== "STAFF") {
    return null;
  }
  return session.user;
}

function getUserName(user: { name?: string | null }): string {
  return user.name ?? "Unknown";
}

// ─── Toggle availability ───
export async function toggleMenuItemAvailability(
  itemId: string,
  isAvailable: boolean
): Promise<ActionResult> {
  const user = await requireAdmin();
  if (!user) return { success: false, error: await tError("unauthorized") };

  try {
    const item = await prisma.menuItem.update({
      where: { id: itemId },
      data: { isAvailable },
      select: { name: true },
    });

    await logAction({
      userId: user.id,
      userName: getUserName(user),
      action: "UPDATE",
      entity: "MenuItem",
      entityId: itemId,
      entityName: item.name,
      severity: isAvailable ? "info" : "warning",
      changes: { after: { isAvailable } },
    });

    revalidatePath("/admin/menu");
    revalidatePath("/menu");
    revalidatePath("/");
    return { success: true };
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[toggleMenuItemAvailability]", error);
    return { success: false, error: await tError("unexpected") };
  }
}

// ─── Toggle featured ───
export async function toggleMenuItemFeatured(
  itemId: string,
  isFeatured: boolean
): Promise<ActionResult> {
  const user = await requireAdmin();
  if (!user) return { success: false, error: await tError("unauthorized") };

  try {
    const item = await prisma.menuItem.update({
      where: { id: itemId },
      data: { isFeatured },
      select: { name: true },
    });

    await logAction({
      userId: user.id,
      userName: getUserName(user),
      action: "UPDATE",
      entity: "MenuItem",
      entityId: itemId,
      entityName: item.name,
      severity: "info",
      changes: { after: { isFeatured } },
    });

    revalidatePath("/admin/menu");
    revalidatePath("/menu");
    revalidatePath("/");
    return { success: true };
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[toggleMenuItemFeatured]", error);
    return { success: false, error: await tError("unexpected") };
  }
}

// ─── Delete item (admin only) ───
export async function deleteMenuItem(itemId: string): Promise<ActionResult> {
  const user = await requireAdmin();
  if (!user) return { success: false, error: await tError("unauthorized") };

  if (user.role !== "ADMIN") {
    return { success: false, error: await tError("adminRequired") };
  }

  try {
    const deleted = await prisma.menuItem.findUnique({
      where: { id: itemId },
      select: { name: true, price: true, categoryId: true },
    });

    if (!deleted) {
      return { success: false, error: await tError("notFound") };
    }

    await prisma.menuItem.delete({ where: { id: itemId } });

    await logAction({
      userId: user.id,
      userName: getUserName(user),
      action: "DELETE",
      entity: "MenuItem",
      entityId: itemId,
      entityName: deleted.name,
      severity: "critical",
      changes: {
        before: {
          name: deleted.name,
          price: deleted.price,
          categoryId: deleted.categoryId,
        },
      },
    });

    revalidatePath("/admin/menu");
    revalidatePath("/menu");
    revalidatePath("/");
    return { success: true };
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[deleteMenuItem]", error);
    return { success: false, error: await tError("unexpected") };
  }
}

// ─── Create menu item ───
export async function createMenuItem(
  input: unknown
): Promise<MenuItemActionResult> {
  const user = await requireAdmin();
  if (!user) return { success: false, error: await tError("unauthorized") };

  const tValidation = await getTranslations("Errors.validation");
  const schema = createMenuItemSchema((key) =>
    tValidation(key as Parameters<typeof tValidation>[0])
  );
  const parsed = schema.safeParse(input);

  if (!parsed.success) {
    const fieldErrors: Record<string, string[]> = {};
    for (const issue of parsed.error.issues) {
      const key = issue.path.join(".") || "_";
      (fieldErrors[key] ??= []).push(issue.message);
    }
    return {
      success: false,
      error: await tError("invalidData"),
      fieldErrors,
    };
  }

  const data = parsed.data;

  try {
    const existing = await prisma.menuItem.findUnique({
      where: { slug: data.slug },
    });
    if (existing) {
      return {
        success: false,
        error: await tError("duplicateSlug"),
        fieldErrors: { slug: [await tError("duplicateSlug")] },
      };
    }

    const item = await prisma.menuItem.create({
      data: {
        name: data.name,
        nameEn: data.nameEn && data.nameEn !== "" ? data.nameEn : null,
        slug: data.slug,
        description:
          data.description && data.description !== ""
            ? data.description
            : null,
        descriptionEn:
          data.descriptionEn && data.descriptionEn !== ""
            ? data.descriptionEn
            : null,
        price: data.price,
        imageUrl:
          data.imageUrl && data.imageUrl !== "" ? data.imageUrl : null,
        categoryId: data.categoryId,
        isAvailable: data.isAvailable,
        isFeatured: data.isFeatured,
      },
    });

    await logAction({
      userId: user.id,
      userName: getUserName(user),
      action: "CREATE",
      entity: "MenuItem",
      entityId: item.id,
      entityName: item.name,
      severity: "info",
      changes: {
        after: {
          name: item.name,
          price: item.price,
          isAvailable: item.isAvailable,
          isFeatured: item.isFeatured,
        },
      },
    });

    revalidatePath("/admin/menu");
    revalidatePath("/menu");
    revalidatePath("/");
    return { success: true, id: item.id };
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[createMenuItem]", error);
    return { success: false, error: await tError("unexpected") };
  }
}

// ─── Update menu item ───
export async function updateMenuItem(
  itemId: string,
  input: unknown
): Promise<MenuItemActionResult> {
  const user = await requireAdmin();
  if (!user) return { success: false, error: await tError("unauthorized") };

  const tValidation = await getTranslations("Errors.validation");
  const schema = createMenuItemSchema((key) =>
    tValidation(key as Parameters<typeof tValidation>[0])
  );
  const parsed = schema.safeParse(input);

  if (!parsed.success) {
    const fieldErrors: Record<string, string[]> = {};
    for (const issue of parsed.error.issues) {
      const key = issue.path.join(".") || "_";
      (fieldErrors[key] ??= []).push(issue.message);
    }
    return { success: false, error: await tError("invalidData"), fieldErrors };
  }

  const data = parsed.data;

  try {
    const before = await prisma.menuItem.findUnique({
      where: { id: itemId },
      select: {
        name: true,
        nameEn: true,
        price: true,
        isAvailable: true,
        isFeatured: true,
      },
    });

    if (!before) {
      return { success: false, error: await tError("notFound") };
    }

    const duplicate = await prisma.menuItem.findFirst({
      where: { slug: data.slug, NOT: { id: itemId } },
    });
    if (duplicate) {
      return {
        success: false,
        error: await tError("duplicateSlug"),
        fieldErrors: { slug: [await tError("duplicateSlug")] },
      };
    }

    const item = await prisma.menuItem.update({
      where: { id: itemId },
      data: {
        name: data.name,
        nameEn: data.nameEn && data.nameEn !== "" ? data.nameEn : null,
        slug: data.slug,
        description:
          data.description && data.description !== ""
            ? data.description
            : null,
        descriptionEn:
          data.descriptionEn && data.descriptionEn !== ""
            ? data.descriptionEn
            : null,
        price: data.price,
        imageUrl:
          data.imageUrl && data.imageUrl !== "" ? data.imageUrl : null,
        categoryId: data.categoryId,
        isAvailable: data.isAvailable,
        isFeatured: data.isFeatured,
      },
    });

    await logAction({
      userId: user.id,
      userName: getUserName(user),
      action: "UPDATE",
      entity: "MenuItem",
      entityId: item.id,
      entityName: item.name,
      severity: "info",
      changes: {
        before: {
          name: before.name,
          nameEn: before.nameEn,
          price: before.price,
          isAvailable: before.isAvailable,
          isFeatured: before.isFeatured,
        },
        after: {
          name: item.name,
          nameEn: item.nameEn,
          price: item.price,
          isAvailable: item.isAvailable,
          isFeatured: item.isFeatured,
        },
      },
    });

    revalidatePath("/admin/menu");
    revalidatePath("/menu");
    revalidatePath("/");
    return { success: true, id: item.id };
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[updateMenuItem]", error);
    return { success: false, error: await tError("unexpected") };
  }
}

<file path="src/components/admin/MenuItemForm.tsx">
// MenuItemForm.tsx
"use client";

import { useState, useTransition } from "react";
import { useScrollToFirstError } from "@/lib/hooks/use-scroll-to-first-error";
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";
import { useRouter } from "@/i18n/navigation";
import { FormField, inputClasses } from "@/components/ui/FormField";
import { ImagePicker } from "./ImagePicker";
import {
  createMenuItem,
  updateMenuItem,
  type MenuItemActionResult,
} from "@/actions/admin-menu";
import { Form } from "@/components/ui/Form";

type Category = {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  slug: string;
};

type InitialData = {
  id?: string;
  name: string;
  nameEn: string;
  slug: string;
  description: string;
  descriptionEn: string;
  price: number;
  imageUrl: string;
  categoryId: string;
  isAvailable: boolean;
  isFeatured: boolean;
};

type Props = {
  categories: Category[];
  initialData?: InitialData;
};

function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .trim()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9\s-]/g, "")
    .replace(/\s+/g, "-")
    .replace(/-+/g, "-");
}

export function MenuItemForm({ categories, initialData }: Props) {
  const router = useRouter();
  const t = useTranslations("Admin.menuForm");
  const isEdit = !!initialData?.id;

  const [formData, setFormData] = useState<InitialData>({
    id: initialData?.id,
    name: initialData?.name ?? "",
    nameEn: initialData?.nameEn ?? "",
    slug: initialData?.slug ?? "",
    description: initialData?.description ?? "",
    descriptionEn: initialData?.descriptionEn ?? "",
    price: initialData?.price ?? 0,
    imageUrl: initialData?.imageUrl ?? "",
    categoryId: initialData?.categoryId ?? categories[0]?.id ?? "",
    isAvailable: initialData?.isAvailable ?? true,
    isFeatured: initialData?.isFeatured ?? false,
  });

  const [isSubmitting, setIsSubmitting] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [fieldErrors, setFieldErrors] = useState<Record<string, string[]>>({});
  const [, startTransition] = useTransition();

  // Auto-scroll to the first errored field on validation failure
  useScrollToFirstError(
    Object.keys(fieldErrors).length > 0 ? fieldErrors : undefined
  );

  function handleChange(
    e: React.ChangeEvent<
      HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | HTMLSelectElement
    >
  ) {
    const { name, value, type } = e.target;
    const checked = (e.target as HTMLInputElement).checked;
    setFormData((prev) => ({
      ...prev,
      [name]: type === "checkbox" ? checked : value,
    }));
  }

  function handleNameChange(e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) {
    const name = e.target.value;
    setFormData((prev) => ({
      ...prev,
      name,
      slug: isEdit ? prev.slug : slugify(name),
    }));
  }

  async function handleSubmit(e: React.SyntheticEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    e.preventDefault();
    setIsSubmitting(true);
    setError(null);
    setFieldErrors({});

    const payload = {
      name: formData.name,
      nameEn: formData.nameEn,
      slug: formData.slug,
      description: formData.description,
      descriptionEn: formData.descriptionEn,
      price: formData.price,
      imageUrl: formData.imageUrl,
      categoryId: formData.categoryId,
      isAvailable: formData.isAvailable,
      isFeatured: formData.isFeatured,
    };

    const result: MenuItemActionResult = isEdit
      ? await updateMenuItem(formData.id!, payload)
      : await createMenuItem(payload);

    if (!result.success) {
      setError(result.error);
      setFieldErrors(result.fieldErrors ?? {});
      setIsSubmitting(false);
      return;
    }
    startTransition(() => {
      router.push("/admin/menu");
      router.refresh();
    });
  }

  return (
    <Form
      onSubmit={handleSubmit}
      className="bg-card border border-border rounded-2xl p-6 md:p-8"
    >
      <div className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-5">
        <FormField label={t("nameLabel")} required>
          <input
            type="text"
            name="name"
            value={formData.name}
            onChange={handleNameChange}
            required
            placeholder={t("namePlaceholder")}
            className={inputClasses}
          />
          {fieldErrors.name && (
            <p className="text-xs text-red-600 mt-1">{fieldErrors.name[0]}</p>
          )}
        </FormField>

        <FormField label={t("slugLabel")} required>
          <input
            type="text"
            name="slug"
            value={formData.slug}
            onChange={handleChange}
            required
            placeholder={t("slugPlaceholder")}
            dir="ltr"
            className={inputClasses}
          />
          <p className="text-xs text-muted mt-1">{t("slugHint")}</p>
          {fieldErrors.slug && (
            <p className="text-xs text-red-600 mt-1">{fieldErrors.slug[0]}</p>
          )}
        </FormField>

        <FormField label={t("priceLabel")} required>
          <input
            type="number"
            name="price"
            value={formData.price}
            onChange={handleChange}
            required
            min="0"
            step="0.5"
            placeholder={t("pricePlaceholder")}
            dir="ltr"
            className={inputClasses}
          />
          {fieldErrors.price && (
            <p className="text-xs text-red-600 mt-1">{fieldErrors.price[0]}</p>
          )}
        </FormField>

        <FormField label={t("categoryLabel")} required>
          <select
            name="categoryId"
            value={formData.categoryId}
            onChange={handleChange}
            required
            className={inputClasses}
          >
            {categories.map((cat) => (
              <option key={cat.id} value={cat.id}>
                {cat.name}
              </option>
            ))}
          </select>
          {fieldErrors.categoryId && (
            <p className="text-xs text-red-600 mt-1">
              {fieldErrors.categoryId[0]}
            </p>
          )}
        </FormField>

        <div className="md:col-span-2">
          <ImagePicker
            value={formData.imageUrl}
            onChange={(val) =>
              setFormData((prev) => ({ ...prev, imageUrl: val }))
            }
            error={fieldErrors.imageUrl?.[0]}
          />
        </div>

        <div className="md:col-span-2">
          <FormField label={t("descriptionLabel")}>
            <textarea
              name="description"
              value={formData.description}
              onChange={handleChange}
              rows={3}
              placeholder={t("descriptionPlaceholder")}
              className={inputClasses}
            />
            {fieldErrors.description && (
              <p className="text-xs text-red-600 mt-1">
                {fieldErrors.description[0]}
              </p>
            )}
          </FormField>
        </div>

                <div className="md:col-span-2">
          <FormField label={t("nameEnLabel")}>
            <input
              type="text"
              name="nameEn"
              value={formData.nameEn}
              onChange={handleChange}
              placeholder={t("nameEnPlaceholder")}
              dir="ltr"
              className={inputClasses}
            />
            {fieldErrors.nameEn && (
              <p className="text-xs text-red-600 mt-1">
                {fieldErrors.nameEn[0]}
              </p>
            )}
          </FormField>
        </div>

        <div className="md:col-span-2">
          <FormField label={t("descriptionEnLabel")}>
            <textarea
              name="descriptionEn"
              value={formData.descriptionEn}
              onChange={handleChange}
              rows={3}
              placeholder={t("descriptionEnPlaceholder")}
              dir="ltr"
              className={inputClasses}
            />
            {fieldErrors.descriptionEn && (
              <p className="text-xs text-red-600 mt-1">
                {fieldErrors.descriptionEn[0]}
              </p>
            )}
          </FormField>
        </div>

        <div className="md:col-span-2 flex flex-wrap gap-6 pt-2">
          <label className="flex items-center gap-2 cursor-pointer">
            <input
              type="checkbox"
              name="isAvailable"
              checked={formData.isAvailable}
              onChange={handleChange}
              className="w-4 h-4 accent-[--color-accent]"
            />
            <span className="text-sm font-medium">{t("isAvailableLabel")}</span>
          </label>

          <label className="flex items-center gap-2 cursor-pointer">
            <input
              type="checkbox"
              name="isFeatured"
              checked={formData.isFeatured}
              onChange={handleChange}
              className="w-4 h-4 accent-[--color-accent]"
            />
            <span className="text-sm font-medium">{t("isFeaturedLabel")}</span>
          </label>
        </div>
      </div>

      {error && !Object.keys(fieldErrors).length && (
        <div className="mt-6 p-3 rounded-lg text-sm bg-red-50 text-red-800 border border-red-200">
          {error}
        </div>
      )}

      <div className="mt-8 flex flex-wrap gap-3 justify-end">
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => router.push("/admin/menu")}
          className="px-6 py-3 rounded-full border border-border hover:border-foreground transition-colors"
        >
          {t("cancel")}
        </button>
        <button
          type="submit"
          disabled={isSubmitting}
          className="bg-accent hover:bg-accent-dark text-white font-medium px-8 py-3 rounded-full transition-colors disabled:opacity-60 disabled:cursor-not-allowed"
        >
          {isSubmitting ? t("saving") : isEdit ? t("save") : t("create")}
        </button>
      </div>
    </Form>
  );
}
</file>

<file path="src/components/auth/LoginForm.tsx">
// src/components/auth/LoginForm.tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";
import { signIn } from "next-auth/react";
import { useRouter, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation";
import { FormField, inputClasses } from "@/components/ui/FormField";
import { Form } from "@/components/ui/Form";

type Result =
  | { kind: "idle" }
  | { kind: "submitting" }
  | { kind: "error"; message: string };

export function LoginForm() {
  const t = useTranslations("Login");
  const router = useRouter();
  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
  const callbackUrl = searchParams.get("callbackUrl") ?? "/admin";

  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
  const [result, setResult] = useState<Result>({ kind: "idle" });

  async function handleSubmit(e: React.SyntheticEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    e.preventDefault();
    setResult({ kind: "submitting" });

    const response = await signIn("credentials", {
      email,
      password,
      redirect: false,
    });

    if (!response || response.error) {
      setResult({
        kind: "error",
        message: t("errorInvalidCredentials"),
      });
      return;
    }

    router.push(callbackUrl);
    router.refresh();
  }

  return (
    <Form
      onSubmit={handleSubmit}
      className="bg-card border border-border rounded-2xl p-8 shadow-sm"
    >
      <div className="space-y-5">
        <FormField label={t("emailLabel")} required>
          <input
            type="email"
            value={email}
            onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
            autoFocus
            required
            autoComplete="email"
            placeholder="admin@lumiere.com"
            dir="ltr"
            className={inputClasses}
          />
        </FormField>

        <FormField label={t("passwordLabel")} required>
          <input
            type="password"
            value={password}
            onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)}
            required
            autoComplete="current-password"
            placeholder="••••••••"
            dir="ltr"
            className={inputClasses}
          />
        </FormField>
      </div>

      {result.kind === "error" && (
        <div className="mt-5 p-3 rounded-lg text-sm bg-red-50 text-red-800 border border-red-200">
          {result.message}
        </div>
      )}

      <button
        type="submit"
        disabled={result.kind === "submitting"}
        className="mt-6 w-full bg-accent hover:bg-accent-dark text-white font-medium py-3 px-8 rounded-full transition-colors disabled:opacity-60 disabled:cursor-not-allowed"
      >
        {result.kind === "submitting" ? t("submitting") : t("submitButton")}
      </button>
    </Form>
  );
}
</file>

import { getTranslations } from "next-intl/server";

// Menu item data as it comes from Prisma
type MenuItemCardProps = {
  item: {
    id: string;
    name: string;
    slug: string;
    description: string | null;
    price: number;
    imageUrl: string | null;
    isFeatured: boolean;
    category: { name: string };
  };
  priority?: boolean;
};

export async function MenuItemCard({
  item,
  priority = false,
}: MenuItemCardProps) {
  const t = await getTranslations("Menu");

  return (
    <Link
      href={`/menu/${item.slug}`}
      className="group bg-card border border-border rounded-2xl overflow-hidden hover:shadow-lg hover:border-accent/40 transition-all duration-300 flex flex-col"
    >
      {/* Image or fallback */}
      <div className="relative aspect-4/3 bg-accent-light overflow-hidden">

        {item.imageUrl ? (
          <Image
            src={item.imageUrl}
            alt={item.name}
            fill
            priority={priority}
            sizes="(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 33vw"
            style={{ aspectRatio: "4 / 3" }}
            className="object-cover group-hover:scale-105 transition-transform duration-500 z-10 animate-[fadeIn_0.4s_ease-out]"
          />
        ) : (
          <div className="absolute inset-0 z-10 flex items-center justify-center text-4xl text-accent/40">
            🍽️
          </div>
        )}

        {item.isFeatured && (
          <span className="absolute top-3 left-3 z-20 bg-accent text-white text-xs font-bold px-3 py-1 rounded-full">

          </span>
        )}
      </div>

          {item.category.name}
        </span>
        <h3 className="text-lg font-bold mb-2 group-hover:text-accent transition-colors">
          {item.name}
        </h3>
        {item.description && (
          <p className="text-sm text-muted leading-relaxed line-clamp-2 mb-4">

<file path="src/lib/validations/menu-item.ts">
import { z } from "zod";

type TranslateFn = (key: string) => string;

export function createMenuItemSchema(t: TranslateFn) {
  return z.object({
    name: z
      .string()
      .trim()
      .min(2, t("itemNameTooShort"))
      .max(80, t("itemNameTooLong")),

    slug: z
      .string()
      .trim()
      .toLowerCase()
      .min(2, t("slugTooShort"))
      .max(80, t("slugTooLong"))
      .regex(/^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/, t("slugInvalidFormat")),

    nameEn: z
      .string()
      .trim()
      .max(80, t("itemNameTooLong"))
      .optional()
      .or(z.literal("")),

    description: z
      .string()
      .trim()
      .max(500, t("itemDescriptionTooLong"))
      .optional()
      .or(z.literal("")),

    descriptionEn: z
      .string()
      .trim()
      .max(500, t("itemDescriptionTooLong"))
      .optional()
      .or(z.literal("")),

    price: z.coerce
      .number()
      .positive(t("priceMustBePositive"))
      .max(10000, t("priceTooLarge")),

    // Accepts: empty string | local path ("/images/x.jpg") | absolute URL (http/https)
    imageUrl: z
      .string()
      .trim()
      .optional()
      .refine(
        (val) =>
          val === undefined ||
          val === "" ||
          val.startsWith("/images/") ||
          /^https?:\/\/.+/.test(val),
        { message: t("imageUrlInvalid") }
      ),

    categoryId: z.string().min(1, t("categoryRequired")),

    isAvailable: z.boolean().default(true),
    isFeatured: z.boolean().default(false),
  });
}

export type MenuItemInput = z.infer<ReturnType<typeof createMenuItemSchema>>;
</file>
