    <header class="hero">
      <div class="kicker">Phase 01 · Foundation</div>
      <h1>Project Foundation &amp; Environment Setup</h1>
      <p class="lede">Establish a production-grade foundation for a single-codebase full-stack restaurant application. This phase configures Next.js 16, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Prisma 6, and a local SQLite database.</p>
      <div class="stack">
        <span>Next.js 16</span><span>TypeScript 5</span><span>Prisma 6</span>
        <span>SQLite</span><span>Tailwind CSS 4</span><span>Node.js 24</span>
      </div>
    </header>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal:</strong> Move from an empty directory to a working Next.js application with a validated Prisma schema pointing at a local database — the foundation every subsequent phase builds on.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li>A working Next.js 16 application served on <code>http://localhost:3000</code>.</li>
        <li>A stable, pinned Prisma 6 installation — not the RC branch.</li>
        <li>A committed, validated <code>schema.prisma</code> with SQLite datasource.</li>
        <li>A clean <code>package.json</code> free of experimental <code>postinstall</code> hooks.</li>
        <li><code>npx prisma validate</code> returns success.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="architecture">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Architectural Decision</h2>
      <p>Why a single Next.js codebase instead of keeping Django as a separate backend?</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Concern</th><th>Two-Server (Django + Next.js)</th><th>Single-Codebase (Next.js)</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Languages</td><td>Python + TypeScript</td><td>TypeScript only</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Deployments</td><td>2 servers, 2 CI pipelines</td><td>1 Vercel project</td></tr>
          <tr><td>API boundary</td><td>HTTP round-trip between servers</td><td>Direct function call in same process</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Database clients</td><td>Django ORM + Prisma</td><td>Prisma only</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Type safety</td><td>Not end-to-end</td><td>End-to-end (Zod + TS + Prisma)</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Engineering rationale</strong>
        Eliminating the network boundary between frontend and backend removes serialization cost, CORS configuration, and duplicated authentication logic. Server Components query Prisma in the same Node process.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="prerequisites">
      <h2><span class="num">3</span> Environment Prerequisites</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Requirement</th><th>Minimum</th><th>Verified Version</th><th>Rationale</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Node.js</td><td>18.17+</td><td><strong>v24.12.0</strong></td><td>Next.js 16 requires Node ≥18.17 for native ESM and Web APIs</td></tr>
          <tr><td>npm</td><td>9+</td><td><strong>11.15.0</strong></td><td>Needed for <code>npx</code> and workspace-aware installs</td></tr>
          <tr><td>OS</td><td>Windows 10</td><td>Windows 10</td><td>Target development environment</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Disk</td><td>~1 GB</td><td>—</td><td><code>node_modules</code> + <code>.next/</code> cache</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="commands">
      <h2><span class="num">4</span> Complete Commands Table</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Command</th><th>Purpose</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>1</td><td><code>node -v</code></td><td>Verify Node.js installed</td></tr>
          <tr><td>2</td><td><code>npm -v</code></td><td>Verify npm installed</td></tr>
          <tr><td>3</td><td><code>npx create-next-app@latest lumiere-nextjs-fullstack</code></td><td>Scaffold Next.js project</td></tr>
          <tr><td>4</td><td><code>cd lumiere-nextjs-fullstack</code></td><td>Enter project directory</td></tr>
          <tr><td>5</td><td><code>dir</code> / <code>dir src</code> / <code>dir src\app</code></td><td>Verify structure</td></tr>
          <tr><td>6</td><td><code>npm run dev</code></td><td>Start dev server on port 3000</td></tr>
          <tr><td>7</td><td><code>npm uninstall prisma @prisma/client</code></td><td>Remove unstable RC Prisma 8</td></tr>
          <tr><td>8</td><td><code>Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .claude, .cursor, .agents, .devin</code></td><td>Delete AI-agent folders from RC init</td></tr>
          <tr><td>9</td><td><code>del prisma.config.ts</code></td><td>Delete RC config file</td></tr>
          <tr><td>10</td><td><code>npm install prisma@6 --save-dev</code></td><td>Install pinned stable Prisma 6</td></tr>
          <tr><td>11</td><td><code>npm install @prisma/client@6</code></td><td>Install matching Prisma Client</td></tr>
          <tr><td>12</td><td><code>npx prisma init --datasource-provider sqlite</code></td><td>Initialize Prisma in SQLite mode</td></tr>
          <tr><td>13</td><td><code>npm install dotenv --save-dev</code></td><td>Required by <code>prisma.config.ts</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>14</td><td><code>npx prisma validate</code></td><td>Validate schema correctness</td></tr>
          <tr><td>15</td><td><code>npx prisma --version</code></td><td>Confirm installed engine versions</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>PowerShell vs CMD</strong>
        <code>rmdir /s /q</code> fails in PowerShell. Use <code>Remove-Item -Recurse -Force</code>.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="structure">
      <h2><span class="num">5</span> Target Folder Structure</h2>
      <pre><code>lumiere-nextjs-fullstack/
├── .env                          ← DATABASE_URL secret
├── .gitignore                    ← excludes .env, /src/generated/
├── next.config.ts
├── package.json
├── prisma/
│   ├── schema.prisma             ← data model blueprint
│   └── (migrations/)             ← empty until Phase 2
├── prisma.config.ts              ← Prisma 6 config
├── public/
├── src/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── favicon.ico
│   │   ├── globals.css
│   │   ├── layout.tsx
│   │   └── page.tsx
│   └── generated/
│       └── prisma/               ← Prisma Client output (gitignored)
└── tsconfig.json</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="step1">
      <h2><span class="num">6</span> Step 1 — Node.js Verification</h2>
      <pre><code>$ node -v
v24.12.0
$ npm -v
11.15.0</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Queries the Node binary for its version tag.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY:</strong> Next.js 16 hard-requires Node ≥18.17. Running on an older runtime causes cryptic ESM and <code>fetch</code> errors during build, not at install.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="step2">
      <h2><span class="num">7</span> Step 2 — Next.js Scaffolding</h2>
      <pre><code>npx create-next-app@latest lumiere-nextjs-fullstack</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> <code>npx</code> downloads <code>create-next-app</code> transiently and executes it. npm forces the project name to be lowercase with hyphens.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY:</strong> The official scaffolder ensures up-to-date Next.js defaults, correct TypeScript config, and a working App Router skeleton.</p>
      <h3>Prompt Answers</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Prompt</th><th>Answer</th><th>Rationale</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Use recommended defaults?</td><td>No, customize</td><td>Explicit control over structure</td></tr>
          <tr><td>TypeScript?</td><td>Yes</td><td>End-to-end type safety</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Which linter?</td><td>ESLint</td><td>Catches bugs before runtime</td></tr>
          <tr><td>React Compiler?</td><td>No</td><td>Still experimental</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Tailwind CSS?</td><td>Yes</td><td>Utility-first styling</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Code inside <code>src/</code>?</td><td>Yes</td><td>Cleaner root directory</td></tr>
          <tr><td>App Router?</td><td>Yes</td><td>Required for Server Components</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Customize import alias?</td><td>No</td><td>Keep default <code>@/*</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="step3">
      <h2><span class="num">8</span> Step 3 — Structure Verification</h2>
      <pre><code>cd lumiere-nextjs-fullstack
dir
dir src
dir src\app</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Expected <code>src/app/</code>:</strong> <code>favicon.ico</code>, <code>globals.css</code>, <code>layout.tsx</code>, <code>page.tsx</code>.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY:</strong> Verify <code>src/</code> and App Router exist — all future Route Handlers and Server Components depend on this path.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="step4">
      <h2><span class="num">9</span> Step 4 — Dev Server Verification</h2>
      <pre><code>npm run dev

▲ Next.js 16.3.5 (Turbopack)
- Local:         http://localhost:3000
✓ Ready in 5.0s
GET / 200 in 9.7s</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> <code>next dev</code> boots Turbopack on port 3000 and compiles pages on-demand.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY:</strong> Confirms the toolchain works before adding Prisma. A 200 status guarantees routing, React rendering, and HTTP stack all function.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="step5">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> Step 5 — Prisma Setup (with RC Downgrade)</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Critical Fix</strong>
        <code>npx prisma init</code> initially installed <code>prisma@8.0.0-rc.15</code>, which created unexpected folders (<code>.claude/</code>, <code>.cursor/</code>, <code>.agents/</code>, <code>.devin/</code>) and failed to generate <code>schema.prisma</code>. This is an unstable pre-release.
      </div>
      <h3>Downgrade &amp; Reinitialize</h3>
      <pre><code>npm uninstall prisma @prisma/client
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .claude, .cursor, .agents, .devin
del prisma.config.ts
npm install prisma@6 --save-dev
npm install @prisma/client@6
npx prisma init --datasource-provider sqlite
npm install dotenv --save-dev
npx prisma validate</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Removes experimental dependencies and their side-effect artifacts, then reinstalls the current stable major (6.x).</p>
      <p><strong>WHY:</strong> RC = Release Candidate = feature-frozen but not production-hardened. RC APIs change without notice; stable versions have documented behavior and community support.</p>
      <pre><code>The schema at prisma\schema.prisma is valid 🚀</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="configs">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> Configuration Files</h2>

      <h3>prisma/schema.prisma</h3>
      <pre><code>generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client"
  output   = "../src/generated/prisma"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "sqlite"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><code>output</code> places the generated client inside <code>src/</code>, not <code>node_modules</code> — makes it visible in the repo tree, allows IDE navigation.</li>
        <li><code>provider = "sqlite"</code> — file-based, zero-install, perfect for development.</li>
        <li><code>url = env(...)</code> — injects the connection string from <code>.env</code>, keeping secrets out of source.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>.env</h3>
      <pre><code>DATABASE_URL="file:./dev.db"</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Prisma CLI resolves <code>./dev.db</code> relative to <code>prisma/</code> directory → creates <code>prisma/dev.db</code>.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY:</strong> The <code>prisma/</code> folder is the natural home for local database files. One line replaces this with a hosted PostgreSQL URL at deploy time.</p>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Runtime caveat</strong>
        Next.js resolves <code>./</code> relative to the project root, not <code>prisma/</code>. This mismatch is fixed in Phase 2 inside <code>src/lib/prisma.ts</code> using an absolute path.
      </div>

      <h3>prisma.config.ts</h3>
      <pre><code>import "dotenv/config";
import { defineConfig, env } from "prisma/config";

export default defineConfig({
  schema: "prisma/schema.prisma",
  migrations: { path: "prisma/migrations" },
  engine: "classic",
  datasource: { url: env("DATABASE_URL") },
});</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><code>import "dotenv/config"</code> — loads <code>.env</code> before Prisma reads it. Mandatory in Prisma 6.</li>
        <li><code>defineConfig</code> — typed configuration helper; enables IDE autocomplete.</li>
        <li><code>engine: "classic"</code> — uses the Node-API query engine for max performance on Windows.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>package.json — Final State</h3>
      <pre><code>{
  "name": "lumiere-nextjs-fullstack",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "next dev",
    "build": "next build",
    "start": "next start",
    "lint": "eslint"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@prisma/client": "^6.19.3",
    "next": "16.3.5",
    "react": "19.2.8",
    "react-dom": "19.2.8"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@tailwindcss/postcss": "^4",
    "@types/node": "^20",
    "@types/react": "^19",
    "@types/react-dom": "^19",
    "dotenv": "^17.4.2",
    "eslint": "^9",
    "eslint-config-next": "16.3.5",
    "prisma": "^6.19.3",
    "tailwindcss": "^4",
    "typescript": "^5"
  }
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Cleanup:</strong> A <code>postinstall</code> script injected by the Prisma RC (<code>"prisma skills sync || exit 0"</code>) was removed — it referenced commands that don't exist in stable Prisma 6.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="flow">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> Request Data Flow (Phase 1 Scope)</h2>
      <p>Phase 1 introduces no HTTP endpoints, but establishes the runtime dependency chain:</p>
      <pre><code>Browser → Next.js Dev Server (port 3000)
             ↓
             Reads .env → DATABASE_URL
             ↓
             Instantiates Prisma Client (generated in src/generated/prisma)
             ↓
             Connects to prisma/dev.db (SQLite)</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Boundary rationale:</strong> Secrets flow one direction only — from <code>.env</code> into server processes. Nothing reaches the browser.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="verify">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> Verification Checklist</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Check</th><th>Command</th><th>Expected</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Node version</td><td><code>node -v</code></td><td>18.17+</td></tr>
          <tr><td>npm version</td><td><code>npm -v</code></td><td>9+</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Dev server boots</td><td><code>npm run dev</code></td><td>Ready in Xs + GET / 200</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Prisma version</td><td><code>npx prisma --version</code></td><td>6.19.3</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Schema valid</td><td><code>npx prisma validate</code></td><td>valid 🚀</td></tr>
          <tr><td>File tree</td><td><code>dir prisma</code></td><td>schema.prisma present</td></tr>
          <tr><td>package.json clean</td><td>Search for <code>postinstall</code></td><td>Not found</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">14</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Uppercase project name</td><td><code>name can no longer contain capital letters</code></td><td>Use lowercase + hyphens</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Prisma RC installed</td><td><code>prisma.config.ts</code> creates AI-agent folders</td><td>Pin <code>prisma@6</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>rmdir</code> in PowerShell</td><td><code>Positional parameter '/q'</code></td><td>Use <code>Remove-Item -Recurse -Force</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Missing <code>dotenv</code></td><td><code>Environment variable not found: DATABASE_URL</code></td><td><code>npm install dotenv --save-dev</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>postinstall</code> leftover</td><td><code>prisma skills sync</code> not found</td><td>Delete line from <code>package.json</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Update prompt to v8 RC</td><td><code>Update available 6.19.3 -&gt; 8.0.0-rc.15</code></td><td>Ignore — never jump majors on live projects</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="glossary">
      <h2><span class="num">15</span> Technical Abbreviations Glossary</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Abbr.</th><th>Full Form</th><th>Plain-English Meaning</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>API</td><td>Application Programming Interface</td><td>Contract for how programs talk</td></tr>
          <tr><td>CLI</td><td>Command-Line Interface</td><td>Programs you run by typing commands</td></tr>
          <tr><td>CUID</td><td>Collision-resistant Unique Identifier</td><td>ID string that won't collide (Phase 2)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>DevDeps</td><td>Development Dependencies</td><td>Packages only needed while building</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ESM</td><td>ECMAScript Modules</td><td>Modern <code>import</code>/<code>export</code> syntax</td></tr>
          <tr><td>HMR</td><td>Hot Module Replacement</td><td>Live code updates without reload</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ORM</td><td>Object-Relational Mapper</td><td>Translates objects ↔ SQL</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RC</td><td>Release Candidate</td><td>Near-final, not production-hardened</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RTL</td><td>Right-to-Left</td><td>Text direction for Arabic/Hebrew</td></tr>
          <tr><td>URI/URL</td><td>Uniform Resource Identifier / Locator</td><td>Address string for a resource</td></tr>
          <tr><td>WASM</td><td>WebAssembly</td><td>Binary format runnable in browsers + Node</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="summary">

        <li>Prisma downgraded from RC 8 to stable 6.19.3</li>
        <li>Schema, <code>.env</code>, and <code>prisma.config.ts</code> in place</li>
        <li><code>dotenv</code> installed; <code>postinstall</code> RC artifact removed</li>
        <li><code>npx prisma validate</code> → valid</li>
        <li>Dev server verified on <code>localhost:3000</code></li>
      </ul>
      <h3>Engineering Outcomes</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Zero-network-boundary architecture validated</li>
        <li>Stable dependency versions pinned</li>
        <li>Environment secrets kept out of version control</li>
        <li>Foundation ready for Phase 2 (data modeling)</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

      <div class="kicker">Phase 02 · Data Modeling</div>
      <h1>Prisma Schema, Migrations &amp; Seed Data</h1>
      <p class="lede">Design and implement the complete relational data model for a restaurant system: menu hierarchy, physical tables, and reservations. Populate it with realistic Arabic seed data that exercises every rule the business will rely on.</p>
      <div class="stack">
        <span>Prisma 6</span><span>SQLite</span><span>Migrations</span>
        <span>Seed Scripts</span><span>tsx</span><span>CUID</span>
      </div>
    </header>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal:</strong> Turn the empty Prisma schema from Phase 1 into a complete, migrated, seeded relational database that every subsequent phase queries against.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li>Four Prisma models: <code>Category</code>, <code>MenuItem</code>, <code>Table</code>, <code>Reservation</code>.</li>
        <li>Two applied migrations in <code>prisma/migrations/</code>.</li>
        <li>A live SQLite database (<code>prisma/dev.db</code>) with all four tables.</li>
        <li>A modular seed system: <code>prisma/data/</code> modules + <code>prisma/seed.ts</code> orchestrator.</li>
        <li>4 categories, 12 menu items, 10 tables populated.</li>
        <li>Visual confirmation in Prisma Studio at <code>localhost:5555</code>.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="decision">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Architectural Decision — Single Source of Truth</h2>
      <p>Why one declarative <code>schema.prisma</code> instead of separate SQL, ORM models, and migrations?</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Concern</th><th>Alternative</th><th>Chosen (single schema.prisma)</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Data definition</td><td>SQL DDL + ORM + migrations separately</td><td>One file generates all three</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Type generation</td><td>Manual TypeScript interfaces</td><td>Auto-generated PrismaClient types</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Migrations</td><td>Hand-written SQL</td><td><code>prisma migrate dev</code> diffs + writes SQL</td></tr>
          <tr><td>IDE support</td><td>Manual type annotations</td><td>Full autocomplete on every query</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Engineering rationale</strong>
        One declarative file eliminates drift between database, application types, and documentation. Any change begins in <code>schema.prisma</code> and cascades down automatically.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="entities">
      <h2><span class="num">3</span> The Four Entities — Domain Model</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Entity</th><th>Represents</th><th>Business Purpose</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>Category</code></td><td>Menu classification</td><td>Groups items (Appetizers, Main Courses, Desserts, Beverages)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>MenuItem</code></td><td>A dish</td><td>Name, slug, price, image, availability flag</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Table</code></td><td>Physical restaurant table</td><td>Number, seating capacity, location, active flag</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Reservation</code></td><td>A booking</td><td>Guest info, date, party size, assigned table, status</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Real-world mapping:</strong> Customer browses <code>MenuItem</code> → submits <code>Reservation</code> → system assigns <code>Table</code> based on <code>capacity</code> and time overlap.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="models-1">
      <h2><span class="num">7</span> Step 1 — Category &amp; MenuItem Models</h2>
      <pre><code>model Category {
  id           String     @id @default(cuid())
  name         String     @unique
  slug         String     @unique
  description  String?
  displayOrder Int        @default(0)
  createdAt    DateTime   @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime   @updatedAt
  items        MenuItem[]

  @@map("categories")
}

model MenuItem {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  name        String
  slug        String   @unique
  description String?
  price       Float
  imageUrl    String?
  isAvailable Boolean  @default(true)
  isFeatured  Boolean  @default(false)
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  categoryId  String
  category    Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@map("menu_items")
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Declares two related tables. <code>Category</code> owns <code>MenuItem</code> via a foreign key.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY:</strong> Separating categories from items allows filterable menus (<code>/menu?category=desserts</code>) without duplicating category names in every row.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="modifiers">
      <h2><span class="num">8</span> Prisma Field Modifiers Reference</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Modifier</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Rationale</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>@id</code></td><td>Primary key</td><td>Unique row identifier</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>@default(cuid())</code></td><td>Auto-generated unique ID</td><td>Collision-resistant across distributed systems</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>@default(now())</code></td><td>Server timestamp on insert</td><td>Audit trail without application code</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>@updatedAt</code></td><td>Auto-updates on write</td><td>Zero-maintenance last-modified tracking</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>@unique</code></td><td>Unique index</td><td>Prevents duplicate slugs/names</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>String?</code></td><td>Nullable field</td><td>Optional data (descriptions, image URLs)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>@default(true)</code></td><td>Boolean default</td><td>New rows favor availability</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>@default(0)</code></td><td>Numeric default</td><td>Safe sort key for display order</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>@@map("...")</code></td><td>Physical table name</td><td>Keeps DB names snake_case</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="relation">
      <h2><span class="num">9</span> Relation Semantics — @relation Explained</h2>
      <pre><code>categoryId  String
category    Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><code>categoryId String</code> — the foreign key column stored in <code>menu_items</code>.</li>
        <li><code>category Category</code> — the TypeScript accessor for the related row (<code>item.category.name</code>).</li>
        <li><code>fields: [categoryId]</code> — which local column holds the FK value.</li>
        <li><code>references: [id]</code> — which column in the parent table it points to.</li>
        <li><code>onDelete: Cascade</code> — deleting a category deletes all its items.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Why Cascade here</strong>
        Orphaned menu items (pointing to a deleted category) break queries and confuse admins. Cascade enforces referential integrity without manual cleanup.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="migration1">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> Migration #1 Execution</h2>
      <pre><code>npx prisma migrate dev --name init_menu_models

SQLite database dev.db created at file:./dev.db
Applying migration `20260915071026_init_menu_models`
Your database is now in sync with your schema.
✔ Generated Prisma Client (6.19.3) to .\src\generated\prisma in 174ms</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Prisma diffs <code>schema.prisma</code> against the current DB state, writes SQL to <code>migrations/</code>, applies it, then regenerates the client.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY:</strong> Versioned migrations give a reproducible path from empty DB to current schema — critical for team onboarding and production deploys.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="studio">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> Verifying via Prisma Studio</h2>
      <pre><code>npx prisma studio
Prisma Studio is up on http://localhost:5555</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Verification:</strong> Left sidebar shows <code>Category</code> and <code>MenuItem</code> models. Both tables show "There are no rows in this table" (expected — no seed yet). Column headers match <code>schema.prisma</code> fields.</p>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Prisma Studio is a Node.js process reading <code>dev.db</code> directly via the query engine.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY:</strong> Visual confirmation that migrations created real, queryable tables before we build on top.</p>
      <div class="screenshot">Screenshot: Prisma Studio showing Category + MenuItem empty tables</div>
    </section>

    <section id="models-2">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> Step 2 — Table &amp; Reservation Models</h2>
      <pre><code>model Table {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  number       Int      @unique
  capacity     Int
  location     String?
  isActive     Boolean  @default(true)
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt
  reservations Reservation[]

  @@map("tables")
}

model Reservation {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  guestName       String
  guestEmail      String
  guestPhone      String
  guestsCount     Int
  reservationDate DateTime
  durationMinutes Int      @default(90)
  status          String   @default("PENDING")
  notes           String?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  tableId String
  table   Table  @relation(fields: [tableId], references: [id])

  @@map("reservations")
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> <code>Reservation</code> links to <code>Table</code> via <code>tableId</code>. No <code>onDelete: Cascade</code>.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY No Cascade:</strong> Deleting a table must not destroy historical reservation records — those are financial/legal artifacts.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="status">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> Design Decision — Status Field &amp; SQLite Enum Limitation</h2>
      <p><strong>Approach:</strong> Use <code>String</code> with <code>@default("PENDING")</code> rather than a native <code>enum</code>.</p>
      <h3>Valid statuses (application convention)</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>PENDING</code> — created, awaiting staff confirmation</li>
        <li><code>CONFIRMED</code> — staff-approved</li>
        <li><code>CANCELLED</code> — cancelled by guest or staff</li>
        <li><code>COMPLETED</code> — guest dined, record closed</li>
      </ul>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Prisma supports enums natively <em>except on SQLite</em>, which lacks the <code>ENUM</code> type.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY String for now:</strong> Keeping <code>String</code> allows the same schema to run on SQLite (dev) and PostgreSQL (prod, Phase 9) without edits. At migration time to Postgres, this field converts to a native enum in one line.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="migration2">
      <h2><span class="num">14</span> Migration #2 Execution</h2>
      <pre><code>npx prisma migrate dev --name add_table_and_reservation

Applying migration `20260915145315_add_table_and_reservation`
Your database is now in sync with your schema.
✔ Generated Prisma Client (6.19.3) to .\src\generated\prisma in 254ms</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Verification in Prisma Studio:</strong> 4 tables visible: <code>Category</code>, <code>MenuItem</code>, <code>Table</code>, <code>Reservation</code>. All empty.</p>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Incremental migration — only the diff (two new tables) is applied.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY Two Migrations instead of one:</strong> Each migration is atomic and named for its intent. If the second migration fails, the first remains intact.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="seed-strategy">
      <h2><span class="num">15</span> Step 3 — Seed Data Strategy</h2>
      <h3>Why seed data matters</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Empty DB → empty UI → nothing to test.</li>
        <li>Realistic data (Arabic names, realistic prices) validates Arabic rendering and RTL flow.</li>
        <li>Repeatable: <code>npm run db:seed</code> wipes and re-populates deterministically.</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>Modular structure chosen</h3>
      <pre><code>prisma/
├── data/
│   ├── categories.ts    ← static arrays
│   ├── menu-items.ts
│   └── tables.ts
└── seed.ts              ← orchestrator (imports data, writes to DB)</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Engineering rationale:</strong> Separating data (<code>data/</code>) from logic (<code>seed.ts</code>) means non-developers can adjust menus without touching orchestration code.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="seed-files">
      <h2><span class="num">16</span> Seed Data Files</h2>

      <h3>prisma/data/categories.ts</h3>
      <pre><code>export const categories = [
  { name: 'مقبلات', slug: 'appetizers',
    description: 'أطباق خفيفة لبدء الوجبة', displayOrder: 1 },
  { name: 'أطباق رئيسية', slug: 'main-courses',
    description: 'الأطباق الرئيسية الشهية', displayOrder: 2 },
  { name: 'حلويات', slug: 'desserts',
    description: 'تحلية ختام الوجبة', displayOrder: 3 },
  { name: 'مشروبات', slug: 'beverages',
    description: 'مشروبات ساخنة وباردة', displayOrder: 4 },
]</code></pre>

      <h3>prisma/data/menu-items.ts (excerpt — 12 items total)</h3>
      <pre><code>export const menuItems = [
  // ─── مقبلات ───
  { name: 'شوربة العدس', slug: 'lentil-soup',
    description: 'شوربة عدس تقليدية مع الكمون والليمون',
    price: 45, isFeatured: false, categorySlug: 'appetizers' },
  { name: 'حمص بالطحينة', slug: 'hummus',
    description: 'حمص كريمي مع زيت الزيتون والصنوبر',
    price: 55, isFeatured: true, categorySlug: 'appetizers' },
  // ... (10 more items across 4 categories)
]</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Each item carries <code>categorySlug</code> (not <code>categoryId</code>) — human-readable, decoupled from DB IDs.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY:</strong> The seed script resolves <code>categorySlug → category.id</code> at runtime, so IDs can be regenerated freely.</p>

      <h3>prisma/data/tables.ts</h3>
      <pre><code>export const tables = [
  { number: 1,  capacity: 2,  location: 'Window' },
  { number: 2,  capacity: 2,  location: 'Window' },
  { number: 3,  capacity: 4,  location: 'Indoor' },
  { number: 4,  capacity: 4,  location: 'Indoor' },
  { number: 5,  capacity: 4,  location: 'Indoor' },
  { number: 6,  capacity: 6,  location: 'Indoor' },
  { number: 7,  capacity: 6,  location: 'Outdoor' },
  { number: 8,  capacity: 6,  location: 'Outdoor' },
  { number: 9,  capacity: 8,  location: 'VIP' },
  { number: 10, capacity: 10, location: 'VIP' },
]</code></pre>
      <p><strong>WHY This Distribution:</strong> Realistic mix — few 2-seaters (couples), many 4-seaters (families), limited 8–10 capacity (groups/events). This exercises the table-assignment algorithm in Phase 5.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="seed-orchestrator">
      <h2><span class="num">17</span> prisma/seed.ts — Orchestrator</h2>
      <pre><code>import 'dotenv/config'
import { PrismaClient } from '../src/generated/prisma/client'
import { categories } from './data/categories'
import { menuItems } from './data/menu-items'
import { tables } from './data/tables'

const prisma = new PrismaClient()

async function main() {
  console.log('🌱 بدء زرع البيانات...')

  await prisma.reservation.deleteMany()
  await prisma.menuItem.deleteMany()
  await prisma.category.deleteMany()
  await prisma.table.deleteMany()
  console.log('🧹 تم تنظيف الجداول')

  for (const category of categories) {
    await prisma.category.create({ data: category })
  }
  console.log(`📂 تم إنشاء ${categories.length} تصنيفات`)

  for (const item of menuItems) {
    const { categorySlug, ...itemData } = item
    const category = await prisma.category.findUnique({
      where: { slug: categorySlug },
    })
    if (!category) throw new Error(`❌ التصنيف "${categorySlug}" غير موجود`)
    await prisma.menuItem.create({
      data: { ...itemData, categoryId: category.id },
    })
  }
  console.log(`🍽️  تم إنشاء ${menuItems.length} أطباق`)

  for (const table of tables) {
    await prisma.table.create({ data: table })
  }
  console.log(`🪑 تم إنشاء ${tables.length} طاولات`)

  console.log('✨ اكتمل زرع البيانات بنجاح!')
}

main()
  .catch((error) => { console.error('❌ خطأ أثناء الزرع:', error); process.exit(1) })
  .finally(async () => { await prisma.$disconnect() })</code></pre>
      <h3>Line-by-line rationale</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>import 'dotenv/config'</code> — loads <code>.env</code> BEFORE Prisma Client initializes (critical — see Slide 20).</li>
        <li><code>deleteMany()</code> order — child tables first to avoid FK violations.</li>
        <li><code>const { categorySlug, ...itemData }</code> — destructures out the helper field, keeping the DB payload clean.</li>
        <li><code>findUnique({ where: { slug } })</code> — resolves category FK by slug, avoiding hardcoded CUIDs.</li>
        <li><code>main().catch(...).finally(...)</code> — guarantees connection cleanup and non-zero exit on failure.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="tsx">
      <h2><span class="num">18</span> Why tsx? — The TypeScript Executor</h2>
      <pre><code>npm install tsx --save-dev</code></pre>
      <p><strong>What tsx does:</strong> Accepts <code>.ts</code> file → transpiles on the fly → runs on Node.js. Uses esbuild (Go-based) for transpilation. Handles both CommonJS and ESM seamlessly.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY needed here:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>Node.js cannot run <code>.ts</code> natively (as of Node 24 without experimental flags).</li>
        <li><code>seed.ts</code> imports from <code>src/generated/prisma/client</code> — a TypeScript module.</li>
        <li>No compile step, no output directory, no <code>tsconfig</code> target confusion.</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>Alternatives rejected</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>ts-node</code> — slower, ESM friction.</li>
        <li><code>esbuild-register</code> — less maintained.</li>
        <li>Compile to <code>.js</code> first — extra step, stale files.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="dotenv">
      <h2><span class="num">19</span> The dotenv Loading Failure &amp; Fix</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Symptom</strong>
        <code>PrismaClientInitializationError: error: Environment variable not found: DATABASE_URL.</code>
      </div>
      <p><strong>Root cause:</strong> <code>tsx</code> does NOT auto-load <code>.env</code>. Running <code>tsx prisma/seed.ts</code> starts Node.js, which reads <code>process.env</code> — but <code>.env</code> was never parsed.</p>
      <h3>Tool-by-tool .env behavior</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Tool</th><th>Auto-loads .env?</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>next dev</code></td><td>Yes (Next.js handles it)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>prisma migrate</code></td><td>Yes (via <code>prisma.config.ts</code>)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>tsx prisma/seed.ts</code></td><td><strong>No</strong> ← here's the problem</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Fix (one line at top of <code>seed.ts</code>):</strong></p>
      <pre><code>import 'dotenv/config'</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> <code>dotenv/config</code> reads <code>.env</code> and merges into <code>process.env</code> at import time — before <code>new PrismaClient()</code> executes.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY the top of the file:</strong> ES module imports execute in declaration order. Placing the dotenv import first guarantees <code>.env</code> is populated before Prisma's engine initialization.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="gitignore">
      <h2><span class="num">20</span> .gitignore Update</h2>
      <pre><code># Prisma generated client
/src/generated/prisma</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> Excludes the entire generated client directory from Git.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY:</strong> <code>src/generated/prisma/</code> contains a 21 MB Windows binary (<code>query_engine-windows.dll.node</code>) and machine-specific code. Committing it would:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>Inflate the repo by hundreds of MB per platform.</li>
        <li>Cause merge conflicts between Windows/macOS/Linux developers.</li>
        <li>Be regenerated automatically by <code>prisma generate</code> on every install.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    </section>

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">22</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>tsx</code> seed fails</td><td><code>Environment variable not found: DATABASE_URL</code></td><td>Add <code>import 'dotenv/config'</code> at top</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Cascade delete order</td><td><code>Foreign key constraint failed</code></td><td>Delete Reservation → MenuItem → Category → Table</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Prisma 8 RC prompt</td><td><code>Update available 6.19.3 -&gt; 8.0.0-rc.15</code></td><td><strong>Ignore</strong> — never upgrade majors mid-project</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>schema.prisma</code> typo</td><td><code>npx prisma validate</code> fails</td><td>Read error — Prisma points to exact line</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Seed re-run duplicates</td><td>Duplicate slug error</td><td>Ensure <code>deleteMany()</code> runs first</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>.env</code> not found</td><td><code>file:./dev.db</code> resolves wrong</td><td>Absolute path fix comes in Phase 3</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="flow">
      <h2><span class="num">23</span> Data Flow (Phase 2 Scope)</h2>
      <p>Phase 2 introduces no HTTP endpoints, but establishes the write path used by every subsequent phase:</p>
      <div class="diagram">Developer terminal
    ↓
npm run db:seed → tsx loads .env → Prisma Client
    ↓
Prisma Client → SQLite engine (query_engine-windows.dll.node)
    ↓
dev.db (single file on disk)
    ↓
prisma/migrations/ records the schema diff
    ↓
src/generated/prisma/ exposes typed API for future use</div>
      <p><strong>Boundary rationale:</strong> Data flows one direction only during seeding — developer intent → disk. No browser involvement, no HTTP layer.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="glossary">
      <h2><span class="num">24</span> Technical Abbreviations Glossary</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Abbr.</th><th>Full Form</th><th>Plain-English Meaning</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>CUID</td><td>Collision-resistant Unique Identifier</td><td>25-char ID; sortable, URL-safe, collision-free</td></tr>
          <tr><td>DDL</td><td>Data Definition Language</td><td>SQL statements that create/alter tables</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ESM</td><td>ECMAScript Modules</td><td>Standard <code>import</code>/<code>export</code> syntax</td></tr>
          <tr><td>FK</td><td>Foreign Key</td><td>Column referencing another table's primary key</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ID</td><td>Identifier</td><td>Unique key for a row</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ORM</td><td>Object-Relational Mapper</td><td>Code layer translating objects ↔ SQL</td></tr>
          <tr><td>PK</td><td>Primary Key</td><td>Column uniquely identifying a row</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RC</td><td>Release Candidate</td><td>Near-final build, not production-hardened</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RTL</td><td>Right-to-Left</td><td>Text direction for Arabic/Hebrew</td></tr>
          <tr><td>SEO</td><td>Search Engine Optimization</td><td>Practices making pages rank well in search</td></tr>
          <tr><td>SQL</td><td>Structured Query Language</td><td>Standard language for relational databases</td></tr>
          <tr><td>tsx</td><td>TypeScript Execute</td><td>Fast Node.js TypeScript runner</td></tr>
          <tr><td>UUID</td><td>Universally Unique Identifier</td><td>36-char ID standard (Prisma prefers CUID)</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <header class="hero">
      <div class="kicker">Phase 06 · Email + WhatsApp</div>
      <h1>Email Notifications &amp; WhatsApp Integration</h1>
      <p class="lede">Deliver transactional emails to guests after every successful reservation and provide a one-tap WhatsApp channel for inquiries. Uses the Strategy Pattern for swappable providers and fail-safe delivery so email failures never break a reservation.</p>
      <div class="stack">
        <span>React Email</span><span>Resend (deferred)</span>
        <span>Console Provider</span><span>Strategy Pattern</span>
        <span>Fail-Safe Design</span><span>WhatsApp Deep Link</span>
      </div>
    </header>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal:</strong> Send Arabic confirmation emails to guests when a reservation is created — and keep a fast, one-tap WhatsApp channel always available — without breaking the bank or violating the strict no-card policy.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li><code>src/lib/email/types.ts</code> — shared types for the email subsystem.</li>
        <li><code>src/lib/email/templates/ReservationConfirmation.tsx</code> — RTL Arabic email template.</li>
        <li><code>src/lib/email/providers/console.ts</code> — development email provider (prints to terminal).</li>
        <li><code>src/lib/email/send.ts</code> — facade that selects the provider at runtime.</li>
        <li>Wiring inside <code>src/actions/reservation.ts</code> — non-blocking email dispatch.</li>
        <li><code>src/lib/constants/contact.ts</code> — WhatsApp number &amp; default message.</li>
        <li><code>src/components/layout/WhatsAppButton.tsx</code> — floating button on every page.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="strategy">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Architectural Decision — Strategy Pattern</h2>
      <p><strong>The problem:</strong> Every environment needs a different email backend.</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Environment</th><th>Requirement</th><th>Solution</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Local development</td><td>No signup, no card, instant feedback</td><td><code>console</code> provider</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Staging / Production</td><td>Real delivery to guests</td><td><code>resend</code> provider (deferred)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Future</td><td>Alternative (SendGrid, AWS SES, etc.)</td><td>Add another provider file</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>Architecture Diagram</h3>
      <div class="strategy">
        <div class="strategy-row"><div class="strategy-box">actions/reservation.ts</div></div>
        <div class="strategy-row"><span class="strategy-arrow">↓</span></div>
        <div class="strategy-row"><div class="strategy-box facade">lib/email/send.ts (Facade)</div></div>
        <div class="strategy-row"><span class="strategy-label">reads EMAIL_PROVIDER from .env</span></div>
        <div class="strategy-row">
          <span class="strategy-arrow">↙</span>
          <span style="width:100px"></span>
          <span class="strategy-arrow">↘</span>
        </div>
        <div class="strategy-row">
          <div class="strategy-box provider-1">providers/console.ts</div>
          <div class="strategy-box provider-2">providers/resend.ts</div>
        </div>
        <div class="strategy-row"><span class="strategy-label">prints to terminal · real delivery (deferred)</span></div>
      </div>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Engineering rationale</strong>
        The Server Action never knows which provider is active. Switching from <code>console</code> to <code>resend</code> requires <strong>zero code changes</strong> — only one line in <code>.env</code>.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="comparison">
      <h2><span class="num">3</span> Comparison with Django Email Backends</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Concern</th><th>Django</th><th>Next.js (this project)</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Dev backend</td><td><code>console.EmailBackend</code></td><td><code>console</code> provider (custom)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Production backend</td><td><code>anymail.backends.resend</code></td><td><code>resend</code> provider (deferred)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Switch mechanism</td><td><code>settings.EMAIL_BACKEND</code></td><td><code>process.env.EMAIL_PROVIDER</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Calling API</td><td><code>send_mail(...)</code></td><td><code>sendReservationConfirmation(...)</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>Why start with console</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><strong>Zero signup required</strong> — no email address, no verification</li>
        <li><strong>Instant feedback</strong> — terminal shows email within milliseconds</li>
        <li><strong>Deterministic testing</strong> — email content reproducible across runs</li>
        <li><strong>Drop-in replacement</strong> — <code>Resend</code> provider added later without refactoring</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Deferred decision</strong>
        Resend signup is scheduled for a future session to verify its card policy together before committing.
      </div>
    </section>

    </section>

    <section id="types">
      <h2><span class="num">6</span> Email Types — types.ts</h2>
      <pre><code>export type EmailProviderName = "console" | "resend";

export type ReservationEmailData = {
  to: string;
  guestName: string;
  reservationId: string;
  tableNumber: number;
  reservationDate: Date;
  guestsCount: number;
};

export type SendEmailResult = {
  success: boolean;
  messageId?: string;
  error?: string;
};</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><code>EmailProviderName</code> — union type narrows <code>EMAIL_PROVIDER</code> to exactly two valid values. Typos become compile errors.</li>
        <li><code>ReservationEmailData</code> — the <strong>canonical input shape</strong> for every email template. New templates (cancel, reminder) reuse this shape or extend it.</li>
        <li><code>SendEmailResult</code> — uniform return contract. All providers must return this shape. Callers don't branch per provider.</li>
        <li><code>messageId?</code> optional — <code>console</code> returns a fake ID; <code>resend</code> returns a real one.</li>
        <li><code>error?</code> optional — populated only on failure.</li>
      </ul>
      <p><strong>Why these three types live in one file:</strong> They form the <strong>interface</strong> of the email subsystem. Any provider or template imports from here. One file to review for API shape changes.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="template-1">
      <h2><span class="num">7</span> React Email Template (Part 1)</h2>
      <pre><code>import {
  Html, Head, Preview, Body, Container, Section,
  Text, Heading, Hr,
} from "@react-email/components";
import type { ReservationEmailData } from "../types";

const colors = {
  bg: "#faf7f2", card: "#ffffff",
  accent: "#c9a961", accentDark: "#a88847",
  text: "#1a1a1a", muted: "#6b6b6b", border: "#e5ddd0",
};

function formatArabicDate(date: Date): string {
  return new Intl.DateTimeFormat("ar-EG", {
    weekday: "long", year: "numeric", month: "long",
    day: "numeric", hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit", hour12: true,
  }).format(date);
}

export function ReservationConfirmation({
  guestName, reservationId, tableNumber,
  reservationDate, guestsCount,
}: Omit&lt;ReservationEmailData, "to"&gt;) {
  const shortId = reservationId.slice(0, 8).toUpperCase();

  return (
    &lt;Html dir="rtl" lang="ar"&gt;
      &lt;Head /&gt;
      &lt;Preview&gt;{`تم استلام حجزك في Lumière — طاولة رقم ${tableNumber}`}&lt;/Preview&gt;
      {/* ... Body continues in next section ... */}
    &lt;/Html&gt;
  );
}</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><code>Omit&lt;ReservationEmailData, "to"&gt;</code> — the template doesn't need the recipient address; excluding it prevents accidental misuse.</li>
        <li><code>Intl.DateTimeFormat("ar-EG", ...)</code> — native Arabic date formatting. <code>"ar-EG"</code> (Egypt) yields <code>الخميس، ١٥ أكتوبر ٢٠٢٦ في ٠٨:٣٠ م</code>. Zero dependency on external date libraries.</li>
        <li><code>&lt;Preview&gt;{...}&lt;/Preview&gt;</code> — <strong>must be a single string</strong>. Template literals force the type, avoiding the TypeScript error <code>number is not assignable to ReactNode &amp; string</code>.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="template-2">
      <h2><span class="num">8</span> React Email Template (Part 2)</h2>
      <pre><code>&lt;Body style={body}&gt;
  &lt;Container style={container}&gt;
    &lt;Section style={header}&gt;
      &lt;Heading style={logo}&gt;Lumière&lt;/Heading&gt;
      &lt;Text style={tagline}&gt;تجربة طعام استثنائية&lt;/Text&gt;
    &lt;/Section&gt;

    &lt;Section style={content}&gt;
      &lt;Heading as="h1" style={h1}&gt;مرحباً {guestName} 👋&lt;/Heading&gt;
      &lt;Text style={paragraph}&gt;
        تم استلام حجزك بنجاح، ونحن في انتظارك بشغف. إليك تفاصيل حجزك:
      &lt;/Text&gt;

      &lt;Section style={detailsBox}&gt;
        &lt;DetailRow label="رقم الطاولة" value={`رقم ${tableNumber}`} highlight /&gt;
        &lt;DetailRow label="عدد الأشخاص" value={`${guestsCount} أشخاص`} /&gt;
        &lt;DetailRow label="التاريخ والوقت" value={formatArabicDate(reservationDate)} /&gt;
        &lt;DetailRow label="رقم الحجز" value={`#${shortId}`} /&gt;
      &lt;/Section&gt;

      &lt;Text style={paragraph}&gt;
        سيتم تأكيد حجزك نهائياً عبر البريد الإلكتروني، أو سيتواصل معك
        فريقنا هاتفياً في حال الحاجة.
      &lt;/Text&gt;

      &lt;Hr style={hr} /&gt;
      &lt;Text style={footer}&gt;
        هذا البريد أُرسل تلقائياً من نظام حجوزات Lumière.
      &lt;/Text&gt;
    &lt;/Section&gt;
  &lt;/Container&gt;
&lt;/Body&gt;</code></pre>
      <p>Every style object (e.g., <code>header</code>, <code>logo</code>, <code>h1</code>) is a JavaScript object that React Email converts to inline <code>style=""</code> attributes during HTML generation.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="inline">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> Why Inline Styles — The Email Client Constraint</h2>
      <p><strong>The core problem:</strong> Email clients are stuck in 2005.</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Feature</th><th>Web Browser</th><th>Gmail</th><th>Outlook</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>&lt;link rel="stylesheet"&gt;</code></td><td>✅</td><td>❌ Stripped</td><td>❌ Stripped</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>&lt;style&gt;</code> block</td><td>✅</td><td>⚠️ Partial</td><td>❌ Mostly stripped</td></tr>
          <tr><td>External CSS variables</td><td>✅</td><td>❌</td><td>❌</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>inline style=""</code></td><td>✅</td><td>✅</td><td>✅</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>The only universally supported approach:</strong> inline <code>style</code> attributes on every element.</p>
      <p><strong>React Email solves this elegantly:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>You write styles as JavaScript objects.</li>
        <li><code>render()</code> from <code>@react-email/components</code> converts them to inline <code>style=""</code> attributes during HTML generation.</li>
        <li>Component tree stays readable; output is 2005-compatible.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="console">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> Console Provider — providers/console.ts</h2>
      <pre><code>import type { ReservationEmailData, SendEmailResult } from "../types";

export async function sendViaConsole(
  data: ReservationEmailData,
  html: string
): Promise&lt;SendEmailResult&gt; {
  const line = "═".repeat(60);

  console.log("\n" + line);
  console.log("📧 [DEV] إيميل جاهز للإرسال (لم يُرسل فعلياً)");
  console.log(line);
  console.log(`   إلى:      ${data.to}`);
  console.log(`   الموضوع:  تأكيد حجزك في Lumière — طاولة رقم ${data.tableNumber}`);
  console.log(`   المعرّف:  ${data.reservationId}`);
  console.log(line);
  console.log("📄 محتوى HTML (مقتطف):");
  console.log(html.slice(0, 400) + "...");
  console.log(line);
  console.log("💡 للتبديل إلى Resend: أضف EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend في .env\n");

  return { success: true, messageId: `console-${Date.now()}` };
}</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><code>async</code> even though there's no <code>await</code> — because the caller awaits it. Making it sync would force a different calling convention per provider. <strong>Uniform interface wins.</strong></li>
        <li><code>html.slice(0, 400)</code> — truncates the HTML preview. Full HTML is thousands of characters; dumping it would drown the terminal.</li>
        <li><code>messageId: \`console-${Date.now()}\`</code> — mimics a real provider's response. Callers depending on a <code>messageId</code> keep working.</li>
      </ul>

    <section id="facade">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> send.ts Facade — Provider Selection</h2>
      <pre><code>import { render } from "@react-email/components";
import { ReservationConfirmation } from "./templates/ReservationConfirmation";
import { sendViaConsole } from "./providers/console";
import type {
  EmailProviderName, ReservationEmailData, SendEmailResult,
} from "./types";

function getProvider(): EmailProviderName {
  const provider = process.env.EMAIL_PROVIDER as EmailProviderName | undefined;
  return provider ?? "console";
}

export async function sendReservationConfirmation(
  data: ReservationEmailData
): Promise&lt;SendEmailResult&gt; {
  try {
    const html = await render(
      ReservationConfirmation({
        guestName: data.guestName,
        reservationId: data.reservationId,
        tableNumber: data.tableNumber,
        reservationDate: data.reservationDate,
        guestsCount: data.guestsCount,
      })
    );

    const provider = getProvider();

    switch (provider) {
      case "console":
        return await sendViaConsole(data, html);

      case "resend":
        console.warn("[email] Resend provider not implemented yet, falling back to console");
        return await sendViaConsole(data, html);

      default:
        return { success: false, error: `مزوّد إيميل غير معروف: ${provider}` };
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[sendReservationConfirmation] error:", error);
    return { success: false, error: "فشل تجهيز الإيميل" };
  }
}</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><code>render()</code> — React Email's core function. Converts a React element tree into an HTML string. Runs on the server; zero client bytes.</li>
        <li><code>process.env.EMAIL_PROVIDER as EmailProviderName | undefined</code> — <code>process.env</code> values are always <code>string | undefined</code>. The cast narrows the type; runtime validation happens in the <code>switch default</code> case.</li>
        <li><code>provider ?? "console"</code> — safe default if <code>.env</code> is missing the key.</li>
        <li><code>default:</code> case — defensive. If <code>.env</code> contains a typo (<code>EMAIL_PROVIDER=consle</code>), the return shape is still <code>SendEmailResult</code> with a clear error.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="env">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> .env Configuration</h2>
      <pre><code># ─── Email Provider ───
# console = print to terminal (development)
# resend  = real delivery (requires API key)
EMAIL_PROVIDER=console</code></pre>
      <p><strong>HOW:</strong> <code>send.ts</code> reads <code>process.env.EMAIL_PROVIDER</code> at call time.</p>
      <p><strong>WHY runtime read:</strong> Unlike some config that is read once at boot, this read happens per email. In development, you can flip the provider by editing <code>.env</code> and — thanks to Next.js hot-reloading the environment — the next submission uses the new provider without restarting the server.</p>
    </section>

      <h2><span class="num">16</span> Wiring the Email into createReservation</h2>
      <pre><code>import { sendReservationConfirmation } from "@/lib/email/send";
// ... other imports

    // ─── Save reservation (primary priority) ───
    const reservation = await prisma.reservation.create({
      data: { /* ... */ },
    });

    // ─── Send confirmation email (never blocks the save) ───
    try {
      const emailResult = await sendReservationConfirmation({
        to: data.guestEmail,
        guestName: data.guestName,
        reservationId: reservation.id,
        tableNumber: bestTable.number,
        reservationDate,
        guestsCount: data.guestsCount,
      });

      if (!emailResult.success) {
        console.error(
          `[createReservation] Email failed for ${reservation.id}:`,
          emailResult.error
        );
      }
    } catch (emailError) {
      console.error("[createReservation] Email exception:", emailError);
    }

    return { success: true, reservationId: reservation.id, tableNumber: bestTable.number };</code></pre>

    <section id="failsafe">
      <h2><span class="num">17</span> Fail-Safe Design — Nested try/catch</h2>
      <p><strong>The two-layer protection:</strong></p>
      <div class="failsafe">
        <div class="failsafe-outer">
          <div class="failsafe-outer-title">OUTER try / catch</div>
          <div class="failsafe-row">Wraps ALL database operations</div>
          <div class="failsafe-row">If it catches: reservation failed → return <code>{ success: false }</code></div>
          <div class="failsafe-inner">
            <div class="failsafe-inner-title">INNER try / catch</div>
            <div class="failsafe-row">Wraps ONLY the email send</div>
            <div class="failsafe-row">If it catches: reservation <strong>SUCCEEDED</strong>, log the error silently, do NOT return success: false</div>
          </div>
          <div class="failsafe-row" style="margin-top:0.75rem">Return: <code>{ success: true }</code> — reservation is safe</div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Failure scenario</th><th>Correct outcome</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Database write fails</td><td><code>success: false</code> — user must retry</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Email provider fails, DB succeeded</td><td><code>success: true</code> — reservation is safe</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <p><strong>Why the customer must not see the email failure:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>The reservation <strong>exists</strong> in the database.</li>
        <li>The admin can manually resend the email.</li>
        <li>Showing an error to the user creates confusion ("Is my table booked?").</li>
      </ul>

      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Anti-pattern avoided</strong>
        <pre style="margin:0.5rem 0 0;background:transparent;border:none;color:inherit;padding:0"><code style="background:transparent;color:inherit;padding:0">// ❌ Bad pattern
const reservation = await prisma.reservation.create(...);
await sendReservationConfirmation(...);   // If this throws → outer catch → success: false
return { success: true };</code></pre>
        Without the inner try/catch, an email failure would bubble up to the outer handler and incorrectly report the reservation as failed.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="contact">
      <h2><span class="num">19</span> Contact Constants — lib/constants/contact.ts</h2>
      <pre><code>export const CONTACT = {
  // WhatsApp number in international format, no "+", no spaces
  // Example: 201001234567 (Egypt)
  whatsappNumber: "201001234567",

  whatsappDefaultMessage:
    "مرحباً Lumière! أرغب في الاستفسار عن حجز طاولة.",

  email: "hello@lumiere.example",
  phone: "+20 100 123 4567",
  address: "القاهرة، مصر",
} as const;

export function getWhatsAppLink(message?: string): string {
  const text = encodeURIComponent(message ?? CONTACT.whatsappDefaultMessage);
  return `https://wa.me/${CONTACT.whatsappNumber}?text=${text}`;
}</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><code>as const</code> — freezes the object literal. <code>CONTACT.whatsappNumber</code> is typed as the literal <code>"201001234567"</code>, not <code>string</code>. Catches typos.</li>
        <li><code>whatsappNumber</code> — the <code>wa.me</code> format requires <strong>no</strong> <code>+</code>, <strong>no</strong> spaces, <strong>no</strong> dashes. Just digits with country code.</li>
        <li><code>getWhatsAppLink()</code> — accepts an optional custom message. When called with no argument, uses the default.</li>
        <li><code>encodeURIComponent</code> — Arabic text and spaces must be URL-encoded. <code>مرحباً</code> becomes <code>%D9%85%D8%B1%D8%AD%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%8B</code>. Without this, WhatsApp would receive garbled text.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="wa-deep">
      <h2><span class="num">21</span> WhatsApp Button Deep-Dive</h2>
      <h3>target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer"</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>target="_blank"</code> — opens WhatsApp Web in a new tab, preserving the restaurant site in the original tab.</li>
        <li><code>rel="noopener"</code> — prevents the new tab from accessing <code>window.opener</code> (a class of phishing / tab-nabbing attacks).</li>
        <li><code>rel="noreferrer"</code> — hides the referrer URL from WhatsApp. Privacy best practice.</li>
        <li><strong>Both attributes are mandatory</strong> when using <code>target="_blank"</code>.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>fixed bottom-6 left-6 z-50</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>fixed</code> — position relative to viewport, unaffected by scrolling.</li>
        <li><code>bottom-6 left-6</code> — 24px from bottom-left corner.</li>
        <li><strong>Why left, not right:</strong> In RTL layouts, the "natural" empty corner shifts. WhatsApp buttons in Arabic UIs conventionally sit bottom-left.</li>
        <li><code>z-50</code> — highest Tailwind z-index tier. Stays above modals, navbars, and images.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>bg-[#25D366] and hover:bg-[#1ebe5a]</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>[#25D366]</code> — arbitrary-value syntax. Bypasses the theme palette for this one case.</li>
        <li><strong>Why not add to @theme:</strong> This color is WhatsApp's brand identity, not Lumière's. Adding it to the theme would be semantically wrong.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>hidden md:inline</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>The text label "تواصل معنا" appears only on screens ≥ 768px.</li>
        <li><strong>Why:</strong> On mobile, the round icon alone is clear; extra text wastes screen space.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>aria-label and aria-hidden</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>aria-label</code> on the anchor — screen readers announce "تواصل معنا عبر واتساب" even when the text is hidden.</li>
        <li><code>aria-hidden</code> on the <code>&lt;svg&gt;</code> — prevents the SVG from being read twice.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="layout-int">
      <h2><span class="num">22</span> Layout Integration</h2>
      <pre><code>import type { Metadata } from "next";
import "./globals.css";
import { Navbar } from "@/components/layout/Navbar";
import { WhatsAppButton } from "@/components/layout/WhatsAppButton";

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: "Lumière | مطعم Lumière",
  description: "مطعم Lumière — تجربة طعام استثنائية",
};

export default function RootLayout({ children }: LayoutProps&lt;"/"&gt;) {
  return (
    &lt;html lang="ar" dir="rtl" className="h-full antialiased"&gt;
      &lt;body className="min-h-full flex flex-col"&gt;
        &lt;Navbar /&gt;
        &lt;main className="flex-1"&gt;{children}&lt;/main&gt;
        &lt;WhatsAppButton /&gt;
      &lt;/body&gt;
    &lt;/html&gt;
  );
}</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li>Mounted once at the layout level → appears on <strong>every page</strong> (home, menu, item detail, reservation, 404).</li>
        <li>Positioned via <code>fixed</code> — its DOM order doesn't affect visual position.</li>
        <li>Placing it after <code>&lt;main&gt;</code> keeps the DOM in semantic order (main content first, floating widgets after).</li>
        <li><strong>This component is a Server Component:</strong> No state, no events, no hooks. Just a static <code>&lt;a&gt;</code> tag with a link. <strong>Zero JavaScript ships to the browser for this button.</strong></li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="flow">
      <h2><span class="num">23</span> Request Data Flow — Full Trace</h2>
      <div class="flow">
        <div class="flow-step">1. User on /reserve fills form → clicks "تأكيد الحجز"</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">2. Client Component calls createReservation(formData)</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-label">─── SERVER BOUNDARY ───</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">3. Server Action executes:<br>a. Zod validates input<br>b. Prisma queries tables within ±3h window<br>c. findBestTable() returns optimal table</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">4. Prisma INSERTs reservation row</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">5. Inner try/catch: sendReservationConfirmation()<br>i. render() converts React template → HTML string<br>ii. getProvider() reads EMAIL_PROVIDER=console<br>iii. sendViaConsole() prints to terminal</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step success">6. Return { success: true, reservationId, tableNumber }</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-label">─── CLIENT BOUNDARY ───</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step success">7. Success screen replaces form</div>
      </div>
      <p><strong>Boundary rationale:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>Server Action input/output serialization is handled by Next.js transparently.</li>
        <li>The email dispatch happens <strong>after</strong> the database write — the reservation is durable before any network call.</li>
        <li>The inner try/catch isolates the network operation from the transactional operation.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">25</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Missing <code>dotenv/config</code> in script</td><td><code>Environment variable not found</code></td><td>Add <code>import "dotenv/config"</code> as first line</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Preview</code> with <code>{number}</code></td><td><code>Type 'number' is not assignable...</code></td><td>Use <code>{`text ${value}`}</code> template literal</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Email failure blocks save</td><td>Reservation not persisted</td><td>Add inner <code>try / catch</code> around email</td></tr>
          <tr><td>WhatsApp link shows <code>%20</code></td><td>Message not decoded</td><td>Ensure <code>encodeURIComponent</code> is applied</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>target="_blank"</code> without rel</td><td>Security warning in console</td><td>Add <code>rel="noopener noreferrer"</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Button covers content</td><td>Floating over text</td><td>Ensure <code>z-50</code> is set</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Committing <code>email-preview.html</code></td><td>Repo pollution</td><td>Add to <code>.gitignore</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Resend provider placeholder</td><td>Console warning "not implemented"</td><td>Expected — deferred to future session</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <header class="hero">
      <div class="kicker">Phase 07 · Authentication</div>
      <h1>Auth.js v5, Credentials Provider &amp; Role-Based Access</h1>
      <p class="lede">Build a complete authentication system from scratch — no Google OAuth, no paid services, no black boxes. Uses Auth.js v5 with credentials, bcrypt password hashing, JWT sessions, Edge middleware, and a User table with role-based access.</p>
      <div class="stack">
        <span>Auth.js v5</span><span>Credentials</span><span>Bcrypt</span>
        <span>JWT Sessions</span><span>Edge Middleware</span><span>RBAC</span>
      </div>
    </header>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal:</strong> Protect the admin dashboard behind a real login system that requires zero external services.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li><code>User</code> model in <code>schema.prisma</code> with <code>email</code>, <code>passwordHash</code>, <code>role</code>, <code>isActive</code>.</li>
        <li><code>src/lib/auth/password.ts</code> — bcrypt hash + verify utilities.</li>
        <li><code>src/auth.config.ts</code> — Edge-safe Auth.js configuration.</li>
        <li><code>src/auth.ts</code> — Node-only Auth.js config extending the above.</li>
        <li><code>src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts</code> — HTTP bridge.</li>
        <li><code>src/components/auth/LoginForm.tsx</code> — RTL Arabic login form.</li>
        <li><code>src/app/login/page.tsx</code> — login page with redirect-if-authenticated.</li>
        <li><code>src/middleware.ts</code> — protects <code>/admin/*</code> at the Edge.</li>
        <li><code>scripts/create-admin.ts</code> — idempotent admin seeder.</li>
        <li><code>src/types/next-auth.d.ts</code> — TypeScript augmentation for <code>session.user.id</code> and <code>role</code>.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="decision">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Architectural Decision — Auth Strategy</h2>
      <p><strong>Three questions, three decisions:</strong></p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Question</th><th>Options</th><th>Chosen</th><th>Rationale</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><strong>Who signs in?</strong></td><td>Credentials / OAuth / Magic Link</td><td><strong>Credentials only</strong></td><td>Only admins need accounts; zero external dependencies</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>How to store sessions?</strong></td><td>JWT / Database</td><td><strong>JWT</strong></td><td>No <code>Session</code> table, no per-request DB lookup</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Need PrismaAdapter?</strong></td><td>Yes / No</td><td><strong>No</strong></td><td>Adapter targets OAuth tables we don't use</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Deployment architecture</strong>
        <ul style="margin:0.5rem 0 0">
          <li>No Google Cloud console setup.</li>
          <li>No Resend API key required (for login).</li>
          <li>No <code>Account</code>, <code>Session</code>, or <code>VerificationToken</code> tables.</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="comparison">
      <h2><span class="num">3</span> Credentials vs OAuth vs Magic Link</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Provider</th><th>Signup Flow</th><th>External Service</th><th>Card Required</th><th>Fits Lumière?</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><strong>Credentials</strong></td><td>Email + password</td><td>None</td><td>No</td><td>✅ Yes</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Google OAuth</td><td>Google popup</td><td>Google Cloud</td><td>No (but console setup)</td><td>❌ Overkill</td></tr>
          <tr><td>GitHub OAuth</td><td>GitHub popup</td><td>GitHub</td><td>No (but console setup)</td><td>❌ Wrong audience</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Magic Link</td><td>Email link</td><td>Resend/SMTP</td><td>Yes for production</td><td>❌ Needs paid tier</td></tr>
          <tr><td>SMS OTP</td><td>SMS code</td><td>Twilio</td><td>Yes</td><td>❌ Paid</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> Credentials only. Restaurant staff get an email and password from the owner. Guests never register.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="sessions">
      <h2><span class="num">4</span> JWT vs Database Sessions</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Feature</th><th>JWT</th><th>Database Sessions</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Storage</td><td>Encrypted cookie</td><td>Row in <code>Session</code> table</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Per-request DB hit</td><td>None</td><td>One <code>SELECT</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Instant revocation</td><td>No</td><td>Yes</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Scaling</td><td>Zero state</td><td>Shared DB required</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Chosen</strong></td><td>✅</td><td>—</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Rationale:</strong> For a single-restaurant dashboard with a handful of staff, JWT is optimal. Revocation isn't critical — a role change or password reset takes effect on next login. If a session must be killed immediately, rotating <code>AUTH_SECRET</code> invalidates all JWTs at once.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="adapter">
      <h2><span class="num">5</span> Why NO PrismaAdapter?</h2>
      <p><strong>What PrismaAdapter adds:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li><code>Account</code> table — links OAuth accounts to users.</li>
        <li><code>Session</code> table — server-side sessions.</li>
        <li><code>VerificationToken</code> table — Magic Link tokens.</li>
      </ul>
      <p><strong>Why we skip it:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>We use <strong>Credentials</strong> → no <code>Account</code> needed.</li>
        <li>We use <strong>JWT</strong> → no <code>Session</code> table needed.</li>
        <li>We use <strong>no Magic Link</strong> → no <code>VerificationToken</code> needed.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Result</strong>
        Three fewer tables, zero adapter imports, no stale <code>@auth/prisma-adapter</code> initialization cost. The package remains installed (harmless) but unused.
      </div>
    </section>
