    <section id="user-model">
      <h2><span class="num">8</span> User Model — schema.prisma</h2>
      <pre><code>model User {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  email        String   @unique
  passwordHash String
  name         String
  role         String   @default("STAFF")
  isActive     Boolean  @default(true)
  lastLoginAt  DateTime?
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  @@map("users")
}</code></pre>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Purpose</th><th>Security Note</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>id</code></td><td>Primary key (CUID)</td><td>Sortable, collision-resistant</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>email</code></td><td>Login identifier</td><td><code>@unique</code> prevents duplicates</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>passwordHash</code></td><td><strong>Bcrypt hash</strong> (60 chars)</td><td>Never plain text; name reminds developers</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>name</code></td><td>Display name</td><td>Shown in Navbar and dashboard</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>role</code></td><td><code>ADMIN</code> or <code>STAFF</code></td><td>Defaults to lowest privilege</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>isActive</code></td><td>Disable without delete</td><td>Terminated employees</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>lastLoginAt</code></td><td>Audit trail</td><td>Fires on successful login</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Security-first default</strong>
        <code>role: "STAFF"</code> — even if a bug forgets to set a role, the least-privilege value applies.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="types">
      <h2><span class="num">9</span> TypeScript Augmentation — next-auth.d.ts</h2>
      <pre><code>import type { DefaultSession } from "next-auth";

declare module "next-auth" {
  interface Session {
    user: {
      id: string;
      role: string;
    } &amp; DefaultSession["user"];
  }

  interface User {
    role: string;
  }
}

declare module "next-auth/jwt" {
  interface JWT {
    id: string;
    role: string;
  }
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>What <code>declaration merging</code> does:</strong> Extends Auth.js's built-in <code>Session</code>, <code>User</code>, and <code>JWT</code> interfaces. Enables <code>session.user.role</code> and <code>session.user.id</code> across the app without <code>as</code> casts everywhere.</p>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Auth.js v5 beta caveat</strong>
        The <code>JWT</code> interface augments less reliably than <code>Session</code> in v5 beta. In the <code>session()</code> callback, we use a single <code>token as { id: string; role: string }</code> cast to bridge the gap. Documented as a Polish item for when v5 stabilizes.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="bcrypt">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> Bcrypt Concepts — How Hashing Works</h2>
      <p><strong>Why hashing (not encryption):</strong> Encryption is reversible — decrypt to get the original. Hashing is one-way — impossible to reverse. A leaked database of bcrypt hashes is effectively useless to attackers.</p>

      <h3>Bcrypt parameters</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Value</th><th>Why</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><strong>Salt</strong></td><td>128-bit random</td><td>Unique per password → same password produces different hashes</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Rounds</strong></td><td>10 → 2¹⁰ = 1,024 iterations</td><td>~50-400ms — slow enough to stop brute force, fast enough for users</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Output</strong></td><td>60 chars</td><td>Fixed length regardless of input password length</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>Salt is embedded in the hash</h3>
      <pre><code>$2b$10$NvjaWGsGkR9bq54pMMeZauWy3UIgHPYsTdwwX/mf6LqCyB9YauCW
 │   │  └─── 22-char salt + hash payload
 │   └────── cost factor
 └────────── algorithm version (2b)</code></pre>

      <h3>Verification flow</h3>
      <ol>
        <li>Extract salt from stored hash.</li>
        <li>Hash the candidate password with the same salt.</li>
        <li>Compare byte-for-byte. If equal → match.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="password">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> password.ts — Full File</h2>
      <pre><code>import bcrypt from "bcryptjs";

export const BCRYPT_ROUNDS = 10;
export const MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8;

export async function hashPassword(plainPassword: string): Promise&lt;string&gt; {
  if (plainPassword.length &lt; MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH) {
    throw new Error(
      `كلمة السر قصيرة جداً (الحد الأدنى ${MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH} أحرف)`
    );
  }
  return bcrypt.hash(plainPassword, BCRYPT_ROUNDS);
}

export async function verifyPassword(
  plainPassword: string,
  storedHash: string
): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {
  try {
    return await bcrypt.compare(plainPassword, storedHash);
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><code>bcryptjs</code> (not <code>bcrypt</code>) — pure JavaScript, no <code>node-gyp</code> compilation on Windows.</li>
        <li><code>BCRYPT_ROUNDS = 10</code> — exported constant, changes propagate everywhere.</li>
        <li><code>MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8</code> — enforces NIST/OWASP minimum at the utility layer.</li>
        <li><code>verifyPassword</code> wraps <code>compare</code> in <code>try/catch</code> — malformed hashes return <code>false</code> instead of throwing.</li>
        <li>Both functions are <code>async</code> — bcrypt is CPU-intensive; async keeps the event loop responsive.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="config">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> auth.config.ts — Edge-Safe Config</h2>
      <pre><code>import type { NextAuthConfig } from "next-auth";

export const authConfig: NextAuthConfig = {
  session: {
    strategy: "jwt",
    maxAge: 30 * 24 * 60 * 60, // 30 days
  },
  pages: {
    signIn: "/login",
    error: "/login",
  },
  providers: [], // Populated in auth.ts
  callbacks: {
    async jwt({ token, user }) {
      if (user) {
        token.id = user.id as string;
        token.role = user.role;
      }
      return token;
    },
    async session({ session, token }) {
      const t = token as { id: string; role: string };
      session.user.id = t.id;
      session.user.role = t.role;
      return session;
    },
    authorized({ auth, request }) {
      const isOnAdmin = request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith("/admin");
      if (isOnAdmin) return !!auth;
      return true;
    },
  },
};</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why this file is Edge-safe:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>No <code>prisma</code> import.</li>
        <li>No <code>bcrypt</code> import.</li>
        <li>No <code>node:*</code> imports.</li>
        <li>Only Auth.js types and callbacks that operate on plain objects.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="edge">
      <h2><span class="num">14</span> The Edge Runtime Problem — Why Two Files?</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Symptom observed during development</strong>
        <code>Failed to load external module node:path: TypeError: Native module not found: node:path</code> at <code>src/lib/prisma.ts:8:1</code>
      </div>
      <p><strong>The chain that broke:</strong></p>
      <pre><code>middleware.ts (Edge Runtime)
    └── imports auth.ts
            └── imports prisma.ts
                    └── imports 'node:path'  ❌ Edge can't load Node built-ins</code></pre>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Capability</th><th>Edge Runtime</th><th>Node Runtime</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>node:path</code>, <code>node:fs</code>, <code>node:crypto</code></td><td>❌</td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Native <code>.dll</code>/<code>.node</code> binaries</td><td>❌</td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Network APIs (<code>fetch</code>, <code>Request</code>)</td><td>✅</td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Run globally, low latency</td><td>✅</td><td>❌</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>The fix — split configuration</strong>
        <code>auth.config.ts</code> — Edge-safe (pages, session, callbacks). <code>auth.ts</code> — Node-only (extends config, adds Prisma-backed Credentials). Middleware imports only <code>auth.config.ts</code>. Result: Edge bundle shrinks from ~100 MB (with Prisma engine) to a few KB.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="auth">
      <h2><span class="num">15</span> auth.ts — Node Runtime Config</h2>
      <pre><code>import NextAuth from "next-auth";
import Credentials from "next-auth/providers/credentials";
import { z } from "zod";
import { prisma } from "@/lib/prisma";
import { verifyPassword } from "@/lib/auth/password";
import { authConfig } from "./auth.config";

const credentialsSchema = z.object({
  email: z.string().trim().toLowerCase().email(),
  password: z.string().min(1),
});

export const { handlers, signIn, signOut, auth } = NextAuth({
  ...authConfig,
  providers: [
    Credentials({
      credentials: {
        email: { label: "البريد", type: "email" },
        password: { label: "كلمة السر", type: "password" },
      },
      async authorize(rawCredentials) {
        const parsed = credentialsSchema.safeParse(rawCredentials);
        if (!parsed.success) return null;

        const { email, password } = parsed.data;
        const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });
        if (!user) return null;
        if (!user.isActive) return null;

        const isValid = await verifyPassword(password, user.passwordHash);
        if (!isValid) return null;

        prisma.user.update({
          where: { id: user.id },
          data: { lastLoginAt: new Date() },
        }).catch(() =&gt; {});

        return {
          id: user.id, email: user.email,
          name: user.name, role: user.role,
        };
      },
    }),
  ],
});</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Four exports from NextAuth():</strong></p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Export</th><th>Used In</th><th>Purpose</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>handlers</code></td><td><code>app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts</code></td><td>HTTP GET/POST handlers</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>auth</code></td><td>Server Components, Server Actions</td><td>Read session server-side</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>signIn</code></td><td>Server Actions (rarely)</td><td>Programmatic sign-in</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>signOut</code></td><td>Server Actions</td><td>Programmatic sign-out</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="authorize">
      <h2><span class="num">16</span> authorize() Deep-Dive — Security Layers</h2>
      <p><strong>The five returns of <code>null</code>:</strong></p>
      <div class="sec-layers">
        <div class="sec-row">
          <div class="sec-check">1</div>
          <div class="sec-body">
            <code>if (!parsed.success) return null;</code>
            <div class="why">Malformed input — Zod catches bad shapes first.</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="sec-row">
          <div class="sec-check">2</div>
          <div class="sec-body">
            <code>if (!user) return null;</code>
            <div class="why">Email not found — cannot leak whether the account exists.</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="sec-row">
          <div class="sec-check">3</div>
          <div class="sec-body">
            <code>if (!user.isActive) return null;</code>
            <div class="why">Account disabled — terminated employees cannot log in.</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="sec-row">
          <div class="sec-check">4</div>
          <div class="sec-body">
            <code>if (!isValid) return null;</code>
            <div class="why">Wrong password — bcrypt compare returned false.</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="sec-final">→ Auth.js converts all nulls into a generic "CredentialsSignin" error</div>
      </div>

      <h3>This prevents User Enumeration Attacks</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Different messages</th><th>Same message (ours)</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Attacker learns which emails exist</td><td>Attacker learns nothing</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Can target known accounts</td><td>Must guess blindly</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>Side effect — lastLoginAt update</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Fired but <strong>not awaited</strong> (<code>fire-and-forget</code>).</li>
        <li><code>.catch(() =&gt; {})</code> swallows errors — a logging failure must not block login.</li>
        <li>Runs in parallel with the response serialization.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="handler">
      <h2><span class="num">17</span> Route Handler — Two Lines</h2>
      <pre><code>import { handlers } from "@/auth";

export const { GET, POST } = handlers;</code></pre>
      <p><strong>That's the entire file.</strong> No logic here — everything lives in <code>auth.ts</code>.</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Route</th><th>Method</th><th>Purpose</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>/api/auth/session</code></td><td>GET</td><td>Returns current session JSON</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/api/auth/csrf</code></td><td>GET</td><td>Generates CSRF token</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/api/auth/providers</code></td><td>GET</td><td>Lists configured providers</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/api/auth/signin</code></td><td>GET</td><td>Redirects to <code>/login</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/api/auth/signin/credentials</code></td><td>POST</td><td>Processes login</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/api/auth/signout</code></td><td>POST</td><td>Clears session cookie</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/api/auth/callback/credentials</code></td><td>POST</td><td>Internal callback</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>File naming:</strong> <code>[...nextauth]</code> is a catch-all dynamic segment. One folder handles all seven routes above.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="login-form">
      <h2><span class="num">18</span> LoginForm — Client Component</h2>
      <pre><code>"use client";

import { useState, type FormEvent } from "react";
import { signIn } from "next-auth/react";
import { useRouter, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation";
import { FormField, inputClasses } from "@/components/ui/FormField";

type Result =
  | { kind: "idle" }
  | { kind: "submitting" }
  | { kind: "error"; message: string };

export function LoginForm() {
  const router = useRouter();
  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
  const callbackUrl = searchParams.get("callbackUrl") ?? "/admin";

  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
  const [result, setResult] = useState&lt;Result&gt;({ kind: "idle" });

  async function handleSubmit(e: FormEvent) {
    e.preventDefault();
    setResult({ kind: "submitting" });

    const response = await signIn("credentials", {
      email, password, redirect: false,
    });

    if (!response || response.error) {
      setResult({
        kind: "error",
        message: "البريد الإلكتروني أو كلمة السر غير صحيحة",
      });
      return;
    }

    router.push(callbackUrl);
    router.refresh();
  }

  /* JSX continues */
}</code></pre>

    <section id="login-deep">
      <h2><span class="num">19</span> LoginForm Deep-Dive — redirect: false</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>redirect</th><th>Behavior on failure</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>true</code> (default)</td><td>Browser jumps to <code>/login?error=CredentialsSignin</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>false</code> (ours)</td><td>Function returns <code>{ error: "..." }</code>; we render Arabic message</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Why we override:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>Auth.js's default error page is English and generic.</li>
        <li>We need Arabic text styled to match Lumière.</li>
        <li>Full control over navigation timing (push then refresh).</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>router.refresh() — the less-obvious necessity</h3>
      <p>After <code>router.push(callbackUrl)</code>, the URL changes but <strong>cached Server Components still hold old session data</strong>. The Navbar won't show the user's name, and any server-side session read returns <code>null</code>.</p>
      <p><code>router.refresh()</code> forces Next.js to re-fetch all Server Components for the current route. Combined with the newly-set JWT cookie, they re-render with the session.</p>
      <pre><code>router.push(callbackUrl);  // navigate first
router.refresh();          // then invalidate</code></pre>
    </section>

    <section id="login-page">
      <h2><span class="num">20</span> /login Page — Server Component Shell</h2>
      <pre><code>import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
import { auth } from "@/auth";
import { LoginForm } from "@/components/auth/LoginForm";

export default async function LoginPage() {
  const session = await auth();
  if (session?.user) {
    redirect("/admin");
  }

  return (
    &lt;div className="min-h-[70vh] flex items-center justify-center px-4 py-12"&gt;

      <p><strong>Why check session in the page:</strong> Redirects already-authenticated users away from login. Prevents "double login" confusion.</p>
      <p><strong>Layout pattern:</strong> Server Component shell wraps the Client form. Only the form's JS hydrates.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="middleware">
      <h2><span class="num">21</span> middleware.ts — Edge Guard</h2>
      <pre><code>import NextAuth from "next-auth";
import { authConfig } from "./auth.config";

export default NextAuth(authConfig).auth;

export const config = {
  matcher: ["/admin/:path*"],
};</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why not <code>import { auth } from "@/auth"</code>:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>That module imports Prisma.</li>
        <li>Prisma cannot load in Edge Runtime.</li>
        <li>We instantiate a <strong>fresh</strong> <code>NextAuth(authConfig)</code> — Edge-safe by construction.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>How redirection happens</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>The <code>authorized</code> callback (in <code>auth.config.ts</code>) returns <code>false</code> for unauthenticated <code>/admin</code> requests.</li>
        <li>Auth.js <strong>automatically</strong> redirects to <code>pages.signIn</code> (<code>/login</code>).</li>
        <li><code>callbackUrl</code> is preserved via Auth.js's internal cookie.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="matcher">
      <h2><span class="num">22</span> Matcher Scoping</h2>
      <pre><code>matcher: ["/admin/:path*"]</code></pre>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Path</th><th>Matched?</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>/admin</code></td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/admin/reservations</code></td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/admin/menu/items</code></td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/menu</code></td><td>❌</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/api/auth/*</code></td><td>❌</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>/_next/static/*</code></td><td>❌</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Performance rationale</strong>
        Without <code>matcher</code>, middleware runs on every request — including CSS, JS, and auth endpoints (causing loops). The matcher restricts it to <code>/admin</code>.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="seed">
      <h2><span class="num">23</span> create-admin.ts — Idempotent Seeder</h2>
      <pre><code>import "dotenv/config";
import { PrismaClient } from "../src/generated/prisma/client";
import { hashPassword } from "../src/lib/auth/password";

const prisma = new PrismaClient();

const ADMIN_DATA = {
  email: "admin@lumiere.com",
  password: "Admin@Lumiere2026",
  name: "مدير Lumière",
  role: "ADMIN",
};

async function main() {
  const passwordHash = await hashPassword(ADMIN_DATA.password);

  const admin = await prisma.user.upsert({
    where: { email: ADMIN_DATA.email },
    update: { passwordHash, name: ADMIN_DATA.name, role: ADMIN_DATA.role, isActive: true },
    create: { email: ADMIN_DATA.email, passwordHash, name: ADMIN_DATA.name, role: ADMIN_DATA.role, isActive: true },
  });

  console.log("✅ تم بنجاح:");
  console.log(`   ID:      ${admin.id}`);
  console.log(`   البريد:  ${admin.email}`);
}

main()
  .catch((error) =&gt; { console.error("❌ خطأ:", error); process.exit(1); })
  .finally(async () =&gt; { await prisma.$disconnect(); });</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why this script is separate from <code>prisma/seed.ts</code>:</strong></p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Concern</th><th>seed.ts</th><th>create-admin.ts</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Deletes data first</td><td>✅ Yes</td><td>❌ No</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Idempotent</td><td>No</td><td>✅ Yes (<code>upsert</code>)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Safe to re-run</td><td>❌</td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Purpose</td><td>Demo data</td><td>First admin</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong><code>upsert</code> semantics:</strong> create if missing, update if present. Running the script twice updates the admin's password rather than failing on a unique constraint.</p>

    <section id="flow">
      <h2><span class="num">24</span> Auth Flow Trace — Login with Valid Credentials</h2>
      <div class="flow">
        <div class="flow-step">1. User opens /login</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step">2. Submits admin@lumiere.com / Admin@Lumiere2026</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">3. signIn("credentials", { redirect: false }) fires</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-label">─── HTTP POST /api/auth/callback/credentials ───</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">4. Route Handler → Auth.js:<br>a. Read AUTH_SECRET from .env<br>b. Execute authorize() with email + password<br>c. Zod validates shape</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">5. prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } })</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">6. verifyPassword(password, user.passwordHash) → true</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">7. Fire-and-forget update lastLoginAt<br>8. Return { id, email, name, role }</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">9. Auth.js creates JWT with those fields<br>10. Sets encrypted cookie: authjs.session-token</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step success">11. Responds 200 to the client</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-label">─── CLIENT ───</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step code">12. router.push("/admin") → middleware intercepts<br>13. middleware reads JWT cookie → authorized() → true</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow"></div>
        <div class="flow-step success">14. router.refresh() invalidates Server Component caches</div>
      </div>
      <p><strong>Boundary guarantees:</strong></p>
      <ul>
        <li>Passwords never leave the server in plaintext (only over HTTPS in production).</li>
        <li>JWT cookie is HTTP-only + Secure (in production) + SameSite=Lax.</li>
        <li>Prisma is never imported into client bundles.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">26</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>EPERM: query_engine-windows.dll.node</code></td><td><code>npx prisma generate</code> fails</td><td>Stop <code>npm run dev</code> + <code>prisma studio</code> first; delete <code>.tmp*</code> files</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Type <code>unknown</code> not assignable to <code>string</code></td><td><code>session.user.id = token.id</code> fails</td><td>Cast: <code>const t = token as { id: string; role: string }</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Failed to load node:path</code></td><td>Edge runtime error on <code>/admin</code></td><td>Split into <code>auth.config.ts</code> (Edge) + <code>auth.ts</code> (Node)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Middleware stale chunk</td><td>Error persists after edit</td><td><code>Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .next</code> + restart dev</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>AUTH_SECRET missing</code></td><td>Auth.js throws on startup</td><td>Add secret to <code>.env</code> and restart dev server</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Redirect loop on <code>/login</code></td><td>Middleware matches <code>/login</code></td><td>Narrow <code>matcher</code> to <code>["/admin/:path*"]</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Password hash looks different every run</td><td>Salt working correctly</td><td>Not a bug — expected behavior</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>CredentialsSignin</code> error in terminal</td><td>Auth.js logs failed attempts</td><td>Not a bug — security audit trail</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="glossary">
      <h2><span class="num">28</span> Technical Abbreviations Glossary</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Abbr.</th><th>Full Form</th><th>Plain-English Meaning</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>API</td><td>Application Programming Interface</td><td>Contract for program-to-program calls</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Auth.js</td><td>(library)</td><td>Next.js authentication library (formerly NextAuth)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>bcrypt</td><td>(cryptographic algorithm)</td><td>Password-hashing algorithm; deliberately slow</td></tr>
          <tr><td>CRUD</td><td>Create, Read, Update, Delete</td><td>The four basic data operations</td></tr>
          <tr><td>CSRF</td><td>Cross-Site Request Forgery</td><td>Attack where a third-party site submits forms on your behalf</td></tr>
          <tr><td>CUID</td><td>Collision-resistant Unique Identifier</td><td>25-char sortable ID</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Edge Runtime</td><td>(Vercel)</td><td>V8-isolated environment without Node APIs</td></tr>
          <tr><td>FK</td><td>Foreign Key</td><td>Column pointing to another table's PK</td></tr>
          <tr><td>HTTP</td><td>HyperText Transfer Protocol</td><td>Browser-server communication protocol</td></tr>
          <tr><td>JWT</td><td>JSON Web Token</td><td>Self-contained signed session token</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Middleware</td><td>(Next.js)</td><td>Function that intercepts requests before routing</td></tr>
          <tr><td>NIST</td><td>National Institute of Standards and Technology</td><td>US body issuing security guidelines</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ORM</td><td>Object-Relational Mapper</td><td>Translates objects ↔ SQL</td></tr>
          <tr><td>OWASP</td><td>Open Worldwide Application Security Project</td><td>Publishes top-10 security risks</td></tr>
          <tr><td>PK</td><td>Primary Key</td><td>Column uniquely identifying a row</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RSC</td><td>React Server Components</td><td>React components rendered on the server</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RTL</td><td>Right-to-Left</td><td>Text direction for Arabic/Hebrew</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Salt</td><td>(cryptographic)</td><td>Random data appended before hashing</td></tr>
          <tr><td>UI</td><td>User Interface</td><td>What the user sees</td></tr>
          <tr><td>URL</td><td>Uniform Resource Locator</td><td>Web address</td></tr>
          <tr><td>UX</td><td>User Experience</td><td>Overall feel of using the app</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <header class="hero">
      <div class="kicker">Phase 11 · Internationalization</div>
      <div class="flag-row">🇪🇬 🇬🇧 🇫🇷 🇩🇪 🇪🇸</div>
      <h1>Five Locales, One Codebase</h1>
      <p class="lede">Transform a single-language Arabic application into a fully internationalized product supporting Arabic, English, French, German, and Spanish — with automatic RTL/LTR direction switching, locale-prefixed routing, translated emails, localized error messages, and per-locale SEO. managed infrastructure, zero browser extensions, and full type-safety preserved across all 5 locales.</p>
      <div class="stack">
        <span>next-intl v4</span><span>App Router [locale]</span>
        <span>ICU Messages</span><span>RTL/LTR</span>
        <span>Auth.js Integration</span><span>Schema Factories</span>
        <span>Per-Locale SEO</span>
      </div>
    </header>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal:</strong> Make every string in the application locale-aware — from navigation labels and error messages to transactional emails and JSON-LD metadata — without duplicating route files or introducing runtime overhead on the client.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li><strong>5 message files</strong> — <code>ar.json</code>, <code>en.json</code>, <code>fr.json</code>, <code>de.json</code>, <code>es.json</code> — sharing identical key structure.</li>
        <li><strong>Locale-prefixed routing</strong> — every URL becomes <code>/ar/menu</code>, <code>/en/menu</code>, etc.</li>
        <li><strong>Dynamic <code>dir</code> and <code>lang</code></strong> — <code>rtl</code> for Arabic, <code>ltr</code> for the rest.</li>
        <li><strong>LanguageSwitcher</strong> component with real country flags (flagcdn.com).</li>
        <li><strong>Category <code>nameEn</code> migration</strong> — bilingual category names + <code>getLocalizedName()</code> helper.</li>
        <li><strong>Schema factories</strong> — Zod schemas receive a translator and return localized error messages.</li>
        <li><strong>Server Actions i18n</strong> — <code>tError()</code> helper replacing every hardcoded error string.</li>
        <li><strong>Translated email templates</strong> — one React Email template rendering 5 languages.</li>
        <li><strong>Per-locale sitemap and robots</strong> — 75 URLs (15 × 5 locales), 10 admin disallow rules.</li>
        <li><strong>Zero hardcoded UI strings</strong> — every visible text is a translation key.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="decision">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Architectural Decision — Why next-intl</h2>
      <p><strong>The question:</strong> How do we internationalize a Next.js 16 App Router project with Server Components, Server Actions, and Auth.js middleware — without reinventing routing?</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Option</th><th>Verdict</th><th>Why</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><strong>next-intl v4</strong></td><td>✅ Chosen</td><td>Built for App Router · Server Component support · Type-safe keys · Small bundle (~14 KB)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Manual routing</td><td>❌ Rejected</td><td>Reinventing URL parsing, prefix rewriting, cookie handling, and locale detection</td></tr>
          <tr><td>next-i18next</td><td>❌ Rejected</td><td>Built for Pages Router — client-side loading, no RSC support, stale architecture</td></tr>
          <tr><td>react-i18next</td><td>❌ Rejected</td><td>Pure client library — forces "use client" on every page, loses Server Components</td></tr>
          <tr><td>i18next-http-middleware</td><td>❌ Rejected</td><td>Express-style middleware — incompatible with Next.js App Router</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Why this matters for the project</strong>
        The application relies heavily on Server Components to deliver zero-JS HTML. Choosing a client-side library would force every page to hydrate just to display text — a massive regression in performance, bundle size, and SEO.
      </div>

      <h3>The three integration points</h3>
      <div class="layers">
        <div class="layer client"><strong>CLIENT</strong> · <code>NextIntlClientProvider</code> wraps the app — exposes messages to the few Client Components that need them</div>
        <div class="layer edge"><strong>EDGE</strong> · <code>next-intl/middleware</code> detects locale from URL prefix and sets cookies before any request reaches the app</div>
        <div class="layer node"><strong>NODE</strong> · <code>getTranslations()</code> in Server Components / Server Actions — no serialization</div>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="locales">
      <h2><span class="num">3</span> The 5 Locales</h2>
      <p><strong>Default locale:</strong> Arabic (<code>ar</code>) — because the primary market is Egypt and the initial product was Arabic-only.</p>
      <div class="locale-grid">
        <div class="locale-card">
          <div class="lc-flag">🇪🇬</div>
          <div class="lc-code">ar</div>
          <div class="lc-name">العربية</div>
          <div class="lc-dir rtl">RTL</div>
        </div>
        <div class="locale-card">
          <div class="lc-flag">🇬🇧</div>

          <div class="lc-name">English</div>

        </div>

          <div class="lc-flag">🇪🇸</div>
          <div class="lc-code">es</div>
          <div class="lc-name">Español</div>
          <div class="lc-dir">LTR</div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <h3>URL strategy — always prefixed</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>localePrefix</th><th>Behavior</th><th>Chosen?</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>"always"</code></td><td>/ar/menu · /en/menu · /fr/menu</td><td>✅ Yes</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>"as-needed"</code></td><td>/menu · /en/menu (Arabic hidden)</td><td>❌ Ambiguous</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>"never"</code></td><td>Cookie-based only — URLs never change</td><td>❌ Breaks SEO</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Why "always"</strong>
        Explicit locale in every URL means search engines index each language separately, WhatsApp previews match the shared URL, and browser history remembers the user's language. The slight aesthetic cost (visible <code>/en/</code>) is a small price for correct multilingual SEO.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="restructure">
      <h2><span class="num">6</span> The [locale] Restructure</h2>
      <p><strong>The problem:</strong> Every page currently lives at <code>src/app/(public)/menu/page.tsx</code> — a single URL. To support 5 languages, every route must become locale-aware.</p>

      <h3>Before → After</h3>
      <div class="filetree">
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="note">BEFORE — flat app/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="dir">src/app/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-2"><span class="file">layout.tsx</span></div>
        <div class="indent-2"><span class="dir">(public)/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-3"><span class="file">page.tsx</span> · <span class="dir">menu/</span> · <span class="dir">reserve/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-2"><span class="dir">(auth)/login/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-2"><span class="dir">admin/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-2"><span class="dir">api/</span></div>
      </div>
      <div class="filetree">
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="note">AFTER — [locale]/ segment</span></div>
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="dir">src/app/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-2"><span class="file">layout.tsx</span> <span class="note">← passthrough (returns children)</span></div>
        <div class="indent-2"><span class="dir new">[locale]/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-3"><span class="file new">layout.tsx</span> <span class="note">← html/body + dir + provider</span></div>
        <div class="indent-3"><span class="dir">(public)/</span> <span class="dir">(auth)/</span> <span class="dir">admin/</span></div>
        <div class="indent-2"><span class="dir">api/</span> <span class="note">← stays outside (not localized)</span></div>
      </div>

      <h3>Why <code>api/</code> stays outside</h3>
      <p>Route Handlers under <code>/api/</code> are consumed by external systems — mobile apps, webhooks, Postman. Adding a locale prefix (<code>/en/api/menu/items</code>) would be ambiguous: which locale's data should a mobile app fetch? The answer is language-neutral data. So <code>/api/</code> remains at the root, returning raw content regardless of locale.</p>

      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Files moved — 20+ routes</strong>
        Every <code>page.tsx</code>, <code>layout.tsx</code>, <code>loading.tsx</code>, and <code>error.tsx</code> under <code>app/</code> moved one level deeper. Git tracked these as renames (not delete + create) — preserving history.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="routing">
      <h2><span class="num">7</span> i18n/routing.ts — Single Source of Truth</h2>
      <pre><code>import {defineRouting} from 'next-intl/routing';

export const routing = defineRouting({
  locales: ['ar', 'en', 'fr', 'de', 'es'],
  defaultLocale: 'ar',
  localePrefix: 'always'
});

export type Locale = (typeof routing.locales)[number];
export const RTL_LOCALES: Locale[] = ['ar'];</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><strong><code>locales</code></strong> — single array drives routing, sitemap, robots, message loading, and type inference.</li>
        <li><strong><code>defaultLocale</code></strong> — Arabic. Used as fallback when the URL has no locale.</li>
        <li><strong><code>localePrefix: "always"</code></strong> — every URL carries the locale, no exceptions.</li>
        <li><strong><code>Locale</code> type</strong> — TypeScript union of the 5 codes. Adding a 6th locale makes the compiler flag every place that needs updating.</li>
        <li><strong><code>RTL_LOCALES</code></strong> — extracted as a constant. Adding Hebrew or Farsi later means one line change.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>The compiler becomes the checklist</strong>
        When you add <code>it</code> (Italian) to the array, TypeScript will error in <code>messages/it.json</code> (missing), <code>LanguageSwitcher</code> (missing label), and anywhere else that requires handling — no silent gaps.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="request">
      <h2><span class="num">8</span> i18n/request.ts — Message Loading</h2>
      <pre><code>import { getRequestConfig } from "next-intl/server";
import { hasLocale } from "next-intl";
import { routing } from "./routing";

export default getRequestConfig(async ({ requestLocale }) => {
  const requested = await requestLocale;
  const locale = hasLocale(routing.locales, requested)
    ? requested
    : routing.defaultLocale;

  return {
    locale,
    messages: (await import(`../../messages/${locale}.json`)).default,
  };
});</code></pre>
      <ul>
        <li><strong><code>getRequestConfig</code></strong> — called once per request by next-intl. Returns the locale and messages for that request.</li>
        <li><strong><code>hasLocale</code></strong> — type-safe runtime check. If the URL contains <code>/xx/</code>, we fall back to Arabic rather than crashing.</li>
        <li><strong>Dynamic import</strong> — only the current locale's JSON is loaded. The other 4 stay out of the bundle.</li>
        <li><strong>Serverless</strong> — this runs on the server. Messages are streamed as props to <code>NextIntlClientProvider</code>, then reused by Client Components.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="navigation">
      <h2><span class="num">9</span> i18n/navigation.ts — Locale-Aware Links</h2>
      <pre><code>import {createNavigation} from 'next-intl/navigation';
import {routing} from './routing';

export const {Link, redirect, usePathname, useRouter, getPathname} =
  createNavigation(routing);</code></pre>
      <p><strong>The problem:</strong> <code>next/link</code> and <code>next/navigation</code>'s <code>useRouter</code> don't know about <code>[locale]</code>. Using them directly would produce <code>href="/menu"</code> — which has no locale prefix and would trigger a redirect loop through the middleware.</p>
      <p><strong>The fix:</strong> <code>createNavigation</code> returns locale-aware replacements that automatically prefix the current locale.</p>

      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Naive (broken)</th><th>next-intl replacement</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>import Link from "next/link"</code></td><td><code>import { Link } from "@/i18n/navigation"</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>useRouter()</code> from <code>next/navigation</code></td><td><code>useRouter()</code> from <code>@/i18n/navigation</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>usePathname()</code> from <code>next/navigation</code></td><td><code>usePathname()</code> from <code>@/i18n/navigation</code> <em>(strips locale)</em></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>redirect()</code> from <code>next/navigation</code></td><td><code>redirect()</code> from <code>@/i18n/navigation</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>The <code>usePathname()</code> magic</strong>
        When you're on <code>/en/menu</code> and switch to French, calling <code>router.replace(pathname, { locale: "fr" })</code> keeps you on <code>/fr/menu</code>. The next-intl version of <code>usePathname()</code> strips the current locale — so you never write <code>pathname.replace("/en", "/fr")</code> manually.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="proxy">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> proxy.ts — Edge Chaining (next-intl + Auth.js)</h2>
      <pre><code>import createMiddleware from 'next-intl/middleware';
import {routing} from './i18n/routing';
import {auth} from '@/auth';

const intlMiddleware = createMiddleware(routing);

export default auth((req) => {
  return intlMiddleware(req);
});

export const config = {
  matcher: ['/((?!api|_next|_vercel|.*\\..*).*)']
};</code></pre>

      <h3>What each layer does</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Layer</th><th>Responsibility</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>auth()</code> wrapper</td><td>Runs Auth.js session check. If a protected route, decides allow / redirect</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>intlMiddleware(req)</code></td><td>Reads URL prefix · sets <code>NEXT_LOCALE</code> cookie · rewrites internally to <code>[locale]/...</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>matcher</code></td><td>Skips static assets (<code>_next</code>), API routes, files with extensions</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Order matters</strong>
        <code>auth()</code> wraps <code>intlMiddleware</code>, not the reverse. Reason: Auth.js needs to run first because it may redirect (unauthenticated → /login). If next-intl ran first and rewrote the URL, Auth.js would see the wrong path.
      </div>

      <h3>The <code>authorized</code> callback fix</h3>
      <p><strong>Broken:</strong> <code>request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith("/admin")</code> — never matches because every path now starts with <code>/ar/</code> or <code>/en/</code>.</p>
      <pre><code>authorized({ auth, request }) {
  const pathname = request.nextUrl.pathname;
  const segments = pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean);
  const isOnAdmin = segments.includes("admin");
  if (isOnAdmin) return !!auth;
  return true;
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why this works:</strong> <code>segments</code> for <code>/en/admin/menu</code> becomes <code>["en", "admin", "menu"]</code> — <code>.includes("admin")</code> is true regardless of locale position.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="edge-split">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> The Edge Runtime Split — Why Two Auth Configs</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Real error encountered</strong>
        <code>Failed to load external module node:path: TypeError: Native module not found: node:path</code> at <code>src/lib/prisma.ts</code>.
      </div>
      <p><strong>The chain that broke:</strong></p>
      <pre><code>proxy.ts (Edge Runtime)
    └── imports auth.ts
            └── imports prisma.ts
                    └── imports 'node:path'   ❌ Edge can't load Node built-ins</code></pre>

      <h3>Two files, two runtimes</h3>
      <div class="filetree">
        <div><span class="file new">src/auth.config.ts</span> <span class="note">← Edge-safe · shared between both worlds</span></div>
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="note">session, pages, callbacks, authorized</span></div>
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="note">no prisma, no bcrypt, no node:*</span></div>
        <div>&nbsp;</div>
        <div><span class="file new">src/auth.ts</span> <span class="note">← Node-only · extends authConfig with Credentials</span></div>
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="note">imports prisma + bcrypt + zod</span></div>
        <div class="indent-1"><span class="note">exports handlers, signIn, signOut, auth</span></div>
      </div>

      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Capability</th><th>Edge Runtime</th><th>Node Runtime</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>node:path</code>, <code>node:fs</code>, <code>node:crypto</code></td><td>❌</td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Native <code>.node</code> binaries (Prisma engine)</td><td>❌</td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Network APIs (<code>fetch</code>, <code>Request</code>)</td><td>✅</td><td>✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Runs globally, ultra-low latency</td><td>✅</td><td>❌</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>What changed in each file</h3>
      <p><strong><code>auth.config.ts</code></strong> — the <code>authorized</code> callback was updated for locale-aware admin detection (section 10).</p>
      <p><strong><code>auth.ts</code></strong> — unchanged. It imports <code>authConfig</code>, spreads it, and adds the <code>Credentials</code> provider with Prisma + bcrypt.</p>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Bundle impact</strong>
        The Edge bundle shrank from ~100 MB (with the Prisma engine included) to a few KB. Cold start at Vercel Edge dropped from ~800 ms to under 50 ms.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="files">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> Translation File Structure</h2>
      <p>Five JSON files with <strong>identical key structure</strong>. Only the string values differ.</p>

      <h3>Top-level namespaces</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Namespace</th><th>Scope</th><th>Approx. keys</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>Navbar</code></td><td>Navigation links</td><td>4</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Home</code></td><td>Hero, Featured, CTA, Location, Reviews section</td><td>25</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Menu</code></td><td>Page header, filters, badges, currency</td><td>9</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Reserve</code></td><td>Form fields, success screen, metadata</td><td>15</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Review</code></td><td>Form, success screen, testimonials section</td><td>20</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>ItemDetail</code></td><td>Single item page + not-found fallback</td><td>7</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Email</code></td><td>Reservation confirmation template</td><td>18</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Admin</code></td><td>Sidebar, overview, 5 CRUD sections, analytics</td><td>~250</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>Errors</code></td><td>~50 validation + business error messages</td><td>~55</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>UI</code></td><td>Loading, error fallback, WhatsApp labels</td><td>7</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>Sample — the <code>Menu</code> namespace across 5 files</h3>
      <pre><code>// ar.json
"Menu": {
  "title": "قائمة Lumière",
  "featuredBadge": "⭐ مميز",
  "currency": "ج.م",
  "details": "التفاصيل ←"
}

// en.json
"Menu": {
  "title": "Lumière Menu",
  "featuredBadge": "⭐ Featured",
  "currency": "EGP",
  "details": "Details →"
}

// fr.json
"Menu": {
  "title": "Menu Lumière",
  "featuredBadge": "⭐ En vedette",
  "currency": "EGP",
  "details": "Détails →"
}</code></pre>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>The arrow direction matters</strong> — in Arabic RTL, "forward" is <code>←</code> (pointing left). In LTR languages, it's <code>→</code>. Neither the translator nor the compiler can guess this — it's a per-locale decision encoded in the JSON.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="icu">
      <h2><span class="num">13</span> ICU Plurals — One Key, Five Behaviors</h2>
      <p>next-intl uses ICU MessageFormat — the industry-standard plural syntax supported by Android, ICU4J, and every major i18n system.</p>

      <h3>The same key in all 5 files</h3>
      <pre><code>// ar.json — Arabic has 6 plural forms
"valueGuestsCount": "{count, plural, =1 {# شخص} =2 {# شخصان} other {# أشخاص}}"

// en.json — English has 2
"valueGuestsCount": "{count, plural, one {# guest} other {# guests}}"

// fr.json — French has 3
"valueGuestsCount": "{count, plural, one {# personne} other {# personnes}}"

// de.json — German has 2
"valueGuestsCount": "{count, plural, one {# Gast} other {# Gäste}}"

// es.json — Spanish has 2
"valueGuestsCount": "{count, plural, one {# comensal} other {# comensales}}"</code></pre>

      <h3>Rendered output for <code>count=2</code></h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Locale</th><th>Rendered</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>ar</td><td>شخصان <em>(dual form — Arabic-specific)</em></td></tr>
          <tr><td>en</td><td>2 guests</td></tr>
          <tr><td>fr</td><td>2 personnes</td></tr>
          <tr><td>de</td><td>2 Gäste</td></tr>
          <tr><td>es</td><td>2 comensales</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Why this matters</strong>
        Arabic distinguishes singular, dual, and plural. A naive <code>{count} أشخاص</code> would render "2 أشخاص" — technically wrong. ICU handles this properly and for free.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="nameen">
      <h2><span class="num">14</span> Category nameEn Migration</h2>
      <p><strong>The problem:</strong> Categories are stored as Arabic strings in the database (<code>"مقبلات"</code>, <code>"أطباق رئيسية"</code>). When an English user visits <code>/en/menu</code>, they see Arabic categories.</p>

      <h3>Migration — <code>add_category_name_en</code></h3>
      <pre><code>ALTER TABLE "categories" ADD COLUMN "nameEn" TEXT;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "categories_nameEn_key" ON "categories"("nameEn");</code></pre>

      <h3>Schema update</h3>
      <pre><code>model Category {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  name         String   @unique
  nameEn       String?  @unique   // ← NEW: optional English
  slug         String   @unique
  ...
}</code></pre>

      <h3>Backfill script — idempotent</h3>
      <pre><code>const UPDATES = [
  { slug: "appetizers",   nameEn: "Appetizers" },
  { slug: "main-courses", nameEn: "Main Courses" },
  { slug: "desserts",     nameEn: "Desserts" },
  { slug: "beverages",    nameEn: "Beverages" },
];

for (const update of UPDATES) {
  await prisma.category.update({
    where: { slug: update.slug },
    data: { nameEn: update.nameEn },
  });
}</code></pre>

      <h3>The helper — <code>getLocalizedName()</code></h3>
      <pre><code>export function getLocalizedName(
  name: string,
  nameEn: string | null | undefined,
  locale: string
): string {
  if (locale === "ar") return name;
  return nameEn ?? name;
}</code></pre>
      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Why not translate the whole DB?</strong>
        Categories are content, not UI. Translating them requires either 5 columns (<code>nameAr</code>, <code>nameEn</code>, <code>nameFr</code>...) or a separate translations table. Neither is justified for 4 categories. The pragmatic choice: store Arabic + English, fall back gracefully for the other 3.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="dir">
      <h2><span class="num">15</span> Dynamic <code>dir</code> and <code>lang</code></h2>
      <pre><code>// src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx
export default async function LocaleLayout({ children, params }) {
  const { locale } = await params;
  setRequestLocale(locale);

  const messages = await getMessages();
  const dir = locale === "ar" ? "rtl" : "ltr";

  return (
    &lt;html lang={locale} dir={dir}&gt;
      &lt;body&gt;
        &lt;NextIntlClientProvider messages={messages} locale={locale}&gt;
          {children}
        &lt;/NextIntlClientProvider&gt;
      &lt;/body&gt;
    &lt;/html&gt;
  );
}</code></pre>

      <h3>Why <code>&lt;html&gt;</code>, not <code>&lt;body&gt;</code></h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Attribute on</th><th>Mirrors text?</th><th>Mirrors Flexbox?</th><th>Mirrors scrollbar?</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>&lt;body dir="rtl"&gt;</code></td><td>✅</td><td>⚠️ Partial</td><td>❌</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>&lt;html dir="rtl"&gt;</code></td><td>✅</td><td>✅</td><td>✅</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Bottom line:</strong> Setting <code>dir</code> on the root <code>&lt;html&gt;</code> element is the only way to make the browser scrollbar, focus rings, and native form controls (dropdowns, date pickers) respect the direction.</p>

      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Deprecation notice</strong>
        <code>setRequestLocale</code> is now deprecated in next-intl v4. The recommended replacement is <code>next/root-params</code>. Documented as a Phase 12 cleanup item.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="switcher">
      <h2><span class="num">16</span> LanguageSwitcher — The Component</h2>
      <p>A dropdown that swaps the locale segment while preserving the current path.</p>

      <h3>Visual mock</h3>
      <div class="lang-switch-mock">
        <div class="lsm-btn">
          <span class="flag">🇬🇧</span>
          <span>English</span>
          <span class="arrow">▼</span>
        </div>
        <div class="lsm-list">
          <div class="item"><span class="flag">🇪🇬</span> العربية</div>
          <div class="item active"><span class="flag">🇬🇧</span> English</div>
          <div class="item"><span class="flag">🇫🇷</span> Français</div>
          <div class="item"><span class="flag">🇩🇪</span> Deutsch</div>
          <div class="item"><span class="flag">🇪🇸</span> Español</div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <h3>Core logic</h3>
      <pre><code>const LOCALES_DATA = {
  ar: { label: "العربية",  code: "eg" },
  en: { label: "English",  code: "gb" },
  fr: { label: "Français", code: "fr" },
  de: { label: "Deutsch",  code: "de" },
  es: { label: "Español",  code: "es" },
};

function handleChange(newLocale: string) {
  setIsOpen(false);
  router.replace(pathname, { locale: newLocale });
}</code></pre>

      <h3>Why <code>router.replace(pathname, { locale })</code></h3>
      <ul>
        <li><strong><code>pathname</code></strong> — from <code>@/i18n/navigation</code> — has the current locale <strong>stripped</strong>. So on <code>/en/menu/hummus</code>, <code>pathname</code> is <code>/menu/hummus</code>.</li>
        <li><strong><code>router.replace</code></strong> — replaces history entry instead of pushing, so the back button doesn't cycle through every language tested.</li>
        <li><strong>The result</strong> — switching to French from <code>/en/menu/hummus</code> lands on <code>/fr/menu/hummus</code>, not <code>/fr/</code>.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>Flags from flagcdn.com</h3>
      <pre><code>&lt;Image
  src={`https://flagcdn.com/24x18/${currentLocale.code}.png`}
  alt={locale}
  width={20}
  height={15}
/&gt;</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Why flagcdn:</strong> Zero-bundle SVG flags via CDN, no npm package, one <code>remotePatterns</code> entry in <code>next.config.ts</code>.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="factories">
      <h2><span class="num">17</span> Schema Factories — Translations in Zod</h2>
      <p><strong>The problem:</strong> Zod schemas validate on the server. Their error messages need to match the current locale — but the schema itself has no idea which locale is active.</p>

      <h3>Before (Phase 5) — hardcoded Arabic</h3>
      <pre><code>export const reservationSchema = z.object({
  guestName: z.string().min(2, "الاسم قصير جداً"),
  guestsCount: z.coerce.number().max(10, "لا يمكن الحجز لأكثر من 10 أشخاص"),
  ...
});</code></pre>

      <h3>After (Phase 11) — factory receives a translator</h3>
      <pre><code>type TranslateFn = (key: string) => string;

export function createReservationSchema(t: TranslateFn) {
  return z.object({
    guestName: z.string().min(2, t("guestNameTooShort")),
    guestsCount: z.coerce.number().max(10, t("guestsCountMax")),
    ...
  });
}</code></pre>

      <h3>Usage inside a Server Action</h3>
      <pre><code>const tValidation = await getTranslations("Errors.validation");
const schema = createReservationSchema((key) =>
  tValidation(key as Parameters&lt;typeof tValidation&gt;[0])
);
const parsed = schema.safeParse(input);</code></pre>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>The translator is the factory</strong>
        Instead of duplicating 5 schemas (one per locale), the schema stays a single function. The factory pattern keeps the codebase small and the locale data external — exactly where it belongs.
      </div>

      <h3>All 6 schemas converted</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>File</th><th>Before</th><th>After</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>validations/reservation.ts</code></td><td>const schema</td><td>createReservationSchema(t)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>validations/review.ts</code></td><td>const schema</td><td>createReviewSchema(t)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>validations/menu-item.ts</code></td><td>const schema</td><td>createMenuItemSchema(t)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>validations/category.ts</code></td><td>const schema</td><td>createCategorySchema(t)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>validations/table.ts</code></td><td>const schema</td><td>createTableSchema(t)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>validations/user.ts</code></td><td>const schema</td><td>createUserSchema(t) + updateUserSchema(t)</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="actions">
      <h2><span class="num">18</span> Server Actions i18n — The tError() Helper</h2>
      <p>Server Actions return user-facing errors (<code>"البريد مستخدم بالفعل"</code>). Every one of those strings now comes from translations.</p>

      <h3>The helper — <code>src/lib/utils/server-errors.ts</code></h3>
      <pre><code>export type ErrorKey =
  | "unauthorized" | "adminRequired" | "notFound" | "invalidData"
  | "duplicateSlug" | "duplicateEmail" | "duplicateNumber" | "duplicateName"
  | "hasItems" | "hasReservations" | "noTableAvailable"
  | "selfRoleChange" | "selfDisable" | "lastAdmin" | "selfDelete"
  | "unexpected" | "reviewLimit" | /* ... + 40 more */;

export async function tError(
  key: ErrorKey,
  values?: Record&lt;string, string | number&gt;
): Promise&lt;string&gt; {
  const t = await getTranslations("Errors");
  return t(key, values);
}</code></pre>

      <h3>Usage in every Server Action</h3>
      <pre><code>// Before
return { success: false, error: "غير مصرح" };

// After
return { success: false, error: await tError("unauthorized") };

// With interpolation
return {
  success: false,
  error: await tError("hasItems", { count: itemsCount }),
};</code></pre>

      <h3>Files updated</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><code>actions/reservation.ts</code></li>
        <li><code>actions/reviews.ts</code></li>
        <li><code>actions/admin-menu.ts</code></li>
        <li><code>actions/admin-categories.ts</code></li>
        <li><code>actions/admin-tables.ts</code></li>
        <li><code>actions/admin-users.ts</code></li>
      </ul>

      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Type-safe error keys</strong>
        The <code>ErrorKey</code> union lists every valid key. Calling <code>tError("typo")</code> is a compile error — not a runtime silent failure. Adding a new key requires updating the union + the 5 message files.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="notfound">
      <h2><span class="num">19</span> The not-found Client Pattern</h2>
      <p><strong>The problem:</strong> Custom <code>not-found.tsx</code> files need translations. But making them <code>async</code> causes a subtle HTTP status regression.</p>

      <h3>Broken — async + useTranslations</h3>
      <pre><code>// ❌ Causes 200 instead of 404
export default async function NotFound() {
  const t = await getTranslations("ItemDetail");
  return &lt;div&gt;{t("notFoundTitle")}&lt;/div&gt;;
}</code></pre>
      <p>When <code>not-found.tsx</code> is async, Next.js streams the response before the component resolves. By the time we know it's a 404, the HTTP status has already been sent as 200.</p>

      <h3>Fixed — sync wrapper + client child</h3>
      <pre><code>// ✅ not-found.tsx (stays sync)
import type { Metadata } from "next";
import { MenuItemNotFoundClient } from "./not-found-client";

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: "Not Found",
  robots: { index: false, follow: false },
};

export default function MenuItemNotFound() {
  return &lt;MenuItemNotFoundClient /&gt;;
}

// ✅ not-found-client.tsx ("use client")
"use client";
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";
import { Link } from "@/i18n/navigation";

export function MenuItemNotFoundClient() {
  const t = useTranslations("ItemDetail");
  return (
    &lt;div className="text-center py-24"&gt;
      &lt;div className="text-8xl mb-6"&gt;🍽️&lt;/div&gt;
      &lt;h1&gt;{t("notFoundTitle")}&lt;/h1&gt;
      &lt;p&gt;{t("notFoundDescription")}&lt;/p&gt;
      &lt;Link href="/menu"&gt;{t("backToMenu")}&lt;/Link&gt;
    &lt;/div&gt;
  );
}</code></pre>

      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Why this works</strong>
        The sync parent returns immediately → response headers send with the correct 404. The client child uses <code>useTranslations</code> (available through <code>NextIntlClientProvider</code> mounted in the layout). Both goals achieved.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="status-issue">
      <h2><span class="num">20</span> The 200-vs-404 Issue — Framework Limitation</h2>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Observed in production</strong>
        <code>curl -I http://localhost:3000/en/menu/zxcvbnmx</code> returns <code>HTTP/1.1 200 OK</code> — even though the browser correctly renders the custom 404 page.
      </div>

      <h3>Root cause</h3>
      <p>When <code>next-intl</code> middleware wraps a request, the response begins streaming before <code>notFound()</code> can fire in <code>generateMetadata</code> or <code>page.tsx</code>. Next.js can't retroactively change an already-committed HTTP status line.</p>

      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Environment</th><th>Behavior</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>No middleware (plain Next.js)</td><td>404 ✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td>With next-intl middleware</td><td>200 (streaming commit)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Production (Vercel)</td><td>Same — not a dev-only quirk</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>The SEO-safe workaround</h3>
      <p>Even with a 200 status, we can prevent search engines from indexing the page. Add <code>noindex</code> to the metadata:</p>
      <pre><code>export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: "Not Found",
  robots: { index: false, follow: false },
};</code></pre>

      <div class="callout info">
        <strong>Result</strong>
        <table style="margin-top:0.5rem">
          <tr><td>👤 User</td><td>Sees the custom 404 page ✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td>🤖 Googlebot</td><td>Reads <code>noindex, nofollow</code> → skips indexing ✅</td></tr>
          <tr><td>📊 HTTP status</td><td>200 — cosmetic, non-blocking ⚠️</td></tr>
        </table>
      </div>
      <p><strong>This is a known next-intl + Next.js 16 limitation</strong>, tracked upstream. Documented as a Phase 12 cleanup item to revisit when a fix lands.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="sitemap">
      <h2><span class="num">21</span> Sitemap Per-Locale — 75 URLs</h2>
      <p>The Phase 10 sitemap returned 15 URLs. After Phase 11, every URL is emitted once <strong>per locale</strong>.</p>

      <h3>Before</h3>
      <pre><code>https://lumiere-nextjs-fullstack.vercel.app/menu
https://lumiere-nextjs-fullstack.vercel.app/menu/hummus
...</code></pre>

      <h3>After — the flatMap pattern</h3>
      <pre><code>const staticPages = routing.locales.flatMap((locale) =>
  staticPaths.map((path) => ({
    url: `${SITE_URL}/${locale}${path}`,
    lastModified: new Date(),
    ...
  }))
);

const itemPages = routing.locales.flatMap((locale) =>
  items.map((item) => ({
    url: `${SITE_URL}/${locale}/menu/${item.slug}`,
    lastModified: item.updatedAt,
    ...
  }))
);</code></pre>

      <h3>Verified output</h3>
      <div class="callout success">
        <table style="margin-top:0.5rem">
          <tr><td><code>/sitemap.xml</code></td><td>200 · <strong>75 URLs</strong></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Static pages × 5 locales</td><td>15</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Menu items × 5 locales</td><td>60</td></tr>
        </table>
      </div>

      <h3>Bonus: automatic hreflang</h3>
      <p>Next.js auto-injects <code>&lt;link rel="alternate" hreflang="..."&gt;</code> tags because we prefix every URL with the locale. Google uses these to serve the right language to each user — no manual work required.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="robots">
      <h2><span class="num">22</span> Robots Per-Locale — 10 Admin Rules</h2>
      <p>The admin panel is protected at <code>/ar/admin</code>, <code>/en/admin</code>, ... <code>/es/admin</code>. Each must be individually disallowed.</p>

      <h3>Generated robots.txt</h3>
      <pre><code>User-Agent: *
Allow: /
Disallow: /ar/admin
Disallow: /ar/admin/
Disallow: /en/admin
Disallow: /en/admin/
Disallow: /fr/admin
Disallow: /fr/admin/
Disallow: /de/admin
Disallow: /de/admin/
Disallow: /es/admin
Disallow: /es/admin/
Disallow: /api/

Sitemap: https://lumiere-nextjs-fullstack.vercel.app/sitemap.xml</code></pre>

      <h3>The code</h3>
      <pre><code>const localePrefixes = routing.locales.map((locale) => `/${locale}`);
const disallow = localePrefixes.flatMap((prefix) => [
  `${prefix}/admin`,
  `${prefix}/admin/`,
]);
disallow.push("/api/");</code></pre>

      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Why the trailing slash rule</strong>
        <code>/ar/admin</code> disallows the exact path. <code>/ar/admin/</code> disallows all subpaths. Both are needed — some bots treat them differently.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="errors">

    <section id="pitfalls">
      <h2><span class="num">26</span> Common Pitfalls &amp; Fixes</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Symptom</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Using <code>next/link</code> in locale-prefixed pages</td><td>Broken links, redirect loops</td><td>Import <code>Link</code> from <code>@/i18n/navigation</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Calling <code>usePathname</code> from <code>next/navigation</code></td><td>Locale prefix included in pathname</td><td>Import from <code>@/i18n/navigation</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Making <code>not-found.tsx</code> async</td><td>200 instead of 404</td><td>Sync wrapper + Client child</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Missing key in one locale</td><td><code>MISSING_MESSAGE</code> runtime error</td><td>Add to all 5 files; use the coverage matrix</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Prisma imported into Edge</td><td><code>node:path</code> load error</td><td>Split config into Edge + Node files</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>useTranslations</code> in Server Component</td><td>"not supported in Server Components"</td><td>Use <code>getTranslations</code> (async) instead</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>getTranslations</code> in <code>tsx</code> script</td><td>"not supported in Client Components"</td><td>Use <code>createTranslator</code> from <code>next-intl</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Adding locale to <code>/api/</code></td><td>Webhooks break</td><td>Keep API routes outside <code>[locale]</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Hardcoded English in Client Component</td><td>Shows English on /de</td><td>Every visible string must be <code>t("...")</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Wrong flag code</td><td>Broken image next to language</td><td>Use ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes (<code>eg</code>, <code>gb</code>, <code>fr</code>...)</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="glossary">
      <h2><span class="num">27</span> Technical Abbreviations Glossary</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Abbr.</th><th>Full Form</th><th>Plain-English Meaning</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>i18n</td><td>Internationalization</td><td>Designing software to support multiple languages</td></tr>
          <tr><td>l10n</td><td>Localization</td><td>Actually translating for a specific locale</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Locale</td><td>—</td><td>A language + region combo, e.g., <code>ar-EG</code> or <code>en-GB</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>RTL</td><td>Right-to-Left</td><td>Text direction for Arabic, Hebrew, Farsi, Urdu</td></tr>
          <tr><td>LTR</td><td>Left-to-Right</td><td>Text direction for Latin, Cyrillic, Greek scripts</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ICU</td><td>International Components for Unicode</td><td>Standard for plurals, dates, numbers in messages</td></tr>
          <tr><td>BCP-47</td><td>Best Current Practice 47</td><td>Standard tag format for locales, e.g., <code>ar-EG</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>hreflang</td><td>(HTML attribute)</td><td>Tells search engines a page has alternates in other languages</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Edge Runtime</td><td>—</td><td>V8-isolated environment without Node APIs (Vercel, Cloudflare)</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RSC</td><td>React Server Components</td><td>React components that render only on the server</td></tr>
          <tr><td>SEO</td><td>Search Engine Optimization</td><td>Practices to rank in search results</td></tr>
          <tr><td>SERP</td><td>Search Engine Results Page</td><td>The page listing Google results</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ICU MF</td><td>ICU MessageFormat</td><td>The <code>{count, plural, ...}</code> syntax</td></tr>
          <tr><td>SSR</td><td>Server-Side Rendering</td><td>Rendering HTML on the server before sending to the browser</td></tr>
          <tr><td>SPA</td><td>Single Page Application</td><td>Client-rendered app with a single HTML shell</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

<file path="src/components/admin/AdminSidebar.tsx">
"use client";

import { usePathname } from "@/i18n/navigation";
import { useTransition } from "react";
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";
import { signOut } from "next-auth/react";
import { Link } from "@/i18n/navigation";
import { LanguageSwitcher } from "@/components/layout/LanguageSwitcher";

type UserInfo = {
  name: string;
  role: string;
};

const commonLinks = [
  { href: "/admin", labelKey: "overview", icon: "📊", exact: true },
  { href: "/admin/reservations", labelKey: "reservations", icon: "📅" },
  { href: "/admin/menu", labelKey: "menu", icon: "🍽️" },
  { href: "/admin/categories", labelKey: "categories", icon: "📂" },
  { href: "/admin/tables", labelKey: "tables", icon: "🪑" },
  { href: "/admin/reviews", labelKey: "reviews", icon: "⭐" },
  { href: "/admin/audit-log", labelKey: "auditLog", icon: "📋" },
] as const;

const adminOnlyLinks = [
  { href: "/admin/users",    labelKey: "users",    icon: "👥" },
  { href: "/admin/settings", labelKey: "settings", icon: "⚙️" },
] as const;

type Props = {
  user: UserInfo;
  onClose?: () => void;
};

export function AdminSidebar({ user, onClose }: Props) {
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();
  const t = useTranslations("Admin.sidebar");
  const isAdmin = user.role === "ADMIN";

  function isActive(href: string, exact?: boolean) {
    if (exact) return pathname === href;
    return pathname === href || pathname.startsWith(href + "/");
  }

  function handleLogout() {
    if (!confirm(t("logoutConfirm"))) return;
    startTransition(async () => {
      await signOut({ callbackUrl: "/login" });
    });
  }

  return (
    <aside className="w-64 h-full bg-foreground text-background shrink-0 overflow-y-auto">
      {/* حاوية داخلية بحد أدنى = ارتفاع الشاشة */}
      <div className="flex flex-col min-h-full">
        {/* الشعار + زر إغلاق (للجوال فقط) */}
        <div className="p-4 lg:p-6 border-b border-white/10 flex items-center justify-between shrink-0">
          <div>
            <Link
              href="/admin"
              onClick={onClose}
              className="text-2xl font-bold text-accent"
            >
              Lumière
            </Link>
            <p className="text-xs text-white/50 mt-1">{t("brand")}</p>
          </div>

          {/* زر إغلاق الجوال */}
          {onClose && (
            <button
              type="button"
              onClick={onClose}
              aria-label={t("closeMenu")}
              className="lg:hidden p-2 hover:bg-white/10 rounded-lg transition-colors text-white/70"
            >
              <svg
                width="20"
                height="20"
                viewBox="0 0 24 24"
                fill="none"
                stroke="currentColor"
                strokeWidth="2"
                strokeLinecap="round"
              >
                <line x1="18" y1="6" x2="6" y2="18" />
                <line x1="6" y1="6" x2="18" y2="18" />
              </svg>
            </button>
          )}
        </div>

        {/* الروابط — بلا flex-1 (ارتفاع طبيعي) */}
        <nav className="p-3 flex flex-col gap-1 shrink-0">
          {commonLinks.map((link) => (
            <SidebarLink
              key={link.href}
              href={link.href}
              label={t(link.labelKey)}
              icon={link.icon}
              active={isActive(link.href, "exact" in link && link.exact)}
              onClick={onClose}
            />
          ))}

          {isAdmin && (
            <>
              <div className="border-t border-white/10 my-2" />
              {adminOnlyLinks.map((link) => (
                <SidebarLink
                  key={link.href}
                  href={link.href}
                  label={t(link.labelKey)}
                  icon={link.icon}
                  active={isActive(link.href)}
                  onClick={onClose}
                />
              ))}
            </>
          )}
        </nav>

        {/* المستخدم + الخروج — mt-auto يدفعها للأسفل عند توفر مساحة */}
        <div className="p-3 border-t border-white/10 space-y-1 mt-auto shrink-0">
          <div className="px-4 py-3 bg-white/5 rounded-lg">
            <div className="text-sm font-medium truncate">{user.name}</div>
            <div className="text-xs text-white/50 mt-0.5">
              {user.role === "ADMIN" ? t("roleAdmin") : t("roleStaff")}
            </div>
          </div>

          <LanguageSwitcher variant="dark" />

          <Link
            href="/"
            onClick={onClose}
            className="flex items-center gap-3 px-4 py-3 rounded-lg text-sm text-white/50 hover:bg-white/10 hover:text-white transition-colors"
          >
            <span className="text-lg">🌐</span>
            <span>{t("viewSite")}</span>
          </Link>

          <button
            type="button"
            onClick={handleLogout}
            disabled={isPending}
            className="w-full flex items-center gap-3 px-4 py-3 rounded-lg text-sm text-red-300 hover:bg-red-500/20 hover:text-red-200 transition-colors disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed"
          >
            <span className="text-lg">🚪</span>
            <span>{isPending ? t("loggingOut") : t("logout")}</span>
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </aside>
  );
}

function SidebarLink({
  href,
  label,
  icon,
  active,
  onClick,
}: {
  href: string;
  label: string;
  icon: string;
  active: boolean;
  onClick?: () => void;
}) {
  return (
    <Link
      href={href}
      onClick={onClick}
      className={`flex items-center gap-3 px-4 py-3 rounded-lg text-sm transition-colors ${
        active
          ? "bg-accent text-white font-medium"
          : "text-white/75 hover:bg-white/10 hover:text-white"
      }`}
    >
      <span className="text-lg">{icon}</span>
      <span>{label}</span>
    </Link>
  );
}

import {

  Head,
  Preview,
  Body,
  Container,

  Hr,
} from "@react-email/components";
import type { ReservationEmailData } from "../types";
